nodeData.topic: Day 02 · Preparing for the Battle of the Day
nodeData.note: SB 11.13.4; Siksastaka 2; BG 9.29; BG 4.11 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Why the hour matters: time is one of the causes that shift the modes of nature, and both scripture and Ayurveda point to the last part of the night. The holy name is fully potent at every hour; what varies is our receptivity — Krishna reciprocates with our disposition to serve, and brahma-muhurta is when that receptivity is easiest. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Brahma-muhurta is the time when Krishna's internal energy is prominent; at other times the external energy and its modes prevail. At this hour we can be in tune with the internal energy. — “So we can be very much in tune with the internal energy”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:10 (auto-transcript): “That's the time today where the energy has its time. That's the time when the internal energy is very much prominent, whereas other times it's the external energy with the moods which is prevalent. So we can be very much in tune with the internal energy of doing that. In…”

In general, activities, mantras and purificatory rites are affected because the modes of nature become prominent differently at different times.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:45 (auto-transcript): “In general, the activities, mantras, and purificatory rituals, the modes of nature become differently prominent.”
The Bhagavatam lists ten factors that bring a mode forward — among them place and time.

The gunas are ever-changing influences, not fixed types of person; time decides which one becomes prominent, and in Krishna's list of ten causes place and time stand side by side.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:19 (auto-transcript): “The Gunas are ever-changing influences, not fixed personality types. The time affects which one becomes prominent. Side by side in Krishna's list of ten causes stand. Desha that is place and Kala that is time. One should do activities at Dramamurta, not at evening and…”

children.topic: Act at brahma-muhurta, not at night
children.note:
A further reference is read: spiritual activities should be done at brahma-muhurta, not in the evening or at midnight.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:37 (auto-transcript): “One should do activities at Dramamurta, not at evening and midnight. Srimad Bhagavan 11.3.6 Everyone walks into the mid-days, the liturgy.”

children.topic: Ayurveda: the day starts with rising
children.note:
Ayurveda's daily regimen (dinacarya) begins not with diet or exercise but with when to rise — the very window scripture recommends, though for a different purpose: protecting the lifespan.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:11 (auto-transcript): “It is a daily regimen. Dinner charia begins not with a diet or exercise but with when to rise. It identifies the very same window that Shastra recommends. Though for a different purpose, Rakshatam Ayushaha, protection of longevity. Different periods of the day are dominated…”

The last watch of the night is the vata period — light, mobile and clear, the bodily counterpart of the mental clarity scripture attributes to this hour. Near sunrise kapha takes over: heaviness and inertia return. That is why the acaryas speak of a muhurta, not just 'the morning'.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:52 (auto-transcript): “The last watch of the night is the Vata period, while the period being near sunrise is governed by Kapha. The last watch of the night is the Vata period, light, mobile and clear, the physiological counterpart to the mental clarity that Shastrak attributes to this hour. Near…”

children.topic: One more hour is a different world
children.note:
Sleeping an extra hour does not only make us later; it puts us in a different environment. — “Sleeping one more hour doesn't just make it later”

🎙 Maharaj at 46:42 (auto-transcript): “Sleeping one more hour doesn't just make it later, it places us in a different environment. The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine confirmed that this time keeping is not a vague brain level habit. It is a molecular mechanism running autonomously inside almost every…”

The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine showed that the body's timekeeping is a molecular mechanism running in almost every cell, keeping a near-24-hour rhythm on its own.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:50 (auto-transcript): “The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine confirmed that this time keeping is not a vague brain level habit. It is a molecular mechanism running autonomously inside almost every cell in the body. The clock is endogenous and self-sustaining. It holds a near 24 hour rhythm…”

As the day goes on the body wears down, mental anxiety and noise increase, and these influences seep into consciousness.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:46 (auto-transcript): “The body is not working on a normal person in the environment and in the modes gradually increase.”

children.topic: Heavier as the night goes on
children.note:
At events you can notice the mood getting heavier as the evening gets later.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:12 (auto-transcript): “For this reason, when you go to different events, you might notice that the moths get heavier and heavier as the evening gets later. The morning hours are important for any type of practice, especially prayers, meditation, chanting and reading. If we engage in any of these…”

So the morning hours are important for every kind of practice — prayer, meditation, chanting, reading — and what is done then carries more potential.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:22 (auto-transcript): “The morning hours are important for any type of practice, especially prayers, meditation, chanting and reading. If we engage in any of these activities in the morning, they will have more potential. I have invested all your potencies in those names and there are no hard and…”
Mahaprabhu's second verse: the Lord has put all his potencies in his names with no strict rules of time or place, yet he laments that, because of offences, he has no attachment for chanting.

children.topic: The treasure is there, but blocked
children.note:
A reflection is read: we may chant for years and still have material desires and bad habits — the treasure is available, but something keeps us from receiving it; this misfortune is called durdaiva.

🎙 Maharaj at 72:25 (auto-transcript): “is accessible but we cannot fully experience it. Reflections 1 verse 2. We may have chanted for a period of time and think I have been chanting for so many years and still I have material desires and bad habits. What is the point of all this chanting? Our treasure is…”

The potency of the name is always there; what we must watch is our own attentiveness. — “The potency is there, but we must also observe our level of attentiveness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 79:25 (auto-transcript): “The potency is there, but we must also observe our level of attentiveness. When it says that there are no hard and fast rules, it means that there is always benefit from the chanting, but some situations are more beneficial than others. It is not that we can only chant in the…”

'No hard and fast rules' means chanting always benefits, at any time, softly or loudly, in temple or home — but certain situations facilitate quality chanting and progress more than others.

🎙 Maharaj at 79:54 (auto-transcript): “There are no hard and fast rules, but certain situations facilitate quality chanting more than others. Right. It's facilitated about chanting, facilitated about progress more than other times. We are attention to love. The name is absolute, all potency, no rules of time.…”

children.topic: Nothing in past chanting is wasted
children.note:
The name is absolute and was never weaker at any hour, so none of our past chanting is demoted. If the name never varies, what varies? That is the question to explore. — “The name acted every single time.”

🎙 Maharaj at 80:25 (auto-transcript): “The name is absolute, all potency, no rules of time. Therefore, nothing was ever wrong with the name at any hour and nothing in your past chanting is demoted. The name acted every single time. Therefore, the words won't question. If the name never varies, what varies in mind?…”

Krishna's invitation is open to everyone: he is equal to all, yet he is especially with those who serve him. The equality is real and so is the asymmetry — the changing factor is on the devotee's side.
Krishna reciprocates in proportion to our surrender.

The exchange is personal because both Krishna and the devotee are conscious — not a signal picked up by a receiver, but a person responding to the direction of our heart.

🎙 Maharaj at 84:45 (auto-transcript): “The exchange is personal, not a broadcast met by a receiver, but a person who responds to the direction of our heart. What He reciprocates is not our schedule, our stamina, or our similarity. It is our response, our receptivity to His invitation expressed in service. How do…”

What Krishna reciprocates is not our schedule, stamina or similarity to others, but our response to his invitation, expressed in service. — “It is our response, our receptivity to His invitation expressed in service.”

🎙 Maharaj at 84:58 (auto-transcript): “What He reciprocates is not our schedule, our stamina, or our similarity. It is our response, our receptivity to His invitation expressed in service. How do we respond to what is available? When you say it, you get more. When you take it, you say it.”

A Padma Purana verse explains the mechanism: the material senses cannot grasp Krishna's name, form, qualities and pastimes; he reveals himself when the senses, beginning with the tongue, are engaged in his service.

The name is not captured by our senses; he appears to one who has the right disposition.

🎙 Maharaj at 86:53 (auto-transcript): “The name cannot be grasped by the material senses. We cannot make him appear. But when those same senses are engaged in service, beginning with the top, then he reveals himself. He appears to one with the right disposition. Variable is receptivity, same one, a disposition for…”

That disposition is for service — not a mood, a talent or a prior attainment — and it is available to anyone, at any stage, starting today.

🎙 Maharaj at 87:26 (auto-transcript): “Variable is receptivity, same one, a disposition for service, not a mood, not a talent, not a prior attainment, not an actress, not an actress. A disposition available to anyone at any stage beginning today. Why did every generation of our Gaudier Acharyas treasure the hours…”

Summing up: Mahaprabhu confesses he has no taste, Krishna reciprocates, the Padma Purana gives the mechanism — Krishna is always available, the practitioner is not always receptive. So the real question is not why the hour matters to the name, but when I am most receptive. — “but the Sadhaka is not always receptive.”

🎙 Maharaj at 90:13 (auto-transcript): “So far we saw Mahaprabhu's confession that I have no taste, Krishna's reciprocation, the Padma Purana's mechanism, and this gives us Krishna is always available, but the Sadhaka is not always receptive. The old question, why does the hour matter to the Holy Name? The real…”

children.topic: What is at stake in this hour?
children.note:
The name reveals himself wherever he finds a heart inclined to serve; the variable was never where you stand, but how you approach.

🎙 Maharaj at 94:05 (auto-transcript): “The name reveals himself wherever he finds a heart inclined to serve. The variable was never where you stand. It has always been how you approach it. In writing, if you wish, answer the following question for yourself.”

Participants are asked to write, for themselves only, an answer to: what is truly at stake in this hour? Nothing will be shared or graded.

🎙 Maharaj at 94:37 (auto-transcript): “In writing, if you wish, answer the following question for yourself.”

children.topic: Greeting the deity in the morning
children.note:
The deity is the representative of transcendence in this world. Coming in the morning to greet the deity and join the kirtan brings reciprocation; we are not always aware how the creeper of devotion is being watered, because the material energy is thick — but these activities do water it.

🎙 Maharaj at 105:10 (auto-transcript): “Ramamoharita Parmaipati. This is actually the representative of transcendence”

Questions and comments from participants; Maharaj's answers are mostly not captured.

🎙 Maharaj at 108:32 (auto-transcript): “the shape the Acharya part big that is not my question is it is said that we are about three and three and a half a.m. it is Brahmamurtha but if I work up early then three like one a.m. or two a.m. then will it work as a Brahmamurtha or it will not will work as a Brahmamurtha…”

If brahma-muhurta is around 3–3:30 a.m., is chanting after rising at 1 or 2 a.m. still brahma-muhurta, or tamas? Someone told the questioner to bathe only after 3 a.m.

🎙 Question from the floor at 109:03 (auto-transcript): “and three and a half a.m. it is Brahmamurtha but if I work up early then three like one a.m. or two a.m. then will it work as a Brahmamurtha or it will not will work as a Brahmamurtha or it will work as a tamas like this it came from my experience that one day i wake up early…”

An Ayurvedic doctor in the US called the devotees' diet perfect, while one in India remarks that devotees have many health problems. Could improper meal times and missing brahma-muhurta be the reasons?

🎙 Question from the floor at 112:01 (auto-transcript): “I met with an elevated doctor. She said that whatever diet you Hare Krishnas are following, actually it's a very perfect diet from an Ayurvedic perspective. And here in India, there is an Ayurvedic doctor who treats many devotees, including many sanyases as well. So one…”

Two devotees can do the same service with different consciousness. Can we purify our motive by our own effort, or does it come by itself one day? A participant had also noted that rising early is not enough without proper consciousness.

🎙 Question from the floor at 118:25 (auto-transcript): “I have a question, like you said that there are same activities two devotees are doing, same activity, same day done, same java, same cooking, everything, but one devotee's consciousness behind that service is different, others is different. So Maharaj, can we correct our…”

nodeData.topic: Day 03 · Rising Early Tomorrow Comes by Preparing Tonight
nodeData.note: BG 14.6; BG 6.16 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma-muhurta is the hour of goodness, but goodness is only a means, not the goal; the hour helps us but cannot do our part. A good morning is decided the evening before — regulated eating, sleeping and winding down — and practised consistently rather than heroically, until the austerity becomes natural and the morning program is seen as a treasure. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Just as a place influences us — no one does peaceful japa in a brothel — time has a strong influence, because everything we do, even the demigods, is under the modes. Brahma-muhurta is the most favourable condition for prayer, chanting, hearing and meditation.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:11 (auto-transcript): “Just as a place influences us, yesterday we talked about it, they said, if you walk into a group of 100 hungry people, how do you feel? Comfortable? You can peacefully do japa there, if you enter a brothel, you do peaceful japa in the hotel, bliss the time has influence yes…”

The holy name is fully potent 24 hours a day; the limitation is never in the name. Our attentiveness and receptivity change with time and the modes. — “so the changing factor is us”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:34 (auto-transcript): “is always fully potent 24 hours they are not hard and fast rules regarding time the limitation is never in the name it is because everything about us is in the mood so the changing factor is us krishna's availability is constant but our attentiveness and receptivity according…”

It does not matter where we stand; what matters is consciousness. We can be close to someone thousands of kilometres away, and far from someone sitting beside us. — “What matters is your consciousness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 19:15 (auto-transcript): “make advancement or rise above everything. Rising is not receptivity. Distance is not disqualification. For example, you said that the cow head balls, they want to touch Krishna? Yes. But it does not matter where you stand. What matters is your consciousness. You can touch…”

children.topic: What are we seeking in this hour?
children.note:
Before going further, Maharaj asks: what are we actually looking for at brahma-muhurta?

🎙 Maharaj at 25:03 (auto-transcript): “Before we go further, we should ask one important question. What is it that we are actually seeking in this hour? Is it important? Is it important? What are we looking for in this Brahmi Mohruta?”

For one who is suffering, time passes slowly; for one enjoying, it is short. — “Therefore time is relative, according to our consciousness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:09 (auto-transcript): “or Father, according to a person who is suffering, the time is very slow. A person who is enjoying, the time is very short, very short. Therefore time is relative, according to our consciousness. Have we come all this way to become calm and do something? We have spent two…”

children.topic: Peace and clarity are not the goal
children.note:
Peace, clarity and a fresh, steady mind are valuable, but they are qualities of goodness, not the goal itself.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:17 (auto-transcript): “peace, clarity, a fresh, steady mind. Is that what we are looking for? To be peaceful. Sancti. Is that what we are looking for? These are all valuable, but they are, but are they the goal? They are the qualities of Satwa and Sri Krishna says.”

Cleanliness alone will not take us back to Godhead; outer cleanliness helps inner cleanliness so that Krishna can sit in the heart. In the same way the hour is a process, a means. — “external cleanliness should help us to have internal cleanliness”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:24 (auto-transcript): “Cleanliness. Cleanliness will take one back home back to God, eh? Cleanliness will take one back home back to God, eh? So, when we say cleanliness, what are we looking at? What are we looking at? Cleanliness. It's the greatest self for Krishna to enjoy, right? external…”
The mode of goodness is purer and illuminating, but it still conditions us through attachment to happiness and knowledge. — “goodness is still conditioning but we're using it”

children.topic: A better prison is still a prison
children.note:
Even a president or prime minister in a prison is a prisoner. We use goodness to advance, not to settle in it. — “a better prison is still a prison”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:38 (auto-transcript): “If you are a president, prime minister in a prison, what is it? You are in a prison. You are not free. whatever position we have as as a prisoner so a better prison is still a prison and this one has good light right does it make sense thank you to continue so the we've laid…”

children.topic: The hour won't do our part
children.note:
In brahma-muhurta the withdrawal of the senses (pratyahara) is largely done for us — no traffic, no phones, no voices, a lightness and clarity. But the hour asks less of us; it does not act in our place.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:54 (auto-transcript): “this part is what the yoga tradition calls Which means what? Kithara means rejecting or fermenting. The retraction of the senses from the object. We will draw the senses from the object and bring it in. We bring the senses inside, not leaving it outside. In the Brahma…”

children.topic: No one can eat for you
children.note:
Maharaj jokes: 'Don't go for prasadam, I'll eat for you; don't bathe, I'll bathe for you.' We must eat, bathe, read, chant and hear attentively ourselves. Distance has no effect, but receptivity does. — “we have to eat ourselves”

🎙 Maharaj at 45:43 (auto-transcript): “you are part for you. The hour does not. My friend don't worry, just sit down. Just ask, can someone eat for you? Don't worry, don't today, don't go for Prasad, I will eat for you. Just do other things you want to do, I will eat for you. Oh Prabhu, you just woke up this month…”

Some devotees dip their beads in Radha-kunda; that is good, but Radha-kunda will not chant for us tomorrow. Brahma-muhurta does not meditate for us — it facilitates our japa, concentration and receptivity.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:00 (auto-transcript): “So they, if you see devotees, some devotees, when they go to Raja Kun, what do they do? They put their beads in there, so Raja Kun, tomorrow morning you. You don't need to chant, you see. Raja Kun is going to chant for you. Every time you beat, you are that kind of water.…”

children.topic: Why not a festival every day?
children.note:
On festival days the deity's potency seems more prominent, and the same worship feels different. Why don't we live every day like that? Because we are lazy, not receptive, taking things for granted.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:03 (auto-transcript): “can make the same prayer yesterday we we discussed that on the we have babies we worship every day their appearance they or those personalities are different because they have the potency their personality is prominent in that deity than other days should appear in this and…”

Preparing for brahma-muhurta begins the evening before, and the consciousness is prepared along with the body.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:35 (auto-transcript): “Preparing for Brahma Murta begins the evening before.”

If you go to bed determined to rise at 3 o'clock, you will rise; if you go to bed thinking 'I am so tired, maybe 6 o'clock', you will not hear the alarm or will keep switching it off. Everyone knows this; the application is difficult.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:23 (auto-transcript): “So, also, the consciousness is prepared. If you want to wake your alarm clock, if you want to wake your alarm clock, what alarm clock wake you, is the consciousness. If you're going to bed thinking, I'm going to get up to 3 o'clock tomorrow, 3 o'clock. Tomorrow you get up to…”

Before an important trip we plan the night before; for a good sadhana tomorrow we must prepare from tonight in the same way.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:24 (auto-transcript): “we naturally prepare before a very important service you know true we are going to travel tomorrow right you prepare the time today you think about what what what I'm going to do tomorrow I want them to do it so that I will get to the important time you know tomorrow morning…”
The Gita's principle: one who eats, sleeps, recreates and works in a regulated way can mitigate material pains through yoga; too much and too little are both failures.

Yukta means regulated, balanced, engaged — connected with Krishna. Maharaj notes Yukta is also a name of a devotee in Krishna's pastimes, and that what Krishna has worn and offered is given to devotees for purification.

🎙 Maharaj at 62:44 (auto-transcript): “Valance, Yukta means? Regulate, needful. Yukta. Engaged, yes. It's engaged. It's engaged. 266. 266. Christian said one will not engage in him. One is not connected. Engaged for So, for us to be happy, we need to be connected with Krishna, and we make sure one devotee”

Those who think religion is the destination fight with others; religion is the vehicle that takes us to the destination. Brahma-muhurta likewise is there to facilitate our Krishna consciousness. — “religion is the vehicle”

🎙 Maharaj at 66:37 (auto-transcript): “many people think religion is what many people think that religion is what the end religion is the end they will fight those who think religion is the end they will fight with others why their knowledge is not complete religion is the vehicle the legion is a very good vehicle…”

From the Caraka-samhita: proper diet, proper sleep and regulated conduct support strength and long life. In the same way, using brahma-muhurta for japa and prayer keeps us progressive — so let us remain steady in practice.

🎙 Maharaj at 67:42 (auto-transcript): “Ayurveda guards the compound word in the previous verse of Kitas 17. Yipta Svartana of Vodashya, Degraded Steak and Wetfulness. Preya Upanishad Upasthampam Viti, Brahmacharya Viti. The three supporting pillars of the life, at least Upasthampam are a proper diet, ahara, proper…”

Rising early, showering and coming to class is an austerity; when we fall away from routine, it becomes even harder.

🎙 Maharaj at 72:47 (auto-transcript): “It is an austerity to wake up, only take a shower, charge up, and come to class. However, when we fall away from the routine, the program will become even harder to follow.”

A Bengali proverb Srila Prabhupada quoted: whatever you accustom the body to, it adjusts to. After six months of practice, it becomes natural.

🎙 Maharaj at 73:42 (auto-transcript): “you probably one lecture proper said there is a bengali proverbs the bengali proverb says that this body this body whatever you fit you fit into the body the body will become adjusted to it For example, if you practice God lifting after six months, this will be this. And…”

For the six Gosvamis and Haridasa Thakura, rising early and chanting was simply normal life. For us it is austerity because we are undoing habits from time immemorial.

🎙 Maharaj at 74:48 (auto-transcript): “This is from Reflections 1, verse 1 from 6 Satsaka. It is an austerity to work up early. For practitioners, for other practitioners, work up early is an austerity, but it is not austerity for the six Goswami's. It is not austerity for Harida Sakura. It is not. Right? This is…”

We credit ourselves for every success and blame others for every failure. When we take a vow — 64 rounds a day — the first days go well, then it becomes hard; to continue we need proper understanding and faith. — “We blame everybody for everything minus ourselves.”

🎙 Maharaj at 77:29 (auto-transcript): “We blame everybody for everything minus ourselves. And we blame everything good for ourselves. Everything good. I did it. I am the one. This is what you do. This kind of yesterday. So, when we fall away from the routine, the program becomes even harder to follow. We have this…”

Small steps practised consistently lead to real enthusiasm, which is a mystic power; artificial enthusiasm — 64 rounds and then collapse — does not last. For a devotee no day is dry. — “Every day is an adventure.”

🎙 Maharaj at 83:30 (auto-transcript): “so is one that feels dry as devotees should not feel should not feel dry every day should be be an adventure for a devotee. Every day is an adventure. Every day. What is there? What is there today? That's what a devotee is saying. What is there today? It's an adventure, not a…”

children.topic: The battle of the first minute
children.note:
A Swami's account is read: the body says 'you are sick', the mind agrees and amplifies, the intelligence says 'sickness comes and goes — what is the big deal?' The same three voices will speak tomorrow in the first minute; the intelligence decides.

🎙 Maharaj at 84:30 (auto-transcript): “Three voices in the dark, Shnankitya to Swami Maharaj described it in his own mourning. The body said, Swami, you are sick. Second, the mind agreed, yes, therefore you should be sad and angry. The intelligence answered, sickness will always come and go. What is the big deal?…”
As Krishna rose immediately at brahma-muhurta, rising is not the outcome of a debate at 3 a.m.; it expresses a decision made the evening before. No planning, no execution.

Entering a war unprepared, you are the first to fall. When body, mind and senses complain tomorrow, the plan must already be decided.

🎙 Maharaj at 91:15 (auto-transcript): “Just like if you enter the war, not Malaysia, nothing. What would you do then? You would be the first person to be killed at the end. So we should keep these same things with us. Tomorrow morning, when the body complains, what we have discussed the previous one, right? What…”

Sitting with devotees who are talking rather than chanting means you will talk too — that is an unplanned morning and a waste of time. Plan when and where you will chant; if sleepy, stand up.

🎙 Maharaj at 93:00 (auto-transcript): “Some devotees, when people are sitting in discussion, they come and sit in the middle day, and people are discussing, what are you doing with them? They are not doing Jaffa, you have been in japa and you are sitting with people and discussing. What would they do there? They…”

The pre-dawn hour is not empty: many of Rupa Gosvami's 64 limbs of bhakti are already on display in the morning program; we must find our place in it.

🎙 Maharaj at 98:21 (auto-transcript): “The room is not, the hour is not empty. Everything is already there, 64 principles of Baptism is already in full display. We have to find our corner in the room. We have to find it as we will go and it first though where is what you see to the special master you see they…”

Association of devotees, chanting, hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam, residing in a holy place and serving the deity; even a little of these awakens love for Krishna. Sadhu-sanga is best, as the other four are included in it.

Following the four regulative principles and attending the morning program steadily, while avoiding offences, deposits spiritual credit. Non-devotees never tire of getting money; we should never tire of increasing the quality of our practice.

🎙 Maharaj at 104:25 (auto-transcript): “You are spiritual billionaires. The system of spiritual credit and debit is similar to depositing and withdrawing from the bank. Just observing the four regulations and participating in the morning program means that we automatically become spiritual billionaires. If we are…”

Questions and comments at the end of the class.

🎙 Maharaj at 109:33 (auto-transcript): “Comments? Questions? Any comments? Yes, Prabhupada. When we are discussing the j-boards, we can easily see a person in a mode of passion and a mode of ignorance. Consciousness is different between a person in a mode of goodness and those who are above the mode of goodness,…”

children.topic: Q1 · How does pure goodness differ?
children.note:
We can recognise passion and ignorance; how is a person above goodness different from one in goodness?

🎙 Question from the floor at 109:44 (auto-transcript): “When we are discussing the j-boards, we can easily see a person in a mode of passion and a mode of ignorance. Consciousness is different between a person in a mode of goodness and those who are above the mode of goodness, they are good. So what is the difference? Can we…”

children.topic: Pleasure of the intellect vs bliss
children.note:
Poets, philosophers and musicians give pleasure to the intellect — still goodness, still a kind of enjoyment. Beyond the modes, in pure goodness, one is free; that constant happiness, unchanged by anything material, is bliss.

🎙 Maharaj at 110:23 (auto-transcript): “The poet, philosophers, musicians, writing, give pleasure to the intellect, that is the entertainment. That is why you see Guyanas speculate, they enjoy it, they enjoy it, it's a pleasure for”

When service regularly runs late into the evening, should we adjust the service or fix something else?

🎙 Question from the floor at 114:47 (auto-transcript): “Mahalaj, sometimes when we are serving, the sliver demands that sometimes he is evening also. And it happens like, then it disturbs our routine. So, at that time, the body really acts less, because this is my, personally telling you, it's never been my body situation. So, at…”

If it is constant, it is a management fault: add people so the service is shared and finishes on time. An occasional emergency is different. Chanting is the qualification for serving Krishna — we can hire a cook but never someone to chant for us. — “The qualification for us to do service for Krishna is that we have chanted.”

🎙 Maharaj at 115:24 (auto-transcript): “If the service is continuously the same thing that you want to sleep late for life, then you have to make adjustments. We increase the number of people to do their service. It is management and management fault. We should not do service and service and service and service and…”

children.topic: Q3 · Rise after a late night?
children.note:
If we travelled late and slept less than six hours, should we still rise at brahma-muhurta?

🎙 Question from the floor at 118:50 (auto-transcript): “We are late in the night. We are travelling somewhere. So, mind says we have not slept in 6 hours. So should we get up during Brahma Murad and take a rest later? Is it advisable or should we sleep five hours and then? Better wake up and chant and do his sadhana. He should get…”

Better to wake up, chant and do the sadhana, and rest afterwards.

🎙 Maharaj at 119:18 (auto-transcript): “Better wake up and chant and do his sadhana. He should get up and do his chamba and he can rest after. My question is about what Brahma during this time? easy thinking to us or is it a way of relation function of our action will you modify your destiny or is he servant or…”

maps.title: Rise Before Sunrise · Day 04 · What Steals Away Our Brahma-muhurta From Us?

nodeData.topic: Day 04 · What Steals Away Our Brahma-muhurta From Us?
nodeData.note: CC Antya 20.16 (Siksastaka 2); BG 2.40 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Why don't we receive the treasure of the holy name at brahma-muhurta? Using Mahaprabhu's second Siksastaka verse and Bhaktivinoda Thakura's four anarthas — confusion about truth, thirst for the temporary, offences and weakness of heart — Maharaj diagnoses what steals our mornings, offers the acaryas' remedy, and names the modern thief: late-night screens and unspiritual association. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: Opening skit: two kinds of association
children.note:
The class opens with a skit Maharaj asks everyone to watch carefully: one devotee poses with the Bhagavad-gita for a selfie, eyes closed as if in samadhi, hunts for a caption, then drifts into talk about prices, traffic and other people's faults. In the second scene devotees share what they have learnt about Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:58 (auto-transcript): “You take one selfie. You post it. What do you believe? You promised me that you will be reading more than the caption after this. Let's see. Let's post it. Let's see what you do. Oh, Bhagavad Gita. Yes, open Bhagavad Gita. Everybody will think that great devotees. Oh, my eyes…”

In the second scene a devotee shares that Mukunda means the giver of liberation, and also the one whose smiling face is like the kunda, a jasmine flower — one meaning for the philosopher, one that melts the heart.

children.topic: The name is constant; we change
children.note:
The holy name never changes, but we do: in goodness we chant many rounds, the next day hardly one; happy one morning, miserable the next. — “Krishna's mercy is constant. Our receptivity rises and falls.”

children.topic: Why the Gosvamis gave up everything
children.note:
Knowing that we are eternally Krishna's servants is what let the six Gosvamis leave very high positions to live in Vrindavan; renunciation is easy for a poor man, not for a minister.

Desires for material objects, heaven, mystic power and impersonal liberation. It is subtle and lies deep in the heart. Every time the temporary becomes more attractive than Krishna's invitation at dawn, we are seeing asat-trsna.

Ten offences to the name, offences in the holy dhama (even playing with one's feet in the Ganga on parikrama), offences in seva, against other living entities and against Vaishnavas — envy, not offering respect, anger. Maharaj contrasts Jatila, who serves Krishna's pleasure, with the fault-finder Ramacandra Puri, and plays on the word: apa-radha, 'no Radha' — no Radha, no Krishna. Offences do not lessen Krishna's mercy; they lessen our capacity to receive it.

Weakness of heart binds us to the world: attachment to things unrelated to Krishna, hypocrisy, envy and the desire for prestige; an inability to let go of attachments, insecurities and ego. Why should a devotee be insecure, when Krishna has clearly declared the devotee's destination (BG 4.9)?

children.topic: Why the acaryas analyse our struggle
children.note:
Out of compassion, like parents who know a child's illness and medicine. Bhaktivinoda Thakura is happy to see someone chant — not for his own gain, but because he loves Krishna, and therefore loves us.

Devotees interfere where Krishna does not. Gadadhara Dasa boldly went to a hostile Kazi: Mahaprabhu and Nityananda have delivered everyone, only you are left — chant Krishna today. When the Kazi said 'tomorrow I'll chant Hari', Gadadhara replied that he had already said the name. Preach boldly, not offensively.

children.note: The acaryas give not just a diagnosis but medicine. Rupa Gosvami distilled it into Upadesamrta verses 2 and 3: six things that destroy bhakti and six that nourish it.

children.note:

nodeData.note: CC Antya 20.16 (Siksastaka 2); BG 2.40 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Why don't we receive the treasure of the holy name at brahma-muhurta? 🎙 Maharaj at 42:47 (auto-transcript): “and the third one is a parada offenses how many how many of them no not only three a parada not only three there are many one namaparad very good namaparad is how many ten see just one alone you got ten namaparad is ten very good damaparad because we're here and let's go for…”

Weakness of heart binds us to the world: attachment to things unrelated to Krishna, hypocrisy, envy and the desire for prestige; an inability to let go of attachments, insecurities and ego. Why should a devotee be insecure, when Krishna has clearly declared the devotee's destination (BG 4.9)?

One sign of weakness of heart is envy of others' prosperity and recognition.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:55 (auto-transcript): “Those who don't consider weakness of the heart to be of four types. Attachment to the worthless objects, i.e. objects unrelated to Krishna, hypocrisy and deceit. One day Sri Sri Sri Chita Mughaprabhu came to the Rupa Goswami, this Sri Chitaan Chaitimrit,”

When Rupa Gosvami read the introduction of his Vidagdha-madhava, Mahaprabhu praised him while watching the other devotees' faces, to see how they felt — teaching us how to behave.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:33 (auto-transcript): “One day Sri Sri Sri Chita Mughaprabhu came to the Rupa Goswami, this Sri Chitaan Chaitimrit, he came with Servobobobha Tacharya, Swarudam Hibbara Goswami, Paramunada Rai, they were Sanatang Goswami. Sanatang Goswami was saying what Arita Sakhala, Jagannath Ruri. That's when…”

That is a measure of advancement: if we feel happy when a devotee is glorified, we are advancing; if we think 'I am better', it is envy. — “If you feel happy, then we are making advancement.”

🎙 Maharaj at 58:12 (auto-transcript): “He is teaching us this. How we should behave. And that is one of the ways you can see our advancement. How do we feel when a devotee is appreciated or glorified? How do we feel? If you feel happy, then we are making advancement. feel but good day and better than this what you…”

A purport of Srila Prabhupada is read: a Vaishnava rejoices when another is empowered to spread the holy name; one envious of that is not a Vaishnava, and such envy is to be neglected. Maharaj notes Prabhupada was speaking of the envy shown toward himself.

Krishna promises there is no loss on this path and even a little advancement protects from the greatest fear. What comes to mind on hearing this? Hope — and Krishna is not a bluffer; he has what he promises. The anarthas obstruct but cannot erase our devotion; still, avoid them. — “Krishna is not a bluffer.”

children.topic: Why the acaryas analyse our struggle
children.note:
Out of compassion, like parents who know a child's illness and medicine. Bhaktivinoda Thakura is happy to see someone chant — not for his own gain, but because he loves Krishna, and therefore loves us.

🎙 Maharaj at 68:57 (auto-transcript): “thinking corner this is a thinking corner thinking let us ask a question why did the chariars analyze our struggle so carefully why did they take their time to analyze everything is it their problem or our problems why why they take interest in this a very compassion”

Devotees interfere where Krishna does not. Gadadhara Dasa boldly went to a hostile Kazi: Mahaprabhu and Nityananda have delivered everyone, only you are left — chant Krishna today. When the Kazi said 'tomorrow I'll chant Hari', Gadadhara replied that he had already said the name. Preach boldly, not offensively.

🎙 Maharaj at 73:35 (auto-transcript): “In Chichanga Bhagwat, he said, the devotee will need enough of Gadadaradas. Gadadaradas. He particularly went against the nine offences of chanting the holy. A very notorious Muslim. Very dangerous Muslim. What is your Krishna? Gadadaradas, he went to him. He went to see this…”

These struggles are common to every sincere practitioner; the right diagnosis gives the right remedy. A gardener must tell the plant he sowed from the weeds that spring up with it. Those doing wonderfully today also struggled; sincere, praying effort is answered.

🎙 Maharaj at 76:59 (auto-transcript): “For a gardener, a gardener has this experience, every gardener has this experience. That the plant you planted will not be the only thing that will come from there. So many other plants will come, right? But a gardener must be able to distinguish which seed you have planted…”

children.topic: Cultivate what nourishes, avoid what weakens
children.note: The acaryas give not just a diagnosis but medicine. Rupa Gosvami distilled it into Upadesamrta verses 2 and 3: six things that destroy bhakti and six that nourish it.

Compassion means being unable to bear others' suffering and doing whatever it takes to help. The acaryas wrote and printed books so we have the medicine today. Not to read them is ingratitude — drinking poison knowingly, like refusing the rope thrown to us in a well.

🎙 Maharaj at 82:33 (auto-transcript): “How do they do that? How do they do that? Writing and printing. How much importance and proper is it given to printing? Distribute books, distribute books, distribute books. Print books, print books, distribute, print books, distribute books. Is it for making money? No. For…”

children.topic: Greedy for service, patient for mercy
children.note:
How can one be both greedy and patient? A devotee answers: greedy for service, patient for mercy. Endeavour and attitude are friends — we serve with all our strength, present our case, and let Krishna respond when he sees fit; we do not make him our houseboy. — “Greedy for the service but patient for the mercy.”

🎙 Maharaj at 90:07 (auto-transcript): “How is that? How is that? He wants to be spiritually greedy and patient. How a greedy person can be patient? A greedy person can be patient? If you are patient, then you are not greedy. And if you are greedy, you cannot be patient. Is it not true? Is it true or not? I'm…”

Live today as if it is the last day: no procrastination, no thinking we have 80 years left — especially in Kali-yuga, where nothing is certain — and leave the results to Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 93:14 (auto-transcript): “Today is my last day. I'm not sure of tomorrow. Today is my last day. Let me put my effort to do what I'll do. Tomorrow, I don't know. That is emergency consciousness. No procrastination. You can do this tomorrow. We still have 80 years or 100 years left. So we take it…”

Which of the four anarthas most often steals tomorrow's morning, and when does it begin? The answers point to the evening: late-night entertainment and scrolling.

🎙 Maharaj at 94:10 (auto-transcript): “conscious life. Healthy, very good persons. We have discussed how many anaratas? How many? Okay. Which of the four anaratas most often stills tomorrow? Which one? Hmm? Hmm? Asad Krishna? Hirdeit Rubalia? Hirdeit Rubalia?”

A devotee wrote that he spent the time scrolling on his phone and did not chant. At a Jagannatha Puri program, most of 150 visiting devotees sat on their phones while Maharaj spoke; on parikrama, beads in one hand and phone in the other — every year he has to shout before they sit and hear. 'This is not a joke; this is serious.'

🎙 Maharaj at 97:15 (auto-transcript): “The mic. Is there a mic? Something like the late night entertainment, the scrolling. scrolling means do you know do you know how dangerous do you know how dangerous these things and how they're destroying us you know imagine two days ago what he sent a message to me how he…”

Session 3's technology: an earlier, lighter meal; the senses wound down before the body; regularity as the mechanism. A devotee adds that according to Ayurveda digestion largely stops after sunset, so late food fills but does not nourish. Without purification we can spend lifetimes unchanged.

🎙 Maharaj at 102:06 (auto-transcript): “tomorrow morning what happened so what we should do what should we do in session three we gave the technology with three healing principles first the earlier lighter meal second the senses wound down before the body third as the mechanism if you have a lighter meal what's…”

Further 'spiritual technologies' are read: sleep regulated and used for remembrance, eating only Krishna prasadam so the first thought at brahma-muhurta is Krishna, and eating mindfully.

🎙 Maharaj at 107:16 (auto-transcript): “Technology, mindful sleep. We have already established that sleep should be regulated, but spiritual life asks even a deeper question. What if sleep itself can support our cultivation of bhakti? Sleep not only provides us with an opportunity to rejuvenate our bodies but it…”

Discussing the skit: association with devotees who talk only of Krishna changes consciousness. A senior devotee has the responsibility to steer conversation away from 'garbage' — helping the other person and ourselves. — “a higher devotee has the responsibility to change the topic”

🎙 Maharaj at 111:37 (auto-transcript): “did you learn association okay next association of the devotees who i see advanced in us. What did you benefit from it? Because we only discuss about Krishna, not blame things at all. Because we saw in the script that the first person was taking selfies at all, but the second…”

Your screen is not just a device; it is association, filling consciousness with garbage that can stay for years. Set a 'screen sunset' — a fixed time when screens are put away — and let the last input of the day be Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 114:45 (auto-transcript): “Guarding the last association. Your screen is not just a device. It is association. What we see before in television, it is not just a device, it is what? Association. But who my way is the setting word? Who my way is the setting word? Garbages. Garbages. We are infiltrating…”

maps.title: Rise Before Sunrise · Day 05 · How to Make Rising Early a Lifelong Habit

nodeData.topic: Day 05 · How to Make Rising Early a Lifelong Habit
nodeData.note: BG 9.14 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The closing VIHE class gathers the week into a personal blueprint: plan the evening so that the morning simply carries out a decision already made. Maharaj teaches mindful reading, consistency in small daily acts like the Vrindavan widow's pot of water, Brahma-muhurta as a daily return to our identity as Krishna's servant, attentive hearing of the holy name, prayer and gratitude, and keeping the practice alive together with other devotees. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: Madhu Mangala ties his foot to Krishna
children.note:
Maharaj opens with a pastime: Madhu Mangala feared Krishna would rise early and leave for the forest without him, so before sleeping he tied his foot to Krishna's. When Krishna woke, Madhu Mangala woke too. He prepared his tomorrow the night before.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:33 (auto-transcript): “So that day, Madhu Pangala preparing his tomorrow morning. He lay down with Krishna and tie his foot with Krishna. Tie it together. Why? When Krishna will wake up, he will also wake up. So Madhu Pangala prepare his tomorrow know? So, and exactly because when he tied the fish…”

In everything we do in Krishna consciousness there is an example set by those who did it before us; we are simply following them. — “We have an example in everything that we do in our movement.”

🎙 Maharaj at 13:29 (auto-transcript): “So we have an example. We have an example in everything that we do in our movement. We have an example. Those who have done it first. And we are simply, we are simply following. We are simply following. So yes, we lived off yesterday. When we're talking about technologies, so…”

Mindful reading is not turning pages to pass the time. Maharaj links it with Bhurijana Prabhu's 'prayerful reading': it is meant for everyone, especially those who have no taste for reading.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:06 (auto-transcript): “Very good. Mindful reading is not going through the pages of the things we have to read. His grace, his grace, Burijan Prabhu also said, he put it in a different way. Burijan Prabhu said the same similarity, prayerful reading. Thank you. prayerful reading is not the time you…”

Give the mind a focus or it will give trouble. Reading with a chosen topic keeps it occupied. — “If the mind is not engaged, it will give us trouble.”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:26 (auto-transcript): “mind, the mind will be engaged. If you don't have any focus for the mind, the mind will give us trouble. Two things. If the mind is not engaged, it will give us trouble. So you don't want trouble for the mind? Keep the mind engaged and so many things to keep the mind engaged.…”

children.topic: The eyes read, the mind does not
children.note:
Two hours of reading leaves nothing if only the eyes were reading. Choose a quiet place with no phone, sit not too comfortably, and pick a topic, such as anger, to search out in the Gita or Bhagavatam.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:06 (auto-transcript): “you read for two hours, you close the book, what happens? Nothing. There's nothing. It means the mind doesn't read. Our eyes are there, but the mind doesn't read. Therefore, they didn't keep anything that anybody can't understand because the mind doesn't read. The mind should…”

In any reading look for the storyline, the analogy, the philosophy, and similarity: where the same point appears elsewhere in Gita or Bhagavatam.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:57 (auto-transcript): “we're looking for four things four things one origin mindful reading by for reading. We are looking for four things of the reading. The story line, story. Analogy, Robert has given the analogy. Philosophy, philosophy, and similarity. Can you get a similar thing, which I'm…”

Absorption leads to contemplation and contemplation to realization. Our scriptures are not novels; even a small book like the Nectar of Instruction shows where we are and where to go. Whatever we meditate on, we are with it: hearing of Madhu Mangala, we are there with him and Krishna. — “absorption will bring out realization no absorption no realization”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:01 (auto-transcript): “absorbed absorption will bring out realization no absorption no realization realization come deep contemplation absorption contemplation realization will come that requires mindful reading. Our scriptures are not just historical novels or some novels. Our literatures are…”

children.topic: One pot of water: the Vrindavan widow
children.note:
From a disciple's memory of Srila Prabhupada in Vrindavan: a widow walked to the Yamuna every morning, even on cold winter nights, and brought back one pot of water for the Radha-Damodara pujaris. Maharaj asks the room what it shows: consistency, determination, sincerity, knowing the goal.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:26 (auto-transcript): “how do you call that what are you looking at here in the consistency very good determination very good very good sincerity very good very good she is consistent determined why consistency Why? Why is it consistent? If you are consistent, then the taste will come from it. Okay.”

She did not do it only because a guru told her; love for the Lord kept her going without fear. Where love is there, consistency follows.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:35 (auto-transcript): “If the love is there for the mother, then you can do that. Or if it's there for the Guru, then you can do that. If it's not there, you won't do it. She must have love for the mother. That's why she is consistently doing that without fear. Yes. If we don't be consistent in any…”

Consistency brings results, results bring taste, and taste increases the desire to continue. — “Success brings more, more success.”

🎙 Maharaj at 30:30 (auto-transcript): “Yes. Success brings more, more success. Okay. Success brings more success. Enthusiasm. Enthusiasm, encouragement to continue. When you are succeeding in something, what you are doing, you are encouraged to continue. Otherwise, they will say, I've been doing this for 10 years…”

A remarkable spiritual life is not built in a day; only great personalities change overnight. The rest of us grow gradually through small acts faithfully repeated.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:53 (auto-transcript): “How many times? Gradually, gradually, gradually, many times, many times, gradually, but steady, steady. Design the current. Session 3 asked you to test a single step. Tonight's work is different. Not another habit to try but a single page that gathers everything today's…”

children.topic: Design the current: a one-page blueprint
children.note:
The week's homework is a single page: one thing to cultivate, one thing to let weaken, the hardest morning understood, and an evening that shapes tomorrow. Plan the evening so that dawn simply carries out a decision already made, as Madhu Mangala did.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:40 (auto-transcript): “so gather some things we gather some things we're going to apply very good at least you have something i have something not empty to have some something want to apply to keep it ourselves i I will maintain this and improve my Krishna consciousness. One thing I will cultivate,…”

Choose a technology from the week, such as mindful sleep, prasadam only, mindful eating, good association or mindful reading, and write down its concrete arrangement. — “If you plan well, you will succeed.”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:20 (auto-transcript): “I wish you plan, so plan it nicely. If you plan well, you will succeed. succeed if you plan well let us plan well what did they prove that i have had something where is the proof application application that i have had something must be applied no application means we didn't…”

Maharaj recalls a devotee who brought a travelling bag full of seminar certificates and kept him two hours looking at them. Gathering knowledge without applying it is of no value; application brings the result.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:32 (auto-transcript): “Gathering, I saw one time, a devotee brought a traveling bag, a traveling bag full of certificates. Yes, he opened the bag on my phone. I was thinking, what is he bringing? When he opened the bag, certificate from the seminary she has attended, for nobody want to keep her in…”

Idle talk pollutes the mind, increases lust and leaves us spiritually depleted, like a car with a flat tire. An intelligent person carefully avoids it. — “gossip flatten our spiritual tire”

🎙 Maharaj at 41:06 (auto-transcript): “loss increased and one becomes spiritually depleted you have a flat tire can you move you are driving you have a flat tire gossip flatten our spiritual tire we cannot move therefore it is dangerous for us to gossip but you know to call it calls the idle talks, idle, idle…”

Devotees share one-sentence takeaways: sleep on time, not now then never, plan to succeed, a pot of water a day. Maharaj adds that we should never look down on anyone who struggles; we were also like that, and we improved because we kept trying.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:05 (auto-transcript): “so we'll continue to describe yesterday's takeaway in one sentence what will it be very good very good mindful mindfulness sleep on time not now then never not now never better now”

children.topic: Why knowing does not become living
children.note:
Knowledge alone does not give realization or pure love of God. Maharaj points out that Lord Brahma tested Krishna not out of ignorance, and that confusion came even after the great compilation of the Vedas.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:21 (auto-transcript): “who don't exist because noise we have discussed knowledge alone will not give one knowledge and love will not give one realization krishna pure love of body because we have so many people who are very knowledgeable no brahma tested krishna is it because of ignorance”

Gopinatha Acarya rebuked Sarvabhauma for not recognising the Lord. Sarvabhauma tried to instruct young Caitanya Mahaprabhu, who humbly asked to learn; after Mahaprabhu explained, the scholar was bewildered and later saw His six-armed form.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:29 (auto-transcript): “Gopinat Acharya and Sarabhambhat Acharya. Remember? Gopinat Acharya was insulting Sarabhambhat Acharya. You are a fool. Your heart is so hard like a stone. You can't understand Krishna by logic. The Supreme God is here. We cannot realize him. It's all about, my friend, we are…”

God is not realised by reading books but by the mercy of pure devotees, who also reveal the scriptures to us. Haridasa Thakura answered Mahaprabhu without study; all the scriptures resided in his heart. — “One can realize God by the mercy of pure devotees.”

🎙 Maharaj at 55:17 (auto-transcript): “One cannot realize God by reading books. One cannot by reading books. One can realize God by the mercy of pure devotees. Yes, pure devotees can show us God. And they also revealed the scriptures for us. When Chitamu asked Haridash to speak the glory to the Holy Name, which…”

children.topic: The illiterate brahmana with the Gita
children.note:
An illiterate brahmana held the Gita, possibly upside down, and wept while devotees laughed. Only Mahaprabhu did not laugh. Asked which chapter gave such bliss, he said he simply followed his guru's order and saw Krishna as Arjuna's chariot driver.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:21 (auto-transcript): “we should not forget the Brahmana who does not know how to but the guru told him read every day. What happened to him? He was holding the guitar upside down and devotees were laughing. See? He's carrying the guitar. You want to teach all that? Yeah? No, this guy was look at…”

The Bhagavatam gives importance to hearing over reading, yet Srila Prabhupada asked us to read every day. Not reading daily, Maharaj says, offends the scriptures. — “I wish you read every day.”

🎙 Maharaj at 58:17 (auto-transcript): “Slava Padmation, Canto 1, chapter 1, text 5, for what? It is better to hear them than reading them. He doesn't say we should not read. The prophet says we should not read. He says we should read for two hours every day. But here, he is saying, it is better to, than, it gives…”

children.topic: Every Brahma-muhurta returns us to our identity
children.note:
Arjuna lacked no information; his collapse was forgetting who he was, and the Gita ends with his memory restored. Sanatana Gosvami asked who am I. We are eternally Krishna's servants; this is absolute knowledge that time, place and circumstance cannot change.

🎙 Maharaj at 62:37 (auto-transcript): “We are truly, eternally, Mitya, Krishna, that is what we are. You know the philosophy of God, it is absolute knowledge. This is absolute knowledge that we are eternally, Krishna, Saravan is absolute knowledge because it does not change time does not change it circumstance…”

Mahaprabhu says he is not a brahmana, king or sannyasi, but the servant of the servant of Krishna. We are not zero; the identity is not acquired but uncovered gradually by practice. — “We are not zero.”

🎙 Maharaj at 65:14 (auto-transcript): “So, what are we looking at here? Identity. Our eternal identity. So, Chita Mahaprabhu said, I am not a Brahmana, I am not a king, I am not a Vaishya, I am not a sutra, I am not a student, I am not a householder, I am not a non-shed, I am not what? They are tired, but, but,…”

children.topic: One question answered in one second
children.note:
Maharaj tells of a devotee who searched many places for years with one question, who am I. Told in a second that he is a spirit soul, eternal servant of Krishna, he never went back to his old business.

🎙 Maharaj at 66:51 (auto-transcript): “and reveal of identity for us when his his grace brahmadana prabhu brahmadana prabhu he told he was he was our uh this resident strong or we join us so he told he told us that for years he was searching well my he said through many pools and and different different places…”

A colleague gradually became like the position he held. If even a temporary identity shapes behaviour so deeply, how much more living from our eternal identity. A cultivated habit is very hard to cure, so cultivate pure Krishna consciousness. — “So we should be careful with what we are cultivating.”

🎙 Maharaj at 69:58 (auto-transcript): “when i was when i was working one of our friends it was like this but the position he has in the company he started working like this eventually eventually became like this i'm just i said he was working because of the position Yes. He became like this. And those who lose him…”

Cultivation must be continuous because forgetting is also continuous. When we keep away from something, forgetfulness of it goes deeper; better to cultivate what is eternal.

🎙 Maharaj at 72:23 (auto-transcript): “Continuous because Because Forgetting also Continuous Is it true? When we keep away from something With them Our forgetfulness goes deeper Eventually it doesn't exist it doesn't exist at all better we cultivate the one that will exist spirituality yes continue we must hear…”

Of all the senses the ear is the most important; while we sleep the eyes and nose rest, but a cry of danger still wakes us.

🎙 Maharaj at 73:51 (auto-transcript): “yes of all the senses the ear is most important when we sleep the eye will see the noise will smell anything can we work no only the ear works so it is very important so hearing Don't forget, 1-1-5 purports. Next. Hearing Jabba is important. Chanting Jabba should be done…”

Prabhupada's advice: chant early, concentrate on the sound, pronounce each name distinctly. Speed comes on its own; what matters is hearing. — “The name is fully independent.”

🎙 Maharaj at 75:00 (auto-transcript): “Very good. It is true. It's in practical. As you continue to make advance by constantly hearing nicely, the speed will naturally come on its own. The name is fully independent. You will be acting like that as you continue to grow. So the speed, we should not depend on that…”

If the names are not pronounced distinctly and heard, we miss much of their potency, which Rupa Gosvami says cannot be estimated.

🎙 Maharaj at 75:35 (auto-transcript): “you think here pronouncing the his name distinctly distinctly that is where everything lies that is where it is coming from if it's not distinctly from us and we don't hear it we are missing we are missing a lot the potency which is there that Rupa Goswami said he cannot…”

Chanting aloud is like shouting at the mind; it pays attention and cannot wander, and we are forced to hear. Chant and hear, regularly, and everything will come. — “if you shout on your mind, Hare Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 76:39 (auto-transcript): “You know, when you chant La out, you are shouting on your mind. If you shout on somebody, what does it do? If you shout on somebody, what does it do? It will give you attention. It will give you attention if you shout on your mind, Hare Krishna. The mind will not go away. You…”

Prayer is the language of a servant. We pray naturally in an earthquake; in material life we are always in danger, so a devotee should always be prayerful.

🎙 Maharaj at 78:26 (auto-transcript): “Yesterday, we were looking at emergency. Emergency means what? Sacrifice said here, if there is an earthquake, then emergency means what? emergency means. Always think that earthquake is an emergency. Now it's an earthquake. So I should always be prayerful. We shouldn't wait…”

Not only ask but thank. Krishna brought each of us here and arranged for us to meet Srila Prabhupada. Lacking appreciation, we miss much of His mercy.

🎙 Maharaj at 79:27 (auto-transcript): “compulsively pray to Krishna. Thank him. Not only harassing him to give us something, but thank him for what he's doing. He gave us realization. Do you know what? Krishna gave us realization. He gave us shelter. He gave us so many things, everything. We should thank him for…”

To see reasons for gratitude, visit a hospital: people crying all day, no money, no family near. We have beautiful deities, devotees, scriptures and prasadam.

🎙 Maharaj at 81:14 (auto-transcript): “thank you. If you want to realize it, visit the hospital. Sure? Visit the hospital. You see people who have been there crying the whole day. Doctors have no attention to them. But we don't have that situation. Some people, they're going to spend the whole of them normally…”

Effort alone means thinking we can do it by our own strength; mercy alone would make Krishna partial. We work on our weaknesses and pray at the same time.

🎙 Maharaj at 83:33 (auto-transcript): “effort and mercy what are necessary and required one is not sufficient effort effort alone means you can get it by your own strength and mercy alone means partiality otherwise one christian will give me i will not give others i will give you not give to me so everyone make it…”

Pray before, during and after japa. No candle, incense or temple is needed; simply talk to Krishna. The deities are persons who hear and see. — “Talk to Krishna. Talk to him.”

🎙 Maharaj at 85:29 (auto-transcript): “that will help us. We need the strength to succeed. And the way to build our strength is to pray, to communicate with Krishna. Praying you don't need a candle, you don't need incense, you don't need a temple, you don't need a date, nothing. You don't need a Ganga water. Just…”

Prabhupada concluded that one who cannot rise early is not very serious about spiritual life. The widow had no grand achievement, only one humble offering faithfully repeated.

🎙 Maharaj at 87:40 (auto-transcript): “yes serious about spiritual life she woke up before continue read the last sentence in john powder seriousness comes first rising good the widow had no ground achievement only one humble offering have fully repeated Seriousness is measured not by dramatic acts, but by small…”

children.topic: Write it and post it around
children.note:
Write the key sentences from these classes and paste them around your room so that you see them and remember what Brahma-muhurta is for.

🎙 Maharaj at 88:32 (auto-transcript): “If we want to remember something, one thoughtful Christian, This is not a serious thing we have discussed that one can write them and paste them around you. Understand? If you write this sentence, paste it around. So you will be seeing them regularly. It will help to remind…”
The mahatmas strictly observe the rules given by the acaryas, so they are sure of the result.

Caturmasya has just begun. Let these four months be the container for rising faithfully during Brahma-muhurta, then decide on a lifelong commitment at Utthana Ekadasi from lived experience.

🎙 Maharaj at 96:07 (auto-transcript): “Okay. Everything is there. Everything is there for us. In one another's morning, 500 years ago in Puri, Swarupa Damodara came daily to Pundarika Vidyanthi's door. Swarupa Damodara would come every day and the two would go together to see Lord Jagannatha. Svarupa Damodara missed Pundarika Vidyanidhi one morning and asked, I did not see you today, what happened? That is caring. A pure devotee has a soft heart, and real japa softens the heart; not checking on others is selfishness.

nodeData.topic: Session 01 · Importance of Brahma Muhurta (Nairobi)
nodeData.note: SB 10.70.4–5 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The first Nairobi session presents Brahma-muhurta as the devotee's treasure: not merely an early hour, since business people are also awake, but the time for spiritual activity. Maharaj explains what the hour is, why everyone agrees with it yet few practise, that real hearing means acting on what enters the heart, and how Krishna Himself rose at this hour in Dvaraka to teach us. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj opens by asking the room what Brahma-muhurta is. Answers come: an auspicious time an hour and a half before sunrise, the most important time for spiritual activity, the time of goodness.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:31 (auto-transcript): “if I should ask you, what is Brahmam Kota? What do you say? What is Brahmam Kota? brahma brahma what does he mean what is it auspicious time in the morning one and a half hours before thank you what else what else what is brahma yes most important time for doing spiritual…”

nodeData.topic: Session 02 · Importance of Brahma Muhurta (Nairobi)
nodeData.note: BG 9.29; SB 5.18.9 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj completes the first section: chanting on waking protects us like a vaccination, the Gurvastakam sung with care and attention promises service to Krishna, and Srila Prabhupada, old and frail, bathed in the Allahabad cold to bring his disciples to mangala-arati. The heart of the class is the difference between following Brahma-muhurta as a rule and cherishing it as a treasure, followed by homework to observe our mornings honestly and a lively question-and-answer session. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Srila Prabhupada writes that on rising one should immediately chant Hare Krishna, or at least Krishna, Krishna. Maharaj calls the practice at this hour a vaccination against the three modes of nature. — “This period and the practice is what? Vaccination.”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:23 (auto-transcript): “How do we sing these? What is our mind when we are singing? What is our mind? Where? What is our mind while we are singing? We are chanting this prayer every morning. So the Vishwana Chakravarti Chakravarti said, we are chanting with great care and attention. He said, we…”

nodeData.topic: Session 03 · Importance of Brahma Muhurta (Nairobi)
nodeData.note: SB 11.13.4; Siksastakam 2 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The sattvic hour: Maharaj answers why devotees treasure Brahma-muhurta when Krishna and His name are available all day. Place and time both shape the mind; scripture, Ayurveda and modern science agree on the value of the early hours; and because we are not yet free of offences, we need the hour's support, just as a feast needs an appetite. Questions follow on strict morning programs and keeping sadhana while travelling. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.
