maps.title: Brahma's Prayers · Day 08 · What Am I Before You?

nodeData.topic: Day 08 · What Am I Before You?
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.11 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma measures himself against Krishna and finds there is no comparison, and Maharaj makes the point vivid: counting the souls in one tiny universe, asking who can walk out of it, and telling the Purana story of Narada searching for the greatest thing. Scripture puts us in our place so that we stay humble and paint our hearts with Krishna. In the questions he speaks on overcoming pride, making every day a festival, and seeing the cause rather than the instrument. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma sets his small body and his universe of material elements beside Krishna, through whose body countless universes drift like specks of dust. Maharaj reads two translations and sums it up: there is nothing to compare.

children.topic: A torch pointed at the sun
children.note:
Shine a torch at the sun and the sun does not even notice it. Brahma is telling us how insignificant we are.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:11 (auto-transcript): “like a good example the thoughts if you point a touch to the Sun do they have effect thoughts if you point a touch to the Sun the any effects no this will listen when they don't even notice it no it doesn't exist they thought I don't exist for the Sun is one of Brahma is…”

Scientists roughly estimate nine or ten billion human beings, and those come from only the 400,000 human species. Maharaj asks the class to reckon how many billions there must be among the aquatics, birds, insects and the rest — and that is one tiny universe.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:51 (auto-transcript): “You know, insignificant. Just look at it, that in this our material universe, this our own material universe, where scientists have imperfectly, imperfectly calculated that there are 9 billion people a man, and that is only human beings. That is only human beings. It is not…”

children.topic: Who can claim to be God?
children.note:
We are one tiny being among all these, inside one small universe that is part of the Lord. Thinking oneself God is madness; even Brahma says, what am I? — “what can be more foolish than this one”

🎙 Maharaj at 41:17 (auto-transcript): “and we are one of one of these tiny ones inside here we're going one tiny one inside so lebron i said so look at the person who is expanding this figure and look at so when are we in comparison for those of us who think we are god what can be more foolish than this one for…”

We do not even know what is happening behind our own back, yet we act as if we know everything.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:03 (auto-transcript): “insignificant tiny tiny foolish creature who knows nothing what is happening behind my back don't see it can you tell me what is happening behind your back your back your own back not somebody's on what is happening there yeah no crazy this is not brahma this is not brahma He…”

children.topic: The gift of scripture and acarya
children.note:
The beauty of scripture, and of an acarya like Brahma who knows our real situation, is that it shows us where we stand, so that we know how to behave. — “The scripture put us where we are so we know our position.”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:39 (auto-transcript): “He is telling us where we are. This is the beauty of the scripture. The scripture put us where we are so we know our position. So we don't act foolishly. The beauty of having scripture, beauty of having an Acharya, a Brahma, who knows exactly our situation. yes yes we are too…”

Can anyone say, 'I'm tired of this place, I'm going to Vaikuntha, goodbye'? No — we are locked in. Our only opportunity comes when the mercy of guru and Krishna descends together.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:14 (auto-transcript): “who know who will know how to behave nice so brahma said i'm enclosed in the spotlight universe we are locked up in this universe can anyone escape this universe without presence mercy can anyone anyone walk out of this i'm tired of this much so let me just get out now go to…”

Even when mercy comes, how many benefit? People find it hard to chant, and two devotees cannot share a room for a day without misunderstanding — all the work of false ego.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:36 (auto-transcript): “together that is our opportunity and even that even that how many people benefit from the mystery a good ambition how many people why would you find it difficult to chance to say you see you see find it difficult to chance to say them for four years straight up thank you…”

Prabhupada explains that Brahma's whole creation cannot compete with Krishna, whose bodily rays produce countless universes. Maharaj: even a man on leave from the office is busy all month; Krishna's mystic sleep is not idleness — he is meeting his managers from many universes.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:22 (auto-transcript): “So look, it is Brahma's experience. From Brahma's experience, you told us that, you know, when even here in the material world, when someone is on leave from office, when someone is on leave from office, or leave is on leave from office, so it doesn't mean the person is not…”

Krishna is conscious of everything, inside and outside, directly and indirectly, from the very first verse of the Bhagavatam. How could anyone compare himself with such a person?

🎙 Maharaj at 49:42 (auto-transcript): “you massage your dead body oh no it's a life only that you massage yes this is krishna the supreme position he's doing everything that has to do outside and inside he is conscious of everything inside and outside therefore right from the beginning of the verbatim christian is…”

A story from the Puranas: Narada, who travels everywhere, is asked by the Lord in Vaikuntha what is the greatest thing he has seen.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:04 (auto-transcript): “okay thank you it's material yes it's material i'll tell you tell you something from the purana One day Lord Narada Muni went to see Lord Vishnu, Vaikunda. He used to go regularly. So one day he went to see Narayana. So Narada said, Oh, Brahmaji. So Naradaji, yeah, I have a…”

Narada says the dense earth element. But water has swallowed half the earth — so water. But a sage chasing two demons drank up the whole ocean — so the sage.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:35 (auto-transcript): “See in this material, what is very dense and is dominating all of us, the element is earth. So Naramuni say yes, the earth element, the earth is dominating, is the most powerful because all the living entities are controlled by this. so now you say are you sure are you sure…”

children.topic: The star, the sky, the Lord
children.note:
That sage became a star, held in the sky; and the sky is covered by the Supreme Lord's form. So the Lord is the greatest.

nodeData.topic: Day 09 · A Child Kicking in the Womb
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma asks Krishna to treat his offence as a mother treats the kicks of the child in her womb, and Maharaj unfolds the image: our helplessness in the womb, Krishna's constant care, and Brahma's tactful plea that he is still a child within the Lord. Through the pastime of baby Nimai eating a brahmana's offering, he shows how a child's faults are met with laughter and how real practice shows in one's life. No questions were taken because of a network failure in Lagos. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma calls Krishna Adhoksaja and asks whether a mother is offended when the child inside her kicks — and whether anything at all lies outside the Lord. Maharaj: the answer is no; everything is within him.

Some pregnant women complain of pain and blame everyone. But in truth a mother is happy to feel the baby move — and worried, off to the doctor, if it stops. — “Actually, the mother feels happy when the child is kicking.”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:09 (auto-transcript): “the brahma said i am you are my mother in your belly i'm kicking touching you because the mother get angry you get up to my woman don't disturb me why are you kicking me i'm cutting you don't you appreciate my sacrifice i'm cutting you for nine more don't you see i'm having…”

The child is shut in a tight place with no door, no window, no air, bent double. That has been our situation again and again.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:23 (auto-transcript): “So the woman said, yes, that is the relationship between me and you. you you are my mother and i am in the room helplessly trying to get out because i'm tight opening tight of very very tight locked up closed can you imagine no ventilation no ventilation in the in the room no…”

Even after birth we are still suffocated — not by our surroundings but by the reactions of our own sinful acts. In the womb at least we feel it.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:11 (auto-transcript): “comfortable situation no that has been our situation since all over even when we get out we are still suffocated what is suffocating us is not even the environment where we are What is suffocating us is the reaction of our sinful activities. So when we are in the womb, it is…”

The Bhagavatam describes the deep, pitiful prayers every one of us made in the womb — let me out and I will worship you — not once but many times. Now we have forgotten.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:50 (auto-transcript): “Chapter 11, it describes how all of us were feeling before now. Now we don't feel it. Before now, when we were in the womb, all of us would make them very, very, very philosophical, pathetic prayers for the Christians. Please, let me get out. I will worship you. All of us…”

Helpless in the womb, we were sustained by Krishna. Now that we are out, we act independent and forget the one who helped us when we could not move.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:45 (auto-transcript): “a living entity as foolish as we are when we are in the womb completely helpless who maintains us helpless in the womb tight of the whole canal no ventilation helpless the body is not even strong to get into who helped us at that time not yogmaya you know yogmaya but…”

Krishna helps all the time, whether we worship him or not; he gives food and air even to those who reject him, and often they have more material facility than believers.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:50 (auto-transcript): “are completely helpless christian helps all the time not sometimes all the time either we worship you don't worship him you pray to him don't pray to him he will give us our food to give us air to breathe if we look carefully if we don't worship christian who doesn't pray to…”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:16 (auto-transcript): “So I am within you, I am within you, I am inside you. Actually, my existence is because of you, which is true. My existence is because of you. Chagana Mishra took…”

The brahmana stopped him: what does a small child know? We punish such a child only by laughing — like a mother who smiles at the mess her baby makes, which in an adult would be abominable. — “That's how you punish a little child. Just laugh.”

Persuaded again, the brahmana cooked once more while the family shut Nimai in a room and guarded the door. Nimai lay smiling at their childish arrangements and pretended to sleep.

All the guards fell asleep and Nimai ate again. 'You called me and I came — have you forgotten me in Vrindavan?' He showed the brahmana his form, and later asked him to keep it secret.

Seeing Visvarupa, Nityananda's form, the brahmana asked whose son this was — a body like Narayana's. Maharaj: the brahmana's own long devotion shone from him too. Our practice should be visible. — “Our practice should show in our daily life.”

🎙 Maharaj at 50:08 (auto-transcript): “Who is the father of this boy? His body is just like Narayan, but do he try to conceal himself? What is he saying? That is a proof of his practice. Our practice should show in our daily life. What we are practicing should show in our daily lives. Our Christian consciousness…”

children.topic: Attract by the quality of life
children.note:
Practise carefully and consciously so that purification shows wherever we are, and people are drawn by the quality of the result.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:57 (auto-transcript): “is showing fully in his body. Let us be like this. Let us be like this, that we are carefully, consciously practicing our Christian consciousness in such a way that our daily practice is bringing you the purification that what we are practicing should be showing in our lives…”

When Jagannatha Misra threatened to beat Nimai, the Lord ran — to give his devotee that pleasure. The cowherd boys fight Krishna to delight him; Bhisma gave him the fight he wanted. Demons fight to kill; only devotees, through love, know how to please him. — “only devotees know the science because of love”

🎙 Maharaj at 53:24 (auto-transcript): “he's running for this devotee the running the devotee will not beat christmas in case i know even when the cowboys are fighting it don't they don't they are not fighting to beat christian they're fighting to give christian pleasure all that comes i wanted to fight to kill…”

Many of us, Maharaj included, feel we pray, chant and fast and get no answer. Yet the brahmana only called and Krishna came. Seeing no answer can come from our own ingratitude.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:16 (auto-transcript): “here many of us including myself and many devotees feel that they're praying and praying and praying and christian no answer i'm begging krishna begging i've chanted almost broken all my teeth chanting fasting all the caddies and what is no answer no answer don't answer so…”

The purport explains Adhoksaja as the one who keeps the senses under his control: I am under your control, so though foolish I am like your child. Brahma deep in the womb is like us in a dark room with no door.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:32 (auto-transcript): “the secondary drama praises the lord trusha the second to be a garden and very i mean monitor of the topic known as adokshaja means he who has the power of the senses under his control he who has the power of the senses under his control adokshaja since i am under your…”

Krishna might reply: you are standing before me, not in a womb. Brahma's answer: the whole universe is within you, so although I appear outside, I am still inside you.

🎙 Maharaj at 63:20 (auto-transcript): “of drama the brahma you are speaking very nicely to me but you are in the womb you are standing before me here you are not inside the womb you are outside so i will tell your friend seriously because you are you are stupid at the challenge the world exists a followers of some…”

Even materially one stays a child before one's father. Srila Prabhupada called grown, married disciples boys and girls — that was his vision. We are all children before Krishna.

So Brahma asks Krishna not to take his offence seriously but to help him mature so he will not offend again. — “Brahma is very wise.”

🎙 Maharaj at 67:03 (auto-transcript): “therefore, don't take my opinion seriously. Rather, you should try to help me so I can get mature and not offend you again in the next time. children.topic: Inside and outside, like the airs
children.note:
Our body has airs and fires both inside and outside — fire digests food within — and a yogi can kindle fire by joining the air within to the air without. In the same way nothing is outside the Lord's energy. — “So all the elements are outside and inside.”

nodeData.topic: Day 10 · Born from You, Your Own Child
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.13-14 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma pleads that he was born directly from the Lord's navel and so deserves a child's forgiveness; Maharaj shows how a king's own son, or a crying baby on a flight, is treated differently — while warning that real parents still correct. Brahma then calls Krishna the original Narayana, and Maharaj explains why the cowherd boy with two hands is the complete Supreme Person, fuller than four-armed Narayana. In the questions he insists that no one is innocent before karma, and that Brahma's bewilderment should make us more careful. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: 10.14.13 — Am I not born from you?
children.note: Brahma recalls that at the dissolution Narayana lies on the waters and Brahma appears on the lotus from his navel — so is he not Krishna's own offspring? Maharaj: Brahma is right.

All living beings, moving and non-moving, come from the Lord as their father. Yesterday Krishna said Brahma was outside the womb; today Brahma adds that he came from it.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:30 (auto-transcript): “It's true. All of us, all living entities, all living entities, both moving, came about the Kassari Vishnu because he is the father,”

Brahma asks special forgiveness as the Lord's direct child. A citizen and the king's son may commit the same crime, but they are not dealt with alike: 'I know your father.'

🎙 Maharaj at 45:12 (auto-transcript): “special forgiveness for offenses. Yes, a citizen may be, some citizen may be arrested for doing something and the child of the king may do the same thing but they don't have the same permission the child of the king has a different punishment because biologically he came out from”

Brahma himself once wanted to punish a son who misbehaved before him, then forgave him because he was his child. Now he asks Krishna for the same.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:12 (auto-transcript): “forgive my foolishness forgive my misunderstanding consider me as a child after the brahma himself did that when one of his son the moon misbehaved before him but i wanted to kill him you are my son well trained a moon you don't know the etiquette grandma wait after him and…”

children.topic: The prince who was sent away
children.note:
In one kingdom the king's son kept robbing and was released every time out of respect for his father. Finally the king himself sent him out. An ideal parent does not pamper a child into ruin. — “We should not pamper the children to the point that they get spoiled.”

🎙 Maharaj at 48:42 (auto-transcript): “or the father is a king in a in a kardashim muhammad one of the kings is one of one of the kings his son was a rogue who were robbing people and he was arrested many times but when they oh it's our king's son he listened but other children were punished for the king…”

children.topic: The baby who cried all flight
children.note:
On a long flight to New Delhi a baby cried without stopping. A passenger shouted at the parents, but they never thought of throwing the child away — it was their own child, so they kept caring for it.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:06 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, I remember one time from New York City and from France to New Delhi, One child cried for friends to leave them continuously, non-stop, continuously. A parent, they tried to control the child to stop crying for the child to continue.”

Maharaj recalls how much he troubled his own mother, who carried him through rain and sun and never abandoned him. Brahma's plea is the same: consider me, I was born from you. — “I disturbed my mother day and night.”

🎙 Maharaj at 55:16 (auto-transcript): “I remember also I disturbed my mother seriously. I disturbed my mother day and night. My mother was carrying me that night alone in the rain, in the sun. She suffered. She didn't throw me away because it's a child for my womb. It's a pleasure. So the Brahma says, please…”

Others may or may not have come from you, Brahma says, but I certainly did. Because the Lord is our father, we too have the right to beg his causeless mercy. — “I have a special relationship with you.”

🎙 Maharaj at 58:28 (auto-transcript): “Others may or may not come from you, but certainly I am. I have a special relationship with you. in that way i'm begging for to beg for costlessness that is our our right our right because the question is our father we have a right to beg for so we'll go to text four”
Brahma declares Krishna the original Narayana, the Supersoul and witness of all, and Narayana his expansion. The purport places this after Brahma's defeat in stealing the boys and calves.

As the Gita says, Krishna pervades everything with one fragment of himself — the Supersoul alone maintains this universe. If a small part does all this, what to speak of Krishna himself? — “Small part of Krishna is doing that.”

Krishna objects: I'm a dark cowherd boy standing here, not lying on the water — how am I Narayana? Brahma replies that nara also means the living beings, whose shelter Krishna is. Krishna draws out his devotees, and they answer to teach us. — “Krishna is very, very smart, stimulating his devotees”

Narayana is perfectly proper; he would never steal butter or cry before his mother. Only Krishna does such things.

children.topic: Q2 · How do I stay safe?

nodeData.topic: Day 11 · Hearing Is Believing
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.15-16 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma asks the Lord to show the same mercy now that he showed when he first revealed himself, and Maharaj draws from Brahma's first experiences of ignorance and fear the lesson that austerity and obedient hearing come before seeing. Through Gajendra he shows that heartfelt prayer to Krishna alone is real fortune, and through the pot-and-house riddle that Krishna holds the universe while standing within it. In the questions he speaks on duty without love, the demigods, and what a guru's silence means. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma, having repented his impudence, now gives reasons why the Lord should forgive him; the verse turns on the Lord being hidden from him and then suddenly revealed.

Maharaj admires Brahma's intelligence: when I searched for you in ignorance, you revealed yourself by causeless mercy; I am in the same foolish state now, so show me that mercy again.

nodeData.topic: Day 12 · Only Krishna Can Do This
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.17-18 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma sees that the universe inside Krishna and the one outside are the same, and Maharaj explains why everyone, even demons, seeks a higher blessing, and why the holy name makes every flawed effort perfect. The material world is not imaginary — we feel heat, cold and hunger — but it is temporary, and only mercy reveals the Lord's deeper pastimes. In verse 18 Krishna becomes the calves, the boys and countless four-armed forms; in the questions Maharaj speaks on touching devotees' feet, pleasing the guru and why blessings come through practice. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: 10.14.17 — The same universe, inside and out
children.note: Brahma says the universe Krishna showed within his abdomen is now manifest outside in exactly the same form — something only his inconceivable energy could arrange.

children.topic: We feel the heat and cold

nodeData.topic: Day 13 · The Supreme and Beautiful Person
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.19-20 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Krishna acts through Brahma, Vishnu and Siva while staying far in the background, and the ultimate truth is a supreme and beautiful person — even Sankaracarya sings of his flute and dress. He appears among every species to show he is equal to all, yet reciprocates with those who surrender, and like the sun he never really comes or goes. In the questions Maharaj explains spiritual numbness, how to deal well with others, whether Brahma is a jiva, and what was wrong with Ekalavya. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 14 · One Krishna, Countless Pastimes
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.21 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma admits no one can understand how the Lord's pastimes go on endlessly through his own energy. Maharaj contrasts a story of one husband who could not deal fairly with twenty-seven wives with Krishna in Dvaraka, doing something different in every queen's palace and attending 16,100 weddings in one day; Varaha shows the Lord is never degraded by the forms he takes. The recording is very fragmentary, and the reflection asks us to stop comparing our journey with others', since Krishna's care for each devotee is personal. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma says no one in the three worlds can understand how and where the Lord expands his mystic energy and performs his pastimes.

Maharaj reads the verse slowly, dwelling on Brahma's admission that the Lord's spiritual potency is beyond anyone's grasp.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:10 (auto-transcript): “Also, the Dhammas, dear Godhead, no one can understand the mystery of how you are spiritual in it.”

These pastimes are going on continuously; there is no moment when Krishna is not performing them — they are happening right now.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:46 (auto-transcript): “Where past signs are taking place continuously in these three worlds. Continuously. There is no person or Christian not performing. It does not exist. This activity is right now. As Christian feels one person, it's all different.”

To show what Krishna does is impossible for anyone else, Maharaj tells of one who married twenty-seven sisters.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:44 (auto-transcript): “Julia, so far, so far. He married 27, 27 daughters. What did he do? He expanded 27 years. So how did he deal with the 27, 26, 27? He couldn't form.”

He could not manage them; he was attached to one, and the others complained they hardly felt married.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:18 (auto-transcript): “So how did he deal with the 27, 26, 27? He couldn't form. He was attached to, what was 26, are we really married? Our husband does not. See, we can't say that we are married to only one sister.”

maps.title: Brahma's Prayers · Day 15 · A Dream Full of Miseries

nodeData.topic: Day 15 · A Dream Full of Miseries
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.22-23 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The material world seems real, like a dream, yet brings repeated miseries; since Krishna made it, we should take his word for it, as we would a manufacturer's manual, and follow the mahajanas. It is not imaginary — we eat and feel it — but it is temporary, a school of love where we learn to serve under expert guidance. In verse 23 Krishna's body is shown to be free of material change, and Maharaj urges devotees to know their Krishna as closely as one knows someone one loves. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma continues describing Krishna's inconceivable potency: by his illusory energy this temporary universe appears real like a dream, covers our consciousness and brings repeated miseries.

Maharaj stresses the words 'repeated miseries': whichever way we turn in this world, there is misery.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:21 (auto-transcript): “And Christian said, this material world is full of, full of repeated miseries, full of repeated miseries, repeated miseries, as a very important translation and words. 🎙 Maharaj at 38:01 (auto-transcript): “Yes, the same thing that Gandhi is speaking to you. This material world is temporal, full of misery. The Christian certified this material world to be temporal. And this is what the creator of the universe of the Christian said, this material world is. So are we not foolish,…”

A friend gave Maharaj a travelling bag with a padlock like two he already had. Sure he knew how it worked, he skipped the manual — and locked it shut. — “The manufacturers knows what it did.”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:06 (auto-transcript): “some years ago a friend bought me a traveling bag and then inside the bag there is a padlock i had similar padlock about two or two that was the third one they looked the same So, I was thinking, ah, it's the same thing. 🎙 Maharaj at 40:15 (auto-transcript): “world is so which among us who think that we know better even the brahma who created he is called secondary creator he's called secondary creator he created after christian has created after christian has given him all the ingredients so the brahma cannot know better than…”

Prahlada Maharaja says he fears not the Lord's ghastly form but his illusory energy, which no effort of his could overcome. Who among us knows better than Prahlada? Our security is to follow the great authorities. — “simply follow the path of the Mahajans”

There is no tiger in your bedroom, yet the dreamer is afraid and feels it. Only one who is awake does not feel it — so a pure devotee, not sleeping like us, is not touched by our illusion.

Maharaj asks how we feel when the urge for sense gratification comes: restless, angry, helpless. What we call enjoyment is only getting free from that pain; the only solution is to wake up.

Yet the universe is real: when we eat a mango, an apple or a peanut we feel it, though hunger and the body come and go. Pure devotees understand this and are not in illusion. — “It is real in that sense. Only it is temporal.”

We have forgotten that we are eternal servants and Krishna the eternal master, so he made this world to teach us. If we have no love for each other we cannot have love for Krishna; we must perfect our life here. — “Krishna has created the school of love for us.”

nodeData.topic: Day 16 · The Guru's Light Removes Fear
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.24-25 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains why the spiritual master is greater than the sun: he gives the eye that sees Krishna as the soul of all souls, and his sound enters the heart through the ear. With the rope-and-snake verse he shows that only waking up through hearing ends fear, while material scientists keep us in anxiety. In the questions he speaks on tasting the holy name, wanting to chant, and crying daily for help. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Lagos, day 16: Brahma continues to glorify Krishna. The verse is about those who receive clear vision from the guru, see Krishna as the soul of all souls, and so cross material existence. Maharaj reads several translations and Bhagavad-gita 4.9.

children.topic: The guru is more than the sun

nodeData.topic: Day 17 · Bhakti Beyond Speculation
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.26 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes Brahma's lesson that bhakti is superior to speculative knowledge: for the eternally free soul both bondage and liberation are ideas born of ignorance, like paper claiming to break iron. Moving into the next verse, he shows how speculators forget both Krishna and themselves, while undivided devotion gives the access they lack. In the questions he says illusion ends when we actually hear, and the speaker's duty is simply to sow the seed. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Lagos, day 17. After the opening prayers Maharaj announces the theme Brahma teaches from text 26 onward and repeats it several times. — “Bhakti is superior to speculative knowledge.”

🎙 Maharaj at 37:27 (auto-transcript): “So we continue our reading from Simad Bhagavatam, Canto 10, Chapter 14, Brahma's Prayers to Lord Krishna. And today we will continue from Text 26. The verse treats both the idea of being bound and the idea of being liberated as products of ignorance, which lose their meaning once the soul is known as distinct from matter. Maharaj reads two translations.

children.note:

nodeData.topic: Day 21 · Krishna Has Given Himself Away
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.34 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma begs for mercy by glorifying Krishna honestly, and wonders what reward Krishna could give the residents of Vraja, since he has already given himself to them. Maharaj describes the heart-to-heart friendship of the cowherd boys, hearts holding nothing but Krishna, and Krishna as the property of his devotees. Questions cover the guru as friend, tasting real bhakti, Putana's family, and why Hanuman is glorified while Lakshmi is not. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Lagos. After some confusion over the text number, the class takes up the next prayer, in which Brahma seeks Krishna's mercy by glorifying him.

It is natural to praise someone whose mercy we want; materially people flatter. Brahma is not flattering — he describes the real qualities that attract him and begs with humility. — “But our system will not flatter.”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:26 (auto-transcript): “This is natural. We want to get the mercy of somebody. Even materially speaking, materially speaking you have to flatter the person. But our system will not flatter. We tell exactly what the person is. This is personal. glorify the person, tell you the qualities of that…”

We name the qualities that draw us to the person and expect that, when pleased, he will grant mercy. Brahma tells exactly the good fortune of the Vrajavasis. — “We tell exactly what the person is.”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:41 (auto-transcript): “We tell exactly what the person is. This is personal. glorify the person, tell you the qualities of that person that is attracting you to the person, and what we expect when the person is pleased, they will grant it. That is natural. We don't go to beg someone, we go to beg…”
Brahma's mind is bewildered: Krishna is every blessing, and he has already given himself to the people of Vraja — even to Putana's family — so what else could he give them?

If we went to Brahma we would ask for houses and children. Brahma asks nothing like that; he is seeing Krishna's pastimes in Vrindavan.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:38 (auto-transcript): “considering what will be happening in Brahma. If you go to Brahma, what do you say? If you go to Brahma today, what do you say? Somebody, houses, kids. The Brahma is not saying that. The Brahma is not saying that. What the Brahma is saying is different. See what Brahma is…”

Maharaj tells of the Lord guarding a devotee's door and refusing to leave without that devotee's permission. Krishna is the property of his devotees — not a lie; he demonstrated it. — “Krishna is the property of his devotees”

🎙 Maharaj at 45:41 (auto-transcript): “Until now, Lord Krishna is a security guard for the body. The demon came there too. So the demon told him, go and go and take care of the demon. Your city is the truth.”

children.topic: A king who asked for friendship
children.note:
Maharaj tells of a king who, about to retire, asked only one thing of those who served him: become my friend. A friend naturally shares what belongs to his friend.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:26 (auto-transcript): “I asked all the citizens, the workers all been working for him. Now I want to retire, so not celebrate. So bring their list, brought their list. So the king said, if I resign now, you'll learn like this.”

Brahma's word for their friendship is not an ordinary friend but a friend of the heart. The cowherd boys don't see Krishna as God.

No, he says Bhandesha, Mitra, Bhandu is just ordinary friend, just ordinary friend, hello, hello, Mitra is, as you read this, he is one who says friends heart to heart, the friends of Krishna, the friends of…”

When it is time for lunch the boys don't say, 'You are the Supreme, you needn't eat'. They say, 'You are hungry too — sit down and eat with us.' — “sit down let's eat together that is friendship”

🎙 Maharaj at 56:29 (auto-transcript): “as soon as you are hungry you also they didn't say you are supreme god here so you don't know to eat they didn't say that so as you are hungry you are also hungry so let us eat together you're watching us you are also hungry sit down let's eat together that is friendship that…”

Sugriva serves Ramacandra with reverence and would never tease him. The cowherd boys can tell Krishna, 'Keep quiet or I'll beat you — have you forgotten yesterday?' — “This is what we mean by friends.”

We eat for ourselves; the cowherd boys and girls eat because of Krishna, keeping the body for him. — “They are eating because of Krishna.”

Maharaj asks us to imagine a heart with no object in it at all except Krishna. That is what Brahma is seeing, and Krishna responds to it. — “their heart never thinks of anything except Krishna.”

children.note:

So that means will you continue devotional service or will you just stop? Because you don't have anything else to…”

Maharaj presses the point: having a second option at all is the downfall; only Krishna is the goal. — “You better think twice.”

children.note:
Scripture says to see the guru as good as Krishna, but that does not make him Krishna; he cannot do what Krishna does. Like iron in fire, he takes on the quality, but the difference remains. — “like a fire and an iron.”

children.note:
Vrajavasis relate to Krishna as friend or lover, not as God. At what stage does our scriptural knowledge give way to pure remembrance?

nodeData.topic: Day 22 · Same Activities, Different Heart
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.36 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. On his appearance day Maharaj explains Brahma's warning that, until we become devotees, desires are thieves, home is a prison and family affection is a chain. Sense gratification quietly steals our real self-interest and our life, while the guru keeps calling us to wake up. His puzzle for the class: the Vrajavasis do the same household work we do — the difference is that theirs is intensely engaged in pleasing Krishna. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Devotees celebrate Maharaj's appearance day. He thanks everyone who helps him in Krishna consciousness and returns to Brahma, who keeps appealing for mercy and glorifying the Vrajavasis.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:25 (auto-transcript): “brinda key yeah hey Krishna went to heartly thank all of you all of you who are making our life life in the christian consciousness thank you our head is eternally at your lotus feet eternally as as this as life continue as the sun shine as the moon shine obeisance is…”
The verse names three things that hold true until people become Krishna's devotees: material desire acts as a thief, the home as a prison, and family affection as a chain.

Maharaj asks what a thief is: one who takes your property without your knowledge — or, these days, openly.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:00 (auto-transcript): “devotees until we become devotees our material attachment and desires remain thieves thieves we all know what teeth means teeth teeth on who took your property without your knowledge or what your knowledge is the umbrella is a same message to you we are coming we are coming…”

Thieves once came in disguise at night, and people said switching on the light would chase them away. Now they come in broad daylight, turn on the light and rob you.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:02 (auto-transcript): “you'll are stealing what our knowledge is this chiefs a day in Africa they say brought daylight right broad daylight stealing before people will disguise themselves they go in the night but today today they turn no disguise no disguise what delight stealing so that is a gross…”

Maharaj tells how he left his phone charging on a train while he went to brush his teeth, half aware someone might take it. Someone walked right past him, and when he returned the phone was gone.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:50 (auto-transcript): “it all come on yeah I come and take it I was charging my phone in the train me train I was charging my phone and I was thinking I'm very clever or thinking that I will I went to brush my teeth or thinking from there I'm going to see to my the way I always say is our foolishly…”

He asks the class what sense gratification steals. Answers come: love for Krishna, focus, mind and intelligence, determination for sadhana, enthusiasm. Maharaj sums it up as our real self-interest, which is spiritual life. — “our self-interest is stolen by sense gratification”

🎙 Maharaj at 49:13 (auto-transcript): “since gratification is a thief a thief saying gratification is stealing what is saying of question stealing what is sense gratification stealing from us it's a question our affection for krishna good love for krishna good bhakti krishna consciousness good what is sense…”

Sense gratification destroys everything imperceptibly. Each sunrise and sunset takes our lifespan, yet we don't notice — just as a parent living with a child doesn't see it grow, while a visitor does.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:15 (auto-transcript): “sales gratification sales gratification is destroying everything imperceptibly everything our duration of life is going without seeing we don't notice that our days is going even though Babatam boldly I got them boldly mentioned as the Sun rise from west or not this way from…”

A pure devotee sees that we are wasting time. Like one sleeping in a burning building, we are asleep in the lap of illusion, and the guru keeps calling us to get up. — “that is the duty of a spiritual master to constantly remind us”

🎙 Maharaj at 52:17 (auto-transcript): “was he talking about similarly a pure devotee sees that we are wasting our time pure devotees that is the duty of a spiritual master to constantly remind us remind us that is the duty this wisdom master has a responsibility to help remind us out is to get up get up from…”

A forest fire burns dry and wet wood alike; the wet just takes longer. Those in goodness may last a little longer, but in Kali-yuga all the material modes end the same way.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:27 (auto-transcript): “a dava nana leader luka randoya canada from the vanilla dava vanilla forest burning everything the fire is burning everything but the dry wood and the wet wood the fire is drying up and bending everything it may take some time for a wood a wet wood to get been but it will be…”

We protest that rising early will make us sick — but the body is already sick. The medicine is bitter, yet it cures; after lifetimes of sleep, what have we gained? — “it is curing the disease”

🎙 Maharaj at 55:00 (auto-transcript): “constantly remind, get off. And we are trying to do that. Get off. Oh, let me sleep. Let me sleep. Get off. Hey, let me sleep, Guru. Let me sleep. Have to sleep. If I wake up early, I will get sick. you already see it you already see where we already sick body the body is…”

Some think they are enjoying life with a clear swimming pool, fine chairs and a waterbed. But a disturbed mind cannot relax, and anxiety follows a person until death.

nodeData.topic: Day 23 · Krishna Acts Like Us, for Us
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.37 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma says the Lord, though beyond the world, plays a worldly role to increase his devotees' joy. Maharaj tells how Krishna tamed King Nagnajit's seven bulls, shows why an acarya practises like a beginner, and explains with the lamp and the diamond why Krishna's pastimes shine brightest in this dark world. In the questions he explains Krishna's special care for devotees, how to hear speakers whose conduct does not match their words, and why we fail to follow the guru's instructions. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: 10.14.37 — Beyond the world, yet playing in it
children.note: Brahma's prayer today is about the Lord appearing on earth and behaving as if he were part of this world, simply to give his surrendered devotees more varieties of joy. The verse is recited and two translations are read.

Since Krishna is everything, there is no difficulty in his behaving like everything. Maharaj adds that what we see, hear and do should all be Krishna. — “whatever we hear should be krishna”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:44 (auto-transcript): “you are very worldly of this world. You behave like a part of this world. After all, Krishna is everything. So what is the difficulty? children.topic: He comes to spread his glories
children.note:
Maharaj recalls Brahma's words in the Brahma-samhita: Krishna displays here the activities of the spiritual world so that we can connect with his glories and save our lives.

Citing the Gita's third chapter, Maharaj notes that Krishna has nothing he must do, yet he acts like a conditioned soul to keep people in order, just as King Janaka set an example.

Maharaj quizzes the class about King Nagnajit, who set a test for anyone who wanted to marry into his family: control his seven bulls.

Like a pujari ready for work, Krishna tied his dhoti up to his knees and seized the bulls by the horns. Maharaj stresses the point is not the marriage but that Krishna behaves exactly like us.

Teaching by doing is the acarya's duty. Following Rupa Gosvami, even a pure devotee keeps the sadhana of a beginner to protect newer devotees from imitation: no one copies a hundred years of steady chanting, but everyone copies the one day it stops. — “everybody will follow that one”

children.topic: A lamp shines in the dark
children.note:
Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura's comparisons — a lamp in shade, a diamond on blue glass — explain why Krishna's pastimes amaze more in this world than in Vaikuntha. Pure devotees like Arjuna never judge Krishna by worldly standards.

children.note: Maharaj answers with the Gita's ninth chapter: Krishna envies no one, yet whoever serves him in devotion is in him and he is their friend. That is natural reciprocation, not discrimination.

children.note:
We belong to a community and should cooperate, so still attend. Fix the mind on the verse and Prabhupada's purport, and if you are eager Krishna will teach you something even through such a speaker; otherwise you leave frustrated.

nodeData.topic: Day 24 · Brahma Says: I Don't Know
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.38 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. After a month of hearing grandfather Brahma, Maharaj says the one thing that matters now is application. In this verse Brahma admits that the Lord's opulences are beyond his mind, body and words, and Maharaj shows why 'I don't know' is so rare and so valuable — the self-confident are the easiest to cheat, while Krishna is conquered only by humble devotees. In the questions he defines humility, compares gurus to teachers with more degrees, and explains how to make amends after hurting someone. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 25 · Giving the Universe Back
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.39 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Brahma asks Krishna's leave and offers back the universe he was only entrusted to manage — teaching us to stop claiming Krishna's property as our own. Maharaj shows Brahma's embarrassment through the image of a family meal spoilt, and Krishna's silence while Brahma talks on. He stresses finishing one's duty before moving on, and tells how Haridasa Thakura's previous lives were shaped by offences. In the questions he speaks on mindful service, making amends for offences to the guru, tulasi, discipline and Ekadasi. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma begs permission to leave, recognising Krishna as the knower and master of everything, and offers him this one universe. The verse is read with a second translation and the Krishna book passage on Brahma feeling out of place amid the simple love of Vrindavan.

Brahma created the universe but did not manufacture its ingredients, so he cannot claim it. We do the same with every little thing we receive — who gave it to you?

If, from familiarity or pride, one offends the spiritual master, sincerely asks forgiveness, and still loses one's services and meets silence — how should a disciple respond?

🎙 Question from the floor at 94:34 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, Gurudev. Please accept my humble obeisances. Thank you. My question is if we offend our spiritual master due to our conditioning like familiarity or superiority complex and also ask forgiveness many times which is really genuine and out of the heart. I mean from…”

Any offence should be rectified: it blocks Radha, Krishna and the return to Godhead. Citing the Gita, one who puts others in anxiety cannot be peaceful — and offending one's own spiritual master is the most dangerous.

🎙 Maharaj at 95:39 (auto-transcript): “If we make offence to anybody, anybody, we should try to rectify it. Because making offences, offences, in Sanskrit it's called aparada. It means no Srimetiradhana, no Krishna, no going back and back together. Zero.”

children.topic: The student who pushed the dean
children.note:
At a college in Lagos, a boy coming for admission pushed past a small, quiet man at the door. Inside, he saw the same man seated as dean of the faculty — and quietly left, losing his chance.

🎙 Maharaj at 97:36 (auto-transcript): “So one day, one day, Yapa College of Technology here in Lagos, here in Lagos, Nigeria, College of Technology, they did not faculty, it has a small body, not tall, not huge, it has a small body so when he's moving you don't you don't”

Do not let such a situation arise. Recognise the offence immediately, beg forgiveness and obtain mercy; avoiding offences is how we advance. — “So beg, beg for forgiveness, rectify it and never repeat it.”

🎙 Maharaj at 100:31 (auto-transcript): “So, we should not allow a situation like this to happen to us. So, if you make offence, we should go and beg off. And try not to repeat it. Nature put us in different, different ways. So beg, beg for forgiveness, rectify it and never repeat it.”

Though already forgiven, Madhai lamented daily for injuring Nityananda Prabhu, in whom all beings reside. Asked how to atone, Nityananda told him to build a bathing ghat on the Ganga for countless people — that is how mercy is obtained.

🎙 Maharaj at 101:52 (auto-transcript): “to repent again and again and again. That's what we learn from Chaitanya. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu already forgave them and took away all the jazz. But still, Madai was still, every day was lamenting, criticizing, criticizing himself, feeling very guilty. Lord Nityanana Prabhu's…”

On the neophyte stage offences are hard to avoid. A godbrother of Maharaj offended their guru by thinking himself senior in age or in memorised verses — but memorising is brain work, not realisation. — “What an age has to do with perfection, purity?”

🎙 Maharaj at 103:33 (auto-transcript): “On the neophyte platform, mundane neophyte platform, we cannot avoid making offence. So many, so many non-sensical things in my mind. One of my god brother was offending my guru by thinking, I'm senior to you, for age. I'm senior to you. May age to instruct me. In that way he…”

May washed, dried tulasi be offered when fresh leaves are not available, and can manjaris be used?

🎙 Question from the floor at 105:18 (auto-transcript): “we have two more questions in the chat box um should we take them now yes uh one question question first question is from his grace we know the bihari prabhuji prabhuji is asking since dried tulsi lasts longer is it okay to offer washed but dried tulsi if there is no constant…”

Outside India where tulasi is scarce, it is fine to dry and carry it — some places count out leaves, while in Mauritius it is so plentiful it garnishes food. Offering with manjaris is best of all.

🎙 Maharaj at 105:51 (auto-transcript): “is a problem in india in other places it's okay in other places yeah truth is very difficult but i don't see that in india so we should always upper race to see when manjaris is very very important very very important so opportunity with manjaris is best best any best so we…”

What is discipline, what does a disciplined devotee look like, and where does someone whose senses run loose begin?

🎙 Question from the floor at 107:40 (auto-transcript): “our last question for today's class from is from aman prabhuji prabhuji is saying thank you so much for the class my question is with respect to discipline he is writing it in three points first what is discipline second what does a disciplined person or a devotee look like…”

Discipline is the beginning of being a disciple: like iron put in fire to take shape, one undergoes difficulty to be transformed. — “Discipline means a process of character reformation.”

🎙 Maharaj at 108:37 (auto-transcript): “Discipline means a process of character reformation. Character reformation. want to reform somebody and that is the beginning of being a disciple disciple one is sent to the special massage to be trained to have a good character good character training training means that you…”

A teacher showed his students a beautiful piece of earthenware that 'told' its story: it was pounded while it cried, cut into shape and finally put in the fire — only then was it admired.

🎙 Maharaj at 110:03 (auto-transcript): “the uh an experienced teacher so he he told his discipline and he he got a new car from the store so he he took asses do you like this you like this do you like this okay you want to be like this it beautiful yes want to do like this yes it's okay do you know what makes this…”

Attractive character; no needless talk; the same behaviour watched or unwatched; keeping one's word; on time for japa and programmes without reminders; self-control even when provoked. — “a disciplined person will not misbehave either”

🎙 Maharaj at 112:52 (auto-transcript): “the second part was uh how does a disciplined person or a devotee looks like or what are the symptoms of disciplined person a disciplined person have character their character will be very appreciative like example because we are attractive because you have wonderful…”

Begin by controlling the tongue on Ekadasi. Maharaj criticises a temple offering lavish grain feasts on Ekadasi and says fasting is compulsory; leaving the body on Ekadasi is very auspicious.

🎙 Maharaj at 118:37 (auto-transcript): “uh there was a third part as well to the question i just wanted i was curious to know that uh yeah if somebody thank you thank you uh if someone whose minds and senses are out of control like a loose cannon as you have told that uh his character has been cushionable…”

maps.title: Brahma's Prayers · Day 26 · Obeisances As Long As the Sun Shines

nodeData.topic: Day 26 · Obeisances As Long As the Sun Shines
nodeData.note: SB 10.14.40 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. In the last class of the series Brahma ends his prayers by offering obeisances to Krishna for as long as the universe lasts, even to his gunja beads and the humble arka plant. Maharaj explains why the material world is real but temporary, why the open atheist is less dangerous than the religious cheat (the cat swami), and why Brahma calls himself a rakshasa from Satyaloka — teaching us to check daily whether our activities please or disturb Krishna. In the questions he distinguishes the gopis' self-forgetfulness from ignorance, and humility from self-pity, and ends by blessing the devotees after the month of Purushottama. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Brahma's final verse glorifies Krishna as the joy of the Vrishnis, the friend of the earth, demigods, brahmanas and cows, and the destroyer of irreligion and demons, and offers obeisances for as long as the universe exists. Gathered on the last day of Purushottama, the devotees hear it with two translations.

Maharaj takes Brahma's words personally: as long as there is life in this body, obeisances go on at Krishna's lotus feet without stopping. Sanatana Gosvami says Brahma is here in the ecstasy of nama-sankirtana, calling out names that recall Krishna's pastimes.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:30 (auto-transcript): “on to you as long as this life in this body as as long address life in this body my business is continuously offered at the lotus feet businesses is continuously offered at the lotus feet non-stop Nipopota Siddha Sanatangoswamy explaining According to Siddha Sanatangoswamy,…”

Brahma's 'millennium after millennium' prompts a question to the class about what it means.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:36 (auto-transcript): “be not such a biscuit um derma some tunnel party you get you get some of me you get you get some millennium after millennium that means what millennium after millennium means what was the minute us millennium after millennium after millennium after millennium what does it…”

The answer from the class: eternally. Brahma's obeisances and Krishna's pastimes continue without end.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:41 (auto-transcript): “me you get you get some millennium after millennium that means what millennium after millennium means what was the minute us millennium after millennium after millennium after millennium what does it mean what does that mean millennium after me what does that mean that was my…”

If the world were simply false, Krishna's appearance, his dancing and living in Vraja would be false too. They are real; the material world is real but temporary, sometimes manifest and sometimes not — and only for the unfortunate is it 'sometimes'.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:26 (auto-transcript): “continues so to say that material world is false is illusion from time immemorial to say that the material is false is illusion to say that material is temporal is real that is true otherwise why crisis appearing is illusion christian's advent is illusion christian's advent…”

Night and day keep alternating; no one calls the night false. It is real, but passing, and to see in it we need another energy — light. — “it is not false it is real but temporarily”

🎙 Maharaj at 46:07 (auto-transcript): “and the day comes night comes day comes night comes day comes so you cannot say the night is false no no it is not dark no it's not dark it is false you will see anything you won't see anything you need another energy the light the beauty to see in the darkness so it is not…”

children.topic: Hidden and open enemies of God
children.note:
Prabhupada's purport names two burdens on the earth: those who come alive after sunset for intoxication, gambling, illicit sex and meat-eating while calling themselves God-fearing, and open atheists.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:26 (auto-transcript): “intoxication gambling and meat eating it means what these activities are these attitudes are what illicit says intoxication gambling and meat eating the activities done in the darkness that means it is dark activity dark activities demoniac demonic activities that is one…”

Maharaj quizzes the class: the one who claims to be godly and cheats, or the one who says publicly there is no God? The atheist is better, because he is straightforward; the religious cheat invites you close and then destroys you.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:08 (auto-transcript): “atheists and demons which one is better after these two those who believe those who claim to be godly who belongs who claim to be godly those who claim to be godly those who claim to be godly and cheat people and those who declare who declare publicly I don't believe in God I…”

A cat dresses as a sannyasi with beads and tilaka and announces he is vegetarian. The relieved mice come for sadhu-sanga, chant and bow down — and the cat, delighted at how easy it is to be a swami, makes a feast of them.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:00 (auto-transcript): “teach you more dangerous more dangerous they are like a cat sanyasi cat sanyasi on the cat dress as a sanyasi down die high in the sky beat back still like on the face carry down i will come out the loo harry krishna harry krishna krishna krishna Hare Hare Hare, Hare Ram,…”

children.topic: The city is the real forest
children.note:
In the forest we know to beware of tigers; in the modern city, with water on tap, we never suspect danger — yet modern life drains our energy into sense gratification and makes us forget our real interest.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:50 (auto-transcript): “dangerous they're more dangerous yes just like our present society our present society are very dangerous than the forest when one is going to the forest we are sure we are concerned that there are tiger asses are the forest but when you live in the city what is it what is…”

One who calls everyone 'Prabhu' and 'Mataji' and becomes a servant only to exploit them is a hypocrite. It is better to be an atheist than a religious cheat. — “hypocrite will pay the price not every day but one day”

🎙 Maharaj at 57:22 (auto-transcript): “But the person says, Prabhu, Maharaji, Mataji, Maharaji, Prabhuji, I'm a servant. When he's becoming a servant so that he can destroy you, very dangerous. One of my music heroes said, you are what? A hypocrite. And hypocrite will have to pay the price one day. Not every day,…”

Krishna removed this burden expertly: he gathered the burdensome in one place and finished it in eighteen days, away from the cities.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:45 (auto-transcript): “to expertly remove this burden expertly expertly christian carried all the the burden of the world to one place to remove them from the city and packed them in one place and for 18 days finish or expertly you're not expert very experts very experts in one place a custom…”

children.topic: Bowing to all that is Krishna's
children.note:
Brahma offers obeisances even to Krishna's gunja necklace and to the lowly arka plant, because he now sees everything connected with Krishna as worshipable.

🎙 Maharaj at 62:34 (auto-transcript): “obeisances to all why because the brahma see that everything brought including your ornament and even the lowly archa tree are object of my worship oh lord who can be merciful merciless who can grant me auspicious or trouble i offer my respectful obeisances namaste to you…”

Having gained realisation, Brahma shows respect to everything related to Krishna; in Vrindavan even a grain of sand is worshipable.

🎙 Maharaj at 63:41 (auto-transcript): “with a little Krishna so Brahma has gotten some realization from knowledge and he is he's showing that respect yes brindavan even the grain of sunny brindavan is worshipable worshipping so vision i check it what is that could i open obeisance is sarva sansaya hiritsarva…”

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura notes that Brahma, ashamed, calls himself a demon from Satyaloka who came to disturb Krishna and his friends. Maharaj calls this the humility that knowledge brings: devotees facilitate Krishna's enjoyment, demons disturb it.

🎙 Maharaj at 65:40 (auto-transcript): “to the edge to destroy blood krishna and his intimate friends and calves this is what knowledge does knowledge help to to brighten to make it very clear for us to understand so the brahma is sing so what i did is it's an offense i i i'm a demon i'm a raksasa from satya loka…”

We should look into our hearts every day and ask whether our activities please Krishna or disturb him. No one can do this for us; without it we remain far from the goal. — “we must check daily”

🎙 Maharaj at 67:05 (auto-transcript): “Krishna that's a devotee we have been mentioning so many times but is a science what is science is what is what am I my activities are my activities a blessing to krishna devotee or it is disturbing krishna demonic this is how to think this is how to check ourselves that is…”

Devotees always ask how to know they are advancing. Being able to see when one's activity does not please Krishna is one sign; thinking oneself the best person in the world is the opposite. — “that is a sign that we're not making advancement”

🎙 Maharaj at 68:45 (auto-transcript): “is a sign that we're making advancement the bodies are always acting how do I know I'm making advancement do it always says there's so many ways to know if we're making a point or not one of the ways is what we're discussing to check if I'm if my activity if I'm able to to…”

Many want to look into Krishna's dealings with his pure devotees without any qualification. Who are we, and whom are we trying to look into?

🎙 Maharaj at 70:08 (auto-transcript): “look at christian's activities without qualification how will you look at christian's activity without qualification what is the qualification for all to look into christian's activities christians dealing with his pure devotees what's our qualification first of all we look…”

A lightweight is never matched against a heavyweight; one punch would destroy him — it would not even be a fight. Approaching Krishna's intimate pastimes in our condition is just as destructive. — “it's not a fight it is just a child's play”

🎙 Maharaj at 70:43 (auto-transcript): “can a lightweight challenge a heavyweight boxer wrestler any any any chance for them lightweight and heavyweight it does not work like that heavyweight will challenge heavyweight lightweight will challenge lightweight amateurly amateur but here see what we are doing we are…”

When tender Krishna and Balarama faced Kamsa's wrestlers in Mathura, the people cried that the match was unfair. Here we amateurs challenge the heavyweight — worse than drinking poison.

🎙 Maharaj at 72:35 (auto-transcript): “notified a budget buses they did a day a busy busy when they came to matura that what they said how can this happen how can this happen look at this tent boy Christian power of their bodies like the lotus flower how can they fight with I own musical and channel this is…”

The gopis are beyond the three modes; Goloka is far above Vaikuntha. Having nothing in their minds but Krishna, they can sacrifice everything; we keep many others in our minds, so we cannot.

🎙 Maharaj at 74:36 (auto-transcript): “why they they don't have anything in their minds other than chrisa that is why they can sacrifice everything we have something else in our mind therefore we cannot sacrifice everything because have so many things in mind there are so many personalities in our mind not krishna…”
Brahma's admission teaches us: a mind that disturbs Krishna's enjoyment is demoniac, and as the Gita says, such people's hopes, knowledge and efforts are all baffled.

Questions and reflections on the whole series.

🎙 Maharaj at 78:00 (auto-transcript): “so today we'll be just proceeding to the reflections devotees would have or any questions that they would like to ask so dear devotees today we are directly proceeding to the question answer or comments or reflections that you have to share from”

The gopis forget everything for Krishna, yet the Gita asks us to be regulated in eating and sleeping. How does one move from regulation to spontaneity?

🎙 Question from the floor at 79:11 (auto-transcript): “today's session but from the previous session so we hear that the gopis are self-forgetful and also like in the previous sessions you mentioned even today you mentioned that when we have nothing but krishna in our mind and that is when we will be able to surrender to krishna…”

Forgetting to rise early, to attend class or to dress properly is the mode of ignorance, not spontaneous love. — “This is tamasic”

🎙 Maharaj at 80:10 (auto-transcript): “principles of what Krishna mentions in the Bhagavad Gita. When we have transcended ignorance, then we have transcended ignorance, forgetting to get up early to do job or to go to class or to forget to dress properly. This is tamasic, the mode of ignorance, not a spontaneous…”

The gopis ran with one earring and soap on their faces, yet arrived before Krishna perfectly dressed — Yogamaya arranged it, and kept their forms at home too. That cannot be compared with our forgetting to brush our teeth.

🎙 Maharaj at 81:43 (auto-transcript): “that that is what sugar goes to be describing no but this one sugar sugar because somebody described but when you look at look at them were there like that when they met krishna no don't say no so what happened well dressed yeah they were dressed who dressed them is it…”

children.topic: Let the fire of bhakti burn
children.note: Ignorance is destroyed by the fire of bhakti, according to how much we put ourselves into the process; Krishna responds to everyone as they approach him. So dress nicely, keep clean and wash your clothes.

How can we tell whether we are really analysing our faults or simply victimising ourselves?

🎙 Question from the floor at 86:03 (auto-transcript): “a bit nicely. All right, to see, keep up. Hare Krishna, dear Gurudev. This is my most humble, basically. Gurudev, could you explain, please, the difference between, or how can we recognize whether we are really analyzing our faults and shortcomings, or we are just…”

Lamenting that I'm useless and can't chant is ignorance and false ego. Our concern is only whether what I do is offerable to Krishna or causes anxiety, checked every day.

🎙 Maharaj at 86:44 (auto-transcript): “oh yeah i'm not a good devotee i'm so useless i can't chance to occur oh my sister is hanging i don't have this i don't have that i am not like this oh lord look at me i see ignorance i know humility i think ignorance false ego i know humility right i'm realizing is what we…”

children.topic: Q3 · Why remember God only in pain?
children.note:
Why do we cry out to the Lord in distress but forget gratitude in happiness?

🎙 Question from the floor at 88:45 (auto-transcript): “chat box from sushant prabhuji prabhuji is saying harry krishna maharaj please accept my humble and respectful obeisances unto your lotus feet why is it that we as conditioned souls have a natural tendency to cry out to and remember the lord more intensely during times of…”

In success we say 'I did it'; with a toothache we suddenly call for the doctor. — “we are not grateful”

🎙 Maharaj at 89:12 (auto-transcript): “prosperity because we lack gratitude gratitude we are not grateful because we are not grateful when something will happen i'm very smart i did it don't know me yes one point you're finished that is me but tomorrow when you have a tooth egg He will forget that we are a…”

Brahma does not plead 'I'm only a child'. He asks forgiveness and a chance to grow, ready to accept whatever punishment he needs — that is gratitude.

🎙 Maharaj at 90:10 (auto-transcript): “No, Brahma will not do like that because he knows that I'm not acting well. I should be punished for what I'm doing. So here, the Brahma is offering prayer. he didn't say christian please you know i'm a child now i'm a child don't punish me he didn't say like that i'm a child…”

children.topic: Q4 · Where do we come from?
children.note:
Some say souls come from the spiritual world, others that no one falls from there. Where do we really come from?

🎙 Question from the floor at 90:52 (auto-transcript): “i have this doubt and i need your help to clarify that there's other platform and there's this discussion was going on where we come from and it is said that others say that we are from the”

It is a controversial question neither side will ever settle. Prabhupada's one-sentence answer: perfect your life and go back; there you will understand.

🎙 Maharaj at 92:03 (auto-transcript): “please can you help me to understand that where do we really come from are you from what are them are wasting their time yes both of them because none of them will understand it none of them will understand it it's a controversial statement or issue so they will never…”

children.topic: First get out of the river
children.note:
A drowning man who demands to know how he fell in before accepting the rescuer's hand will die there. — “get out then you can ask”

🎙 Maharaj at 93:13 (auto-transcript): “example the analogy probably analogy very powerful if you are drowning yeah you are drawn in the river somebody come hey my friend hold it let me drag you how do i fall inside this whole person tell me how i fell here first then you can deliver me you die inside there get out…”

Maharaj tried from every direction and no one gave a satisfying answer; when he traced it himself to a point, he stopped and simply accepted what Prabhupada says.

🎙 Maharaj at 94:06 (auto-transcript): “i'm telling you my spirit because i have i have such all directions i've tried to say from all direction nobody has ever given me a satisfactory answer and when i trusted myself where i got it to i ended there i didn't continue because it would bring to us i'm telling from…”

children.topic: Q5 · How to beg? Dress for whom?
children.note:
How should we beg the spiritual master for mercy, and for whom do we dress well if we cannot see Krishna?

🎙 Question from the floor at 97:04 (auto-transcript): “thank you next question Hare Krishna Guru Maharaj Danvat Pranam my humble and respectful obeisance is on to you sorry people might say I am asking again I don't know I'm asking again or not but out of this class I am asking like you explained right now like we will say I…”

Read the meanings of beg, begging and beggar — then you will know how to beg.

🎙 Maharaj at 98:04 (auto-transcript): “please go to a dictionary open dictionary and look at the word begging, see the meaning look at what the meaning so you can read it then in dictionary begging beg beggar look at the three words there you can get it then you can so your question was how do we beg so please go…”

Nobody wants to see your dress; we want to see a pure soul. Just follow instructions: all understanding begins with hearing, one who has heard practises, and one who practises gets realisation. — “so you should hear attentively”

🎙 Maharaj at 99:40 (auto-transcript): “so you don't need to see christmas before you dress off the room just follow instructions you follow that's all by falling and you get the realization the presentation to you to see the same letter the beginning is hearing at the beginning of all sciences understanding begin…”

Maharaj thanks the team whose daily reflection exercises went to the heart, and blesses all who joined for the whole month: after these thirty days they cannot be who they were, and he prays for their transformation. — “you cannot be the same person again”

🎙 Maharaj at 103:11 (auto-transcript): “Before we start, I want to thank you for, before Madura starts, we want to thank you and like Mataji says, thank you for the wonderful, and with all the team, all of you who perfectly arranged this thing and all the problems which everybody benefited I observed that so many…”
