maps.title: Radha Sunya · Session 22 · Forgiveness Is Not Enough

nodeData.topic: Session 22 · Forgiveness Is Not Enough
nodeData.note: SB 4.30.48 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Through Daksha's offence to Lord Shiva Maharaj distinguishes ksama, being forgiven, from anugraha, winning the favour of the one offended: Shiva forgave Daksha, yet Daksha kept suffering because his pride never let him seek Shiva's mercy. The stolen-car analogy shows restitution, and Haridasa Thakura's three past offenders show how sincerely one must beg. The questions cover relationships turning dry, procrastinating over rectification, difficult children, the uniqueness of Vrindavan and parikrama, and counting percentages of blame. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Daksha, son of Brahma, offended Lord Shiva, the topmost Vaishnava, at his great sacrifice. Shiva did not take it as an offence and forgave him when Daksha wept and begged — yet the Lord does not easily forgive an offence to his devotee, and Daksha still suffered.

🎙 Maharaj at 07:25 (auto-transcript): “Daksha is offence of Lord Shiva. Darsha, the son of Lord Brahma, organized a great sacrificial ceremony. But in the process, he committed an offense. The offense was to the topmost Vaishnava, Lord Shiva. Lord Shiva did not take Darsha's offense seriously. And afterwards,…”

The verse tells of Daksha's later birth from the wife of the Pracetas. Maharaj explains he had to give up his body twice for disrespecting Shiva: no one can really offend Shiva, but it is very risky for us to try.

Brahma told Shiva that those who keep offending Vaishnavas are already condemned by their own acts. If devotees also become angry with them they will never get the chance to be delivered, so devotees forgive; after paying for their offences they may one day be delivered. — “They are already condemned.”

🎙 Maharaj at 11:34 (auto-transcript): “Lord Brahma told Lord Shiva, people who are Offensive and always offending Vashnavas, devotees, they are already condemned. Either one takes the offense or not takes the offense, they are already condemned for their offensive behavior activity towards the Vashnavas. They are…”

In his next birth Daksha offended Narada Muni, and Jiva Gosvami calls this a result of his earlier offence to Shiva. When we do not correct our consciousness after an offence, one leads to another — like small lies that need more lies until we believe them ourselves.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:13 (auto-transcript): “The continuing consequences. As a result of his offense on the Shiva, Daksha had to take birth again. This time in a Shatteria family, the Prachetas. In the next birth, Daksha also committed an offense at the lotus feet of Sri Narada movement. Slajiva Goswami commented that…”

Daksha apologised by etiquette but inside still thought: he is my son-in-law, a homeless beggar without proper clothes, and I am a great personality. Thinking in bodily terms, he never obtained Shiva's mercy and kept offending. — “So poor, so useless, such a shame to have Lord Shiva as his in-law.”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:56 (auto-transcript): “Daksha begged Lord Shiva for forgiveness, Lord Shiva did, but he did not obtain his mission because Daksha was still thinking. He's my son-in-law, after all. I am superior to him. He is inferior to me. I am a great personality. A Lord Shiva is just an ordinary person who…”

To be free of an offence to a great soul, one must please that very person through constant bhakti, beginning with chanting. Nama-kaumudi says such offences end either by suffering their calamities or by gaining the anugraha of the offended devotee — and Daksha never sought it; his ego deprived him. — “This Daksha did not do.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:42 (auto-transcript): “To be free, to be freed from offenses, to be free from offenses. We may question, if Lord Shiva forgave Daksa, then why is it that Daksa still had to suffer multiple reactions? We explained that Lord Shiva didn't take Daksa's behavior as an offense. And he forgave Daksa when…”

A thief who stole your car comes humbly to apologise and you forgive him: that is ksama. Anugraha is when he then works, raises money, buys the same kind of car and brings it back — restitution.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:03 (auto-transcript): “The stolen car analogy. Shema, forgiveness. Someone steals your car. Later you find out who it was. And the thief knows that you know. The thief comes to your house and very humbly apologizes. apologizes. I did it. I made a mistake. I wasn't in a proper state of mind, but I…”

Forgiving means I give up my anger. But tomorrow when I must take the children to school, the car is not there; I remember the thief and my mind counts my difficulties. Only replacing what was taken sets both free. — “The car is not there.”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:39 (auto-transcript): “Why? Because I may say I have forgiven you. The group will explain here. Yes, I have forgiven you. What have I done? In the act of forgiveness, one has given up anger or agitation concerning the theft. because the person has come to bed. So the anger is gone. And my mind is…”

Lord Shiva was never angry; he is completely sober and undisturbed, so he cannot really be offended. Daksha simply was not humble enough to fall at his feet and take their dust on his head with a good heart. — “Therefore, you cannot offend him.”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:23 (auto-transcript): “He only begged him for forgiveness. Because in the first place, Lord Shiva was not angry. He didn't take any offense because it's Mahade. Mahade. He is called what? Dira. Mahade, Lord Shiva, is Dira. He is completely sober. Undisturbed. He is undisturbed. Therefore, you…”

Maharaj has seen devotees who hurt someone, touch the person's feet mechanically, put the hand to their head and walk away thinking they are free. Such whimsical sorry, without realising the wrong, means we repeat it — this is Daksha's mentality. — “That is very dangerous.”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:13 (auto-transcript): “We should understand this principle very nicely. I've seen many devotees, once you hit somebody, we don't, yes, we know that, okay, I have hit somebody, maybe by mistake I have done that. But we don't have the patience to humbly talk to the person what they have. We just…”

children.topic: Stop and beg from the heart
children.note:
We should stop where we are, collect our mind, go down and beg forgiveness sincerely and take the dust of the person's feet. Then we are free of that offence.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:54 (auto-transcript): “We should stop where we are going. Put our mind together and beg the person for forgiveness. Go down and beg the person from the heart for forgiveness. Take the dust from his feet. Then we'll be free from that offense. We'll physically touch the person and put it in our hand…”

Indra did not just touch Krishna's feet and run: he begged forgiveness, then performed a bathing ceremony and named him Govinda. Brahma too begged to be born on the outskirts of Vraja where the Vrajavasis' foot-dust would fall on his head.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:16 (auto-transcript): “We shouldn't do that. When Indra offended Lord Vishnu, he didn't just touch the feet and run away. Indra begged for forgiveness and after with the help of Sri Ravi And after Krishna forgave him, Indra came to do a beating ceremony to Lord Krishna and gave him the name…”

Maharaj says Haridasa Thakura, the namacarya, is three personalities together, each of whom had offended, and so he took birth in a Muslim family.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:54 (auto-transcript): “He became Haridas Tekura. Haridas Tekura is three persons together, not one person, three persons together. And all of the three personalities, they came to have the Haridas Tekura as an offended people. people, offensive people, offensive. One is Lord Brahma, who offended…”

Lord Brahma, who offended Krishna; a boy cursed by his devotee father for bringing tulasi carelessly; and Prahlada Maharaja, who did not offer respect to the four Kumaras while absorbed in meditation. In Narayana's abode Prahlada was reminded, fell flat before the Kumaras and begged them — yet he too became part of Haridasa.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:21 (auto-transcript): “One is Lord Brahma, who offended Lord Krishna. Second is another person called Brahma. His father is a devotee, so he sent him to go and get a tulsi for his puja. And the boy went and brought a tulsi, but he didn't watch it properly. If I had cursed him, you are so low,…”

After the beating, Haridasa was thrown in the Ganga, revived and returned; his purity humbled the Kazi and Nawab, who begged his mercy. He told grieving devotees not to be angry: he had been punished for staying silent while the Lord was blasphemed. Whatever happens, we must never give up Krishna consciousness. — “That is why I was punished.”

🎙 Maharaj at 31:52 (auto-transcript): “You know, when Harada was being beaten, and after he was beaten in 22 marketplaces, he went into a coma, he was brought to the Kazi, he should be buried. The Kazi said, no, he should not be buried. Of course, he was influenced to do that, but he didn't know. He should be…”

children.topic: Reflection: why sorry is not enough
children.note:
A sin may be cleared without involving the one wronged, but after an offence there can still be a reaction even when forgiven; an extra step of rectification is needed. Devotees discuss apologies they never followed through, and how to tell favour from mere forgiveness.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:40 (auto-transcript): “Next, going into our true reflections, why forgiveness isn't always enough. Ten minutes. A sin can be more easily forgiven. It can be eradicated even without the reaction with the person to whom the sinful behavior was directed. However, after the committing of an offense,…”

Groups say sorry is often lip service said to keep serving together; making things right shows real remorse. A glued vase is never the same; we treat everyone as a pure devotee except our own roommate or spouse; true favour shows in a sweet, light relationship.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:28 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna Maharaj please accept my humble obeisances at your lotus feet basically three to four devotees have shared their reflections in our group. In case of asking forgiveness, many times devotees have asked forgiveness wherein they don't actually feel the feel that but…”

Responding, Maharaj says that when we beg sincerely from the heart we feel at once a relief, as if a burden is lifted from our head — no one needs to tell us. Without it, the heart stays heavy, fearful and angry. — “The breeze that will flow through your heart will come automatically”

🎙 Maharaj at 73:23 (auto-transcript): “yes so all the group did mention that how do we know if a person who was offended has we have obtained a message how do I know I have obtained a message of the person who was offended You see, when we genuinely, sincerely from the heart, beg somebody, I'm really sorry.…”

children.topic: Meet to help, not to criticise
children.note:
Good association has great power. Criticising differs from looking for ways to help: when a problem or person is discussed, someone should bring a practical solution. Devotees are servants of devotees and never want to hamper another's growth.

🎙 Maharaj at 74:49 (auto-transcript): “results the power of good association there is a positive side to this principle is so much power in good associations and so power acts on many levels to help the benefited person how much power There is a difference between criticizing and trying to find ways to improve or…”

For every offence to the holy name, Haridasa Thakura recommends associating with sadhus. Being free from malice and envy, their company gives us the strength to overcome our offensive nature.

🎙 Maharaj at 77:05 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, you will see that while we're discussing with Haridam Chen, Haddad Secura repeated every discussion, every discussion, every offense, Haddad Secura recommended one should go and associate with Saddam. We should be able to rectify ourselves on all the offenses we…”

Address problems openly, positively and honestly — not to judge but to help the person out. Vrajavasis of every kind brought their family troubles to Sanatana Gosvami, who answered out of compassion; this should be our principle. — “the idea is not to crucify the person.”

🎙 Maharaj at 78:15 (auto-transcript): “So here also, I'm going to give you some advice. I wish we would honor each other outside. When there is a problem, the person will address it openly, in a positive way, and with honesty. Everything is placed on the table. And it is difficult. The idea is not to judge the…”

Questions on unaware offenders, relationships that turn dry, and delaying rectification.

🎙 Maharaj at 81:37 (auto-transcript): “We'll open the floor for questions. We have so many questions. First, we have a question from Gaurudhya Anad Prabhuji. He has put his question in the chat. It goes like How should we act in a situation where someone has offended us in various ways and we perceive that they've…”

children.topic: Q1 · The offender doesn't see it
children.note:
Should we tell someone who doesn't realise he offended us? If there is a relationship, gently say what made you uncomfortable; if he apologises, explain and resolve it. If he is not interested, stop — forcing him only increases his problem.

🎙 Question from the floor at 81:47 (auto-transcript): “It goes like How should we act in a situation where someone has offended us in various ways and we perceive that they've made a mistake but the other person doesn't perceive or acknowledge their mistake or offense In order for the other person to realize their mistake should…”

Friends become distant and formal though I ask forgiveness — why?

🎙 Question from the floor at 86:02 (auto-transcript): “please accept my humble viscences unto the divine speak Srila Gurudev what I am sharing it is not with everybody my relationship but generally what happens i am sharing and that is really a problem for me initially their relationship are very sweet they are very helping to me…”

Biting a sweet mango you don't know about the seed until you reach it. Close relationships reveal hidden sides, as Maharaj saw in an elder brother's new marriage. If one always argues and claims to be right, the other quietly keeps distance. When someone feels offended, we are no longer right; we must correct it.

🎙 Maharaj at 87:17 (auto-transcript): “If you observe that, yeah. Okay, let me start this bit. You see, when you take a mango, if you take an Alfonso mango, you are biting it, it's very sweet. It's enjoyable. So in the beginning, you don't know that there is seed inside you. Because again, there is no seed. But…”

Every time I try to complete a rectification, illness or something else intervenes. Maharaj: it is not the illness — we are not ready and want to justify ourselves. Ask someone to help you beg; don't procrastinate, since no one is guaranteed health tomorrow.

🎙 Question from the floor at 94:49 (auto-transcript): “continue So in the scenario that we identified one situation where we have apologized but not fully rectified, we do have awareness of what is missing. but if one is finding difficulty of in fulfilling the act to do what is missing for that situation whatever it is but…”

What if children feel offended when corrected? Maharaj says a child who cannot be corrected may have come to settle a past-life debt; pray to Krishna. One who refuses all guidance and behaves like a robber is not acting as a child and should not stay in the house.

🎙 Question from the floor at 99:24 (auto-transcript): “next. Hare Krishna, dear Shira, good day. My question is that in our homes, we live with our children, our stepchildrens. And for instance, if I did something wrong and my Guru Maharaj chastised me I feel so relieved and happy and I feel so much love Maharaj sometimes in our…”

Questions on an unforgiving offended party, the holy dhamas and parikrama, cow service, and dividing blame.

🎙 Maharaj at 104:11 (auto-transcript): “Guru Maharaj, we've just seen that when somebody has offended, then he finds many excuses not to go ask for forgiveness. He procrastinates the exercise. But what about the one who has been offended? He is not ready to receive the person who has offended him. So in that…”

children.topic: Q5 · The offended won't receive me
children.note:
Send a friend of his to beg on your behalf; if that fails, pray to the deities. Don't complain that he kicked you out — feel your terrible position. If every attempt with a senior makes it worse, improve your own sadhana and character first; your change will affect him.

🎙 Question from the floor at 104:11 (auto-transcript): “Guru Maharaj, we've just seen that when somebody has offended, then he finds many excuses not to go ask for forgiveness. He procrastinates the exercise. But what about the one who has been offended? He is not ready to receive the person who has offended him. So in that…”

children.topic: Q6 · Hiding mistakes; dhama and parikrama
children.note:
If you discover an offence, run back and apologise, or pray to the deities if you don't know the person. All the Lord's abodes are wonderful and not to be belittled.

🎙 Question from the floor at 108:10 (auto-transcript): “Krishna Shreela Gurita, Mahatai Ji has two questions. First question says that by virtue of some bad habits, she has committed some mistake. And she's just thinking not to ask for forgiveness so that it remains in the forgotten state and eventually it wipes off. And the…”

Rupa Gosvami calls Krishna complete in Dvaraka, more complete in Mathura and most complete in Vrindavan; Sanatana Gosvami says Goloka is kept far beyond Vaikuntha. Narayana would send a servant to tend cows, but Krishna goes himself and even tells Yasoda he will disobey her to go. Maharaj keeps only Vrindavan, Mayapur and Jagannatha Puri in his mind.

🎙 Maharaj at 110:17 (auto-transcript): “Still, still, Sr. Rupa Goswami has explained that Krishna in Dwaraka is Purna, it's complete. But we know that Krishna in Dwaraka is Krishna with four hands. It means Narayan. Narayan now will be Baikunta. So it is mentioned it is complete. Because it is Abodho Krishna, it is…”

Parikrama is not walking for lack of a car. Each step purifies; the place, the Lord's activities and the pure devotees who speak of them are connected, and the dhama is revealed only by hearing from pure devotees there. — “Every step it is for purification.”

🎙 Maharaj at 118:13 (auto-transcript): “Parikrama, Parikrama, it's not that I don't have money to pay for a car or for a truck. That is not Parikama. Parikama means heavy activity, heavy step. Every step it is for purification. So we do Parikama to give us purification, to take the blessing from the place Krishna…”

You cannot log in to Krishna-prema; it comes only from a person who has it, like Srinivasa Acharya. Maharaj adds that when Srinivasa was left sleeping outside under a tree, Mahaprabhu came in a dream to Saci-devi to complain on his behalf. — “You can only get it from a person.”

🎙 Maharaj at 120:13 (auto-transcript): “Prima online Christian Prima online log into Christian Prima and you get it online. You'll never get it there. You'll never get it. You can only get it from a person. Whose person? Krishna Premi Bhatta. Because they have got him. We're talking about Nebatacharya. He came to…”

children.topic: Q7 · Why devotees ignore the cows
children.note:
Cow herding is Krishna's own occupation; if we loved him we would want to do what he likes. Lack of interest shows we are not really aiming for his abode — Srila Prabhupada said many devotees end up in heaven, and Maharaj agrees.

🎙 Question from the floor at 123:37 (auto-transcript): “Krishna Maharaj. So one question is, if cow hoarding is so pleasing to Krishna, cows are so pleasing to Krishna, so when we are doing cow protection, not even pay, I mean, We don't even get a slightest encouragement, not even bother to visit cows or do any service. I mean,…”

The other person was more at fault, yet it still haunts me. Maharaj: calculating percentages is a wrong foundation — both did wrong. The heart is unclean because we have not rectified it; if you love yourself, go and do it. He closes asking prayers for a devotee recovering after a serious car accident who joined from hospital.

🎙 Question from the floor at 125:46 (auto-transcript): “first of all thank you for the classes whenever I have heard your classes I have realized flaws and things in me and where I need rectification so thank you for everything so my question is like if we have if two people are involved in a mistake 40 percent is my mistake 60…”

maps.title: Radha Sunya · Session 23 · Devotion and Extreme Forbearance

nodeData.topic: Session 23 · Devotion and Extreme Forbearance
nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj tells how King Kulottunga, an offensive Shaiva, plotted to kill Ramanujacharya, and how the disciples Kuresa and Mahapurna went in his place, were tortured and blinded, and still prayed for the king. Their selfless service melted Ramanuja's heart; Kuresa begged mercy even for his tormentors and regained his sight as his guru's property. Maharaj separates humility from foolishness and forbearance from enabling abuse, and in the questions explains that practice prepares us for trials, that the holy name is where surrender begins, and that tests come according to our level. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
King Kulottunga, ruling from Kanchipuram over the land of Sri Rangam, grew envious of Ramanujacharya. As a Shaiva with a narrow, ritualistic vision, he wanted Ramanuja and his followers converted to Shiva worship, and planned to kill him whether he won or lost a debate with the court panditas.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:24 (auto-transcript): “Adibu, Samanganuja Acharya and King Kulutunga. There was a great Acharya in the voice of our lineage, Ramanuja Acharya, who was an external, who was an eternal associative Krishna, and extremely potent and powerful. King Kulutunga I, whose capital was in Kanchipuram, and…”

Maharaj recalls South Indian temples where Shiva is on the altar and Vishnu is put behind. Worshipping Shiva alone is already an offence; pushing Vishnu aside shows how offenders lose the intelligence to see right and wrong, as Krishna describes the demoniac in the Gita. — “That is part of the danger of being offensive.”

A fool is one thing; a foolish rascal establishes his foolishness as supreme and forces everyone to follow it — as the king tried to do.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:25 (auto-transcript): “One thing is to be a fool. Another thing is to be a foolish rascal. A foolish rascal will establish, not only being a fool, a foolish rascal means what? He's not only a fool, but he will establish his foolishness or her foolishness as the supreme. And he wants to force…”

Lord Shiva and Parvati worship Lord Sankarshana; the serpent on Shiva's neck is Sankarshana. Those who worship Shiva's own master are the ones Kulottunga wanted to make Shiva worshippers.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:59 (auto-transcript): “Who is the worshipable deity of Lord Shiva? Whom does Lord Shiva worship? Lord Shiva's deity is Lord Sankarshan. Shiva and Parvati worship Sankarshan. A snake on Lord Shiva's neck, that is Sankarshan. Not just a snake, it's Sankarshan, Lord Sankarshan. Who is Lord Bhadara?…”

children.topic: Disciples go in the guru's place
children.note:
Mahapurna, who stood in the position of Ramanuja's guru yet served him like a disciple, and Kuresa, his initiated disciple, knew the king's duplicity. They told Ramanuja not to go; Kuresa dressed as his master and the two went to the court themselves.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:58 (auto-transcript): “This is a teaching, a very important teaching. The Mahanodacharya had two disciples, Mahapurna, who was actually the disciple of Ramun Acharya and in the position of Ramun Acharya's guru who served Ramun Acharya sincerely as though he were a disciple. And Kureshi who was the…”

The panditas argued for Shiva's supremacy and the two Vaishnavas repeatedly established Vishnu's. The enraged king had them imprisoned, tortured and their eyes put out — an order Maharaj compares to Duryodhana's cruelty.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:28 (auto-transcript): “The panditas gave their argument in favor of Lord Shiva's supremacy. And Kureish and Mahapurna gave argument showing Lord Vishnu's undeniable supremacy. The two Vaisalas were repeatedly successful in the debate. The king flew into a rage, imprisoned and tortured them, and…”

This is dedication: a selfless disciple who surrenders his life to the spiritual master is the one empowered by the guru's mercy.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:36 (auto-transcript): “yes This is the point where a disciple is demonstrating his dedication. When we say dedication, we are talking about dedication. A disciple should be selfless and dedicated. A soul surrenders the soul to the spiritual master. These are the devotees who exemplify this. the…”

Beaten and blinded, Kuresa thanked the king for letting him serve his guru this way and prayed that Narayana bless him. He saw only his spiritual master, not the king — even the hard-hearted court was awestruck. — “He is not angry with this demonic king.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:37 (auto-transcript): “Just look at the mentality. He is not angry with this demonic king. He is praying for him. Even the hard-hearted king and his men were awestruck. Yes. Yes. This is a disciple, first-class disciple. This is a first-class disciple. They have been beaten totally the same way.…”

By contrast, we serve mechanically, want the whole world to know about it, and complain that the guru doesn't like us. Maharaj asks what the quality of our service really is. — “We render very mechanical service.”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:15 (auto-transcript): “We render very mechanical service. I want the whole world to know about it. Guru doesn't like me. Quresh is thinking like this. This is the mentality of Quresh. is that the mentality what is the quality of our service that we want the whole world to know about and you will…”

The elderly Mahapurna, mortally wounded, died in Kuresa's arms, accepting the pain as service. There was nothing to lament: his mind was fixed on his guru and he longed to meet him. He did not think, as we do, 'look what I lost because I became a devotee'.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:15 (auto-transcript): “Mahapurna was quite elderly and was mortally wounded by the torture. But he died gracefully in Koresh arms, accepting the suffering as his service to Samaranoja Acharya. He spoke his final words to Koresh. You must go alone to Sri Lanka. for I can tell that the time has come…”

Maharaj tells of a devotee jailed and condemned by a king after initiation. His father sent a powerful tantric through a tunnel with a mantra to free him, but the devotee refused: his guru had given him Krishna's mantra, and his only concern was his guru's lotus feet, in prison or out. — “My only concern is the Lord's feet of my spiritual master.”

🎙 Maharaj at 37:16 (auto-transcript): “When a devotee's name took initiation from the two chiefs, the two chiefs, who surrendered and became a devotee, and the king arrested him after he became a devotee. I just forgot the name. when he was arrested and put in jail and the king wanted to kill him the king already…”

Hearing what his disciples had suffered, Ramanujacharya was overwhelmed with compassion — the quality of one who is selfless and cannot bear another's pain.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:04 (auto-transcript): “Dhammanuja's compassionate plan. When Dhammanuja Acharya heard what had happened to Krish and Mahapuru, he was overwhelmed with compassion. Yes, compassion. He was overwhelmed with compassion. Compassion is one who is completely selfless and cannot tolerate the pain of…”

Citing Srila Prabhupada on Gita 4.34, Maharaj says a bona fide guru is soft-hearted: seeing selfless service, his heart melts and blessings go to that disciple without being asked. — “The blessing comes automatically.”

children.topic: Your eyes are your guru's property
children.note:
Ramanuja sent Kuresa to worship the powerful deity Varadaraja in Kanchipuram. When the deity offered a boon Kuresa asked for nothing; Ramanuja sent him back with an order: say you lost two of your guru's properties and want them back for his service. A surrendered disciple belongs completely to his guru. — “It is a guru's property.”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:33 (auto-transcript): “Kuresh, for the first time, a deity came and asked, what can I do to you? He said, ah, there's nothing. I'm just happy to sue. I'm just happy. So a deity went back. And Kuresh came back to meet the Manuja chariot. Manuja chariot said, what happened? The deity did not come to…”

The power of devotion, love and extreme forbearance is greater than any deviation. Devotees ask whether they have ever seen suffering as a chance to serve the guru, what Kuresa teaches about staying Krishna conscious in trials, and how healthy forbearance differs from enabling abuse.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:42 (auto-transcript): “Going internal through the lectures. The interior reality of love. Ten minutes. This story is very powerful. It teaches that the power of devotion, love, and extreme forbearance is greater than any deviation, even to the point of humbly accepting and I suffered. Oh, personal…”

Maharaj doubts we do: we complain that people mistreat us or that the guru only listens to certain devotees — as if the guru were useless and could decide nothing.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:21 (auto-transcript): “I doubt. Otherwise, we will not be complaining. This, that, they don't like me. They do me like this. They mistreated me. They pushed me away. All kinds of nonsense we talk. or guru doesn't listen to me only listen to this only this people guru cannot listen to me because of…”

Groups admit they usually ask how to get rid of suffering, not how to serve through it. Healthy forbearance leaves service and consciousness intact and brings us closer to guru and Krishna; abuse damages them. One recalls Bhakti Tirtha Swami in a Russian prison saying he is never alone, being always with his spiritual master.

🎙 Maharaj at 61:15 (auto-transcript): “The first question I start with my own reflection first it comes up that no, I have never seen this until this point, I think it was also one more devotee that until this point we haven't seen that suffering should be considered as an opportunity to serve our spiritual master…”

Since many groups could not draw the line, Maharaj explains: humility and forbearance are spiritual qualities, completely different from foolishness or accepting abuse.

🎙 Maharaj at 78:29 (auto-transcript): “There is a great difference between humility and foolishness. And also forbearance and abuse. and they are a completely different thing. Humility is a spiritual quality. It is 100% different from being foolish. So forbearance is a wonderful quality, not a mundane quality.…”

Abuse is someone using me for their own gratification. Kuresa and Mahapurna were caught in a plot they could not escape. Offering your eyes to someone who wants to harm you when you are free to leave is not tolerance. — “That is foolishness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 79:53 (auto-transcript): “An abuse is different. An abuse is something that someone is using me for his or her gratification. That is a different thing. But this is a plot by somebody trying to attack. So they went to face the debates. So this is a plan. And abuse, if I'm misusing someone for my…”

If someone harasses you and you have a chance to escape, you should leave rather than stand there to prove something.

🎙 Maharaj at 83:31 (auto-transcript): “But if I foolishly someone want to plug up my eye and I have a chance and someone harassing want to plug, if you have a chance to run away, you should run away, leave the cliff. To stand, prove that yes. What do you think we must do for a couple of”

Before asking anything for himself, Kuresa begged the Lord to deliver the man who had incited the king, and then the king himself. He held no grudge, like Haridasa Thakura, and the Lord, responding to his pure devotee, liberated both — as Nityananda delivered Jagai and Madhai though they wounded him.

🎙 Maharaj at 81:37 (auto-transcript): “Okay. The ultimate forgiveness. He asked that the person named Chetugra, who had agitated King Kulutunga against him and catered the situation by which he was blinded and tortured, be delivered from material existence and received the Lord's mercy. The Lord agreed, but…”

Moved, Ramanuja had Kuresa continue his service and ask for his sight on his master's behalf; when the deity next spoke, Kuresa asked to recover two lost possessions of his master, and his sight was restored.

🎙 Maharaj at 84:53 (auto-transcript): “When Ramanuja heard how the deity had reciprocated and how Krishna, instead of asking something for himself, had asked for misi for those who had been in great offence, he was overwhelmed. Ramanuja requested Kureish to continue with his puja or service. He sent a message to…”

Krishna consciousness means being conscious of Krishna in every circumstance, not only when things are easy. For an advanced devotee the worst outcome is going back to the spiritual world — like Bhishma on his bed of arrows with Krishna and the Pandavas before him. — “That's what will happen to a devotee, to go back to Godhead.”

🎙 Maharaj at 87:45 (auto-transcript): “The worst thing that can happen to advanced devotees who are facing Christian consciousness is that they will go back to the spiritual world. So we see General Bhishma Devi lying on the bed of Arashia, and all, and the five Pandavas including the Krishna is also here too,…”

Questions on being fixed in Krishna consciousness, facing suffering, the guru as the way to the Lord, and devotees' departures.

🎙 Maharaj at 90:52 (auto-transcript): “so it's question time if you have some reflections as well can share them at this time so we have a few hands raised we will start with uh shweta mataji you can kindly unmute yourself and let me share your question or realization very well shweta mataji we can see you but we…”

What does fixed in Krishna consciousness mean — is it possible all the time? Maharaj has SB 10.14.8 shown: one who patiently accepts his karma, awaits the Lord's mercy and offers obeisances with heart, words and body has a rightful claim to liberation, like an heir who simply stays alive. He asks her to read it carefully.

How can we stay Krishna conscious when suffering burns? Only by having practised well beforehand; otherwise we are like the student who didn't listen in class, staring at the ceiling and sweating until time is up. — “we will be able to handle the situation nicely”

🎙 Question from the floor at 96:42 (auto-transcript): “So when that suffering situation comes, so the vibration itself, we could realize that it is so much burning sensation. So how to stay in that moment in such situation to be in Krishna consciousness, transcendental vibration. So sometimes it's like... Continue to practice if…”

How do we develop Kuresa's vision? Through sadhana-bhakti. Kuresa and Mahapurna were not neophytes; they had practised to that first-class level. Maharaj felt deep appreciation for Ramanuja's sacrifice when he visited Melkote; we hear these stories to raise our practice.

🎙 Question from the floor at 99:37 (auto-transcript): “please accept my humble businesses um we tend to go to supreme lord first during any situations or in reversals as well thinking i mean he's and also like you know we think all of our senses are managed by him rishi kesha is lord's property this body is given by us as a gift…”

children.topic: Q4 · Refusing treatment at the end
children.note:
How do we understand senior devotees who declined treatment or travelled knowing they would not return? Maharaj says they knew their time had come and consciously left rather than waste time and money; it is we who lament.

🎙 Question from the floor at 104:17 (auto-transcript): “we just learned that suffering this is also an aspect of using it to the service of the spiritual master so referring to the life of Kandamakannan Maharaj when he was diagnosed that he has cancer then he refused to take any treatment he was just taking water and finally he…”

Kuresa's situation was inevitable — the king had planned everything. If there is no alternative, accept it as Krishna's arrangement; if treatment keeps failing, understand what Krishna wants. A devotee does not waste his last days on dangerous, futile efforts.

🎙 Question from the floor at 107:17 (auto-transcript): “so Gurudev my question is from forbearance and abuse that how you mentioned the distinction between foolishness and humility and how you also mentioned that we should not foolishly tolerate someone trying to harm us by plucking our eyes out So my question is in this regard…”

Further questions on cleanliness, pleasing Radharani, the first step to surrender, a controversial offering, and small sufferings.

🎙 Maharaj at 111:44 (auto-transcript): “Shilagurdev Mattia Ji is saying that first of all she would like for forgiveness because the question is not exactly related from today's class but she wishes to know that when like she is engaged in her household activities like keeping her house very clean the question…”

Being clean is never an offence, but cleaning the house without cleaning the heart by chanting is useless. Maharaj describes encouraging devotees during a cleaning service; Bhaktivinoda Thakura says outer refinement with a heart full of garbage is not correct.

🎙 Question from the floor at 111:44 (auto-transcript): “Shilagurdev Mattia Ji is saying that first of all she would like for forgiveness because the question is not exactly related from today's class but she wishes to know that when like she is engaged in her household activities like keeping her house very clean the question…”

Radharani is pleased when Krishna is served nicely, and Krishna cannot be served without serving his devotees. Serve devotees and chant Hare Krishna, and Radha and Krishna are pleased.

🎙 Question from the floor at 115:28 (auto-transcript): “kamalakshi mataji hara krishna gurudev gurudev as you told in one class that if anyone does service of srimati radharani and please her then all the offenses he did krishna takes on his own and vanquishes all offenses. So, Gurudev, please tell us how we can serve and please…”

From the name come the form, qualities and pastimes; the name reveals everything. Put effort into chanting, especially in the association of devotees. — “everything starts from the holy name”

🎙 Question from the floor at 117:01 (auto-transcript): “we have Vaishali Mataji who asked Hare Krishna, Maharaji, Danvat Pranam. Maharaji, what is the very first thing we'll have to develop in us to have this kind of surrender and devotion and love to our guru and teachers? Kindly guide us, Maharaji, Hare Krishna. The kind of…”

children.topic: Q9 · Human hair for the deity?
children.note:
Asked about a video of a devotee's hair being cut and packaged for deity use, Maharaj calls it an abomination he has never heard of in Vaishnava history; a devotee adds that Hari-bhakti-vilasa lists human hair as unofferable. Better to give our heart.

🎙 Question from the floor at 119:46 (auto-transcript): “thank you forgive me for for for this question is not related to the class but i really want to ask him half clarification there's video circulated where a devotee grow his hair and they cut this hair and this hair was packaged that they are going to use for Krishna and there…”

Such extraordinary tests are rare. Krishna gives taste and tests according to our level, and uses more advanced devotees to demonstrate such lessons because they can stand the test.

🎙 Question from the floor at 126:07 (auto-transcript): “Yes, Jaren Russell? Yes, Muratel. Regarding today's lecture, it seems like there is a higher principle when we surrender to the spiritual master and we do something extraordinary. Now, nowadays, that situation for most of us might be difficult to attain where our lives will…”

nodeData.topic: Session 24 · Krishna Conscious on Life's Battlefield
nodeData.note: BG 2.15 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Taking up devotional service is declaring war on Maya, and our Kurukshetra is our own consciousness. Krishna is present, but as with Arjuna we must fight: the austerity we spent acquiring bad habits must now be spent removing them, and the devotee who stays steady in happiness and distress is dear to Krishna and fit for liberation. In the questions Maharaj speaks on tolerance, honouring prasadam mindfully, forgiveness, Bhishma-pancaka fasting, and transforming lust back into love. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: We have declared war on Maya
children.note:
Being tested is part of devotion. When we take up devotional service we declare war on Maya; Arjuna represents everyone trying to take shelter of Krishna, and the Gita is not ancient history or a novel but Krishna speaking to us.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:43 (auto-transcript): “The Bhargita is our story. It is a part of the process of devotion. and from time to time, everyone must be tested in various ways. When we check to a devotional service, we are declaring for a gay smile. We are on a battlefield, engaged in our own battle of crucifixion. We…”

children.topic: The Gita is speaking to me
children.note:
Srila Prabhupada opened a talk to a Rotary Club in Chandigarh by saying they had gathered to hear what Krishna wants to tell them. Our approach to the Gita should be to hear what Krishna is telling me, not someone else. — “but what Krishna is telling me.”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:35 (auto-transcript): “So the Papa was in Chandigarh to address the Rotary Club members. So Papa said, ladies and gentlemen, you are welcome to this evening discussion on Bhagavad Gita. All of us have gathered here to hear what Krishna wants to tell us. This is the approach. What Krishna wants to…”

Arjuna was never truly bewildered; Krishna put him in that position to speak the Gita for us. Standing between the armies, Arjuna understood everything because he was Krishna's friend and devotee, while Duryodhana understood nothing. Likewise the Gita existed long before, but only Srila Prabhupada's, coming from a devotee and friend of Krishna, had the potency to reveal Krishna to the world.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:45 (auto-transcript): “So we should understand that Arjuna is not a conditioned soul. When you look carefully in Bhagavad Gita, Krishna had already declared Arjuna to be a good case. It is one who has conquered illusion, one who is not bewildered. Arjuna had to undergo bewilderment and serious…”

Our Kurukshetra is not in Haryana but in our own consciousness, and the opponent is Maya. We are not fighting a harmless child but a formidable servant of Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:52 (auto-transcript): “So we are on the battlefield. In another book, Gurudev explains, our battlefield is not physically on the battlefield in Khrushchev in Haryana, India. Our battlefield is our own consciousness. That's our consciousness. And the target is what? The target is Maya. Gurudev said…”

Krishna calls his external energy divine and very difficult to overcome; we, conditioned souls, are not called divine. We cannot defeat a power thousands of times stronger — only by surrendering to Krishna is it made easy.

children.topic: Krishna is present, but we fight
children.note:
Krishna did not tell Arjuna to go and meditate while he destroyed the soldiers with his disc. He explained the whole philosophy and then told Arjuna to do his duty; he wants his devotees to earn the credit of staying devoted through difficulty.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:23 (auto-transcript): “Next. Krishna is present, but we must fight. We will also have to undergo challenges and deal with all kinds of choices. But Krishna is always there for us too. Krishna did not tell Arjuna. We have been together since time immemorial. So you just sit back and watch me deal…”

Krishna did not put these destructive narratives in our consciousness; we worked tirelessly, with sleepless nights, to acquire them. Consciousness is covered, not diluted, and it is our duty to uncover it. — “We have to do our duty.”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:36 (auto-transcript): “Yes, we have to deal with all the narratives we have accumulated in our consciousness. Because it is not Krishna who put all those narratives. We work tirelessly, having sleepless nights, performing all kinds of austerity to acquire all these destructive narratives.…”

Sense gratification itself takes great effort — people work day and night, even perform austerities for power, to rob or cheat. The same seriousness is needed to get free, through Bhishma-pancaka, Ekadasi and all the vratas.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:07 (auto-transcript): “We should know why posterity is necessary. Why is posterity necessary? We use posterity to accumulate all the sinful things that have covered our pure consciousness. Is it not true that we make a lot of sacrifice, a lot of austerity to commit all the sinful activities? Is it…”

In the twelfth chapter of the Gita Krishna says devotees who are unaffected by happiness and distress are most dear to him — not those who stay focused only while given opulence, fame and comfort. Their austerity has removed the dualities.

The verse names the steady person equal in happiness and distress as eligible for liberation. Maharaj stresses that Krishna does not say the joyful or the distressed qualify — both are dualities. The purport adds Mahaprabhu taking sannyasa at 24, leaving wife and mother for the higher cause. — “Eligibility for liberation is completely outside duality.”

children.topic: In the world, not of it
children.note:
Krishna will arrange many experiences. Even in a materialistic environment we should not give in to duality because others do. A person of character does the right thing whether seen or not.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:54 (auto-transcript): “Krishna will arrange many experiences for us. He has already arranged. In the midst of duality and strife, we should not become of the world. Even though we may have to participate in worldly things or be situated in a materialistic environment, we should not give in to a…”

If someone kindly gives a hungry person food, he does not then feed him with his own hand. Glorifying the giver as saviour of the fallen is fine, but we must eat until satisfied — the guru supplies strength, but does not fight our battle for us. — “We should now use our hands to eat the food.”

🎙 Maharaj at 48:53 (auto-transcript): “If we are hungry, helpless, if we are fortunate to have some provide us with food, it is not the person who gave us food that he or she should come and use his hand to feed us. We should now use our hands to eat the food. Yes, that is our duty. They have cooked.”

children.topic: The plane is given — fly it
children.note:
Srila Prabhupada said in a lecture that the airplane has been built and fuelled; now we have to fly it. Every facility is given — now sit and chant attentively, hear the glories of Krishna and his devotees, and plan our service.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:26 (auto-transcript): “satisfied and i don't need to eat anymore that is my duty yes so the proper give give one lecture And he was saying that all of us who are in our airplane, we have to fly it. That means that the airplane has been given to us, where everything it is made is fueled, now we have…”

Distractions are necessary to check the quality of our focus and how ready we are. They are not mistakes; they come by Krishna's arrangement. — “nothing can come without the permission of Krishna”

🎙 Maharaj at 51:44 (auto-transcript): “There will be a lot of distractions. Those distractions are necessary to check what is our focus in Christian consciousness, to check the quality of our focus in Christian consciousness, to check how much we are ready in Christian consciousness. That is why other distractions…”

Devotees ask where they find it hardest to stay spiritually focused, how to see Krishna's presence in their worst circumstances, and how to balance detachment with necessary worldly work.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:41 (auto-transcript): “going internal through reflections. Your personal culture, 10 minutes. We are on a battlefield engaged in our own battle of culture, personal reflection. In what situation do I find it hardest to remain spiritually focused? Two, how can I see Krishna's presence even in my…”

Groups name work pressure, illness, anger, lusty thoughts and poor morning sadhana; small subtle anarthas are harder than big crises. Balance comes from following guru, sadhu and sastra, completing sadhana first, and doing one's duties fully as an offering — not neglecting family while managing a temple.

🎙 Maharaj at 69:34 (auto-transcript): “we will request the group representative to please raise your hands and then we'll take them we'll hear one by one I don't see any other hand up so probably I can go first for as a representative for my group Srila Gurudev so in the in the discussion when we talked about what…”
SB 10.14.8 is shown again: one who patiently bears his past reactions while waiting for the Lord's mercy and bowing with heart, words and body has a rightful claim to liberation.

Those who give in are like students who cheat or don't study: they fail and lose what they could have learned. We must not join a culture of cheating, deviation and aparadha just because it is easy or common; the universe runs on laws.

🎙 Maharaj at 86:10 (auto-transcript): “Those who give in are like the students in school who cheat or don't study. Later, such people fail, but they have cheated themselves because they miss out on the opportunity to learn something which you will have been of use. They cheat themselves. We must be careful not to…”

children.topic: Results are not ours to decide
children.note:
We are free to act, but higher authorities decide the result. A devotee who deliberately misbehaved asked Maharaj to just forgive him without consequence — scripture does not allow that. Bribing an examiner may pass an exam, but when we must perform, we have cheated only ourselves. — “The high authorities, they decide.”

🎙 Maharaj at 87:19 (auto-transcript): “that is shown. Karma driver, let's do it now. We have the right to do the activity. That freedom we have, but what it is done, we don't have the right to get over the result. The high authorities will decide. The high authorities, they decide. Not we. Like for example, the…”

children.topic: A claim that has been paid for
children.note:
The kingdom of God becomes a rightful claim because we have paid the price by doing our part well — as one who has done his business well enjoys its profit.

🎙 Maharaj at 89:54 (auto-transcript): “Let us do the right thing. by doing the right thing when it is said here the kingdom of God becomes one's rightful claim it is the rightful because we have paid the price if we don't pay the price we cannot claim it is a rightful claim the rightful claim because we have done…”

Each morning, pray aloud that today's difficulties may be reactions or tests, asking not for their removal but for strength to stay conscious of Krishna, fighting like Arjuna with Krishna beside us. Each evening, check honestly whether we remembered him.

🎙 Maharaj at 91:14 (auto-transcript): “until your 30 day notebook for today's focus but refute consciousness every morning before facing your day pray this out loud Manipaya Krishna today I face difficulties some are reactions to my past some are tests you have given me I don't know which is which but I am not…”

Questions held over from the previous day on tolerance, prasadam, forgiveness and deviated devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 93:36 (auto-transcript): “we will now open the floor for questions Srila Gurudev, there are certain questions pending from yesterday's session is it okay if you take them first Srila Gurudev yes so the first question is from his grace Vishnumurthy Sevak Prabhuji he wants to know like how to consider…”

How to tolerate while serving, and how to see cooking and honouring prasadam as something great?

🎙 Question from the floor at 93:52 (auto-transcript): “his grace Vishnumurthy Sevak Prabhuji he wants to know like how to consider cooking, serving or honoring prashadam to be something very great. As Srila Gurudev you mentioned in one of the past times about Srinivas Acharya where he distributed prashadam to 10 brahmanas. And he…”

A moment of tolerance can save a hundred years in jail. We cannot call summer when we dislike winter; intolerance is passion, full of anxiety, while tolerance comes from knowledge, in goodness. — “If we don't tolerate, we just suffer.”

🎙 Maharaj at 94:37 (auto-transcript): “To tolerate you have to learn to understand what is tolerance what is the benefit What is the benefit of tolerance? Why should I tolerate? Why? Why should I tolerate? For what purpose? Because we know that. We have spoken about this so many times. Simple. If we don't…”

Who would go out for book distribution or preaching without prasadam? Mahaprabhu said even Brahma and Shiva seek mahaprasada, which gives love of God. Fasting at his departure, Haridasa Thakura still bowed to the prasadam brought to him. — “Prasadam is spiritual food.”

🎙 Maharaj at 98:52 (auto-transcript): “So, cooking, we need food to give us the strength to do our sadhana, to do whatever. So, it's one thing that cooking is useless. book distribution is the best yes brahmana brahmana I'm going to preach to the professors I'm going to preach to the university I'm going to meet…”

Stepping on or over prasadam and talking over it are offences; Maharaj avoids meals where senior devotees hold discussions. Mindfulness means remembering everyone behind the plate — whoever paid, shopped, cooked, served and offered it, the guru and Krishna. Some temples once had a reader during meals.

🎙 Maharaj at 102:02 (auto-transcript): “to avoid offenses for prasadam. Otherwise, we'll get a good problem. To step on prasadam is an offense. To step over prasadam is offense. To talk on prasadam is also an offense. All that disrespect. And when we have the heavy consequences. So many devotees, when they're…”

Forgiveness is given when someone begs for it, and we forgive because we need forgiveness too. With a serious crime we remove it from our mind but take care not to expose ourselves to such people again — and Krishna will still act. — “But Krishna will not forgive.”

🎙 Question from the floor at 105:06 (auto-transcript): “We have a question from Raksha Bhatt Mataji. It is related to the previous sessions where we discussed about forgiveness. She wants to know, Gurudev, if someone has committed heinous crime and not feeling bad or repenting, so in this case, is forgiveness a right choice?…”

children.topic: Q3 · A devotee joins another group
children.note:
If a long-practising devotee goes to another sampradaya, talk to him if you can; if not, pray for his success.

🎙 Question from the floor at 107:20 (auto-transcript): “Next, we have Gitanjali Mataji. She has a question. Wants to know if a long practicing devotee gets deviated for some other Sampradaya, let's say Gaudi Amat, what can be done to get him back? You can talk to the person, if you can. If you can, then you talk to the person. If…”

You cannot truly beg forgiveness while feeling you did nothing wrong. Only when you see your fault, whether before a senior or a junior, can you sincerely apologise — and it is for your own benefit.

🎙 Question from the floor at 108:15 (auto-transcript): “One last question from yesterday is from Vaishali Mataji. She wants to know if a person is a non-devotee but belongs to a family and is elder and is invading our personal space which seems wrong to us but right to them how can we seek forgiveness and even if I don't feel it…”

Questions on the Bhishma-pancaka fast, the title Srila, and how to be free of lust.

🎙 Maharaj at 110:22 (auto-transcript): “Dair Rupsham, Dair Rupsham, Amataji, maybe please request you to unmute and have your question. Hare Krishna Maharaj, please accept my humble wishes. So, my question is very tiny. I have this question Maharaj that like from tomorrow when we start fasting for Bhishma Panchak,…”

Srila is a term of respect and opulence for an exalted person. For the fast: no grains or beans, eating once after sunset — fruits, nuts, boiled roots, ghee with limited spices — decided in advance and kept, not turned into a feast. Maharaj describes the traditional fuller observance for those who wish, and reminds devotees to give charity according to their means at the end.

🎙 Question from the floor at 110:22 (auto-transcript): “Dair Rupsham, Dair Rupsham, Amataji, maybe please request you to unmute and have your question. Hare Krishna Maharaj, please accept my humble wishes. So, my question is very tiny. I have this question Maharaj that like from tomorrow when we start fasting for Bhishma Panchak,…”

How can lust be uprooted?

🎙 Question from the floor at 122:25 (auto-transcript): “Mataji can please hear from you my humble obeisance is on to you Thank you for everything Guru Maharaj Thank you Because of saints like you we are getting something otherwise we are not so qualified or not so great to access Guru Maharaj my question is that We know all that…”

Pure love is what the soul is made of, like milk and sugar in a rasagulla, so it cannot be uprooted — only purified. As we worked hard to become sinful, we must work hard to transform it. — “So we have adulterated this pure love, what we call now lust.”

🎙 Maharaj at 123:53 (auto-transcript): “You cannot approve it, you cannot purify it because loss is opposite to pure love of Godhead every living entity has pure love originally, naturally. So we cannot uproot pure love from the heart because it's part of the soul, like desire. It cannot uproot desire. It is the…”

Start by caring for whoever is next to you. One who cannot even greet people or see them as persons cannot be free from lust, however realised he thinks he is. Those who care for others at their own expense are not lusty.

🎙 Maharaj at 125:21 (auto-transcript): “Beginning, the beginning, to begin the process, we must treat everyone kindly, nicely. Everyone will be treated nicely. The attitude of caring will be developed in us. you cannot go to hospital to go and get some tonic to purify it for that. The tonic to do this is the person…”

Krishna says he is sex life not contrary to religious principles; love, lust and such sex are different things, and confusing them makes us miserable. Lust is the body acting; in Vedic culture one speaks of placing the seed in the womb as service.

The elderly Caitanya dasa prayed daily to Jagannatha for a son, while Mahaprabhu prayed for a devotee to continue his mission. When his wife Lakshmipriya said the Lord wanted them to have a child, it was confirmed — Srinivasa Acharya's birth was pure devotional service.

🎙 Maharaj at 131:01 (auto-transcript): “come? how did he come? the parents were already old Chetayadas and Lakshmi Priya. Yes, Lakshmi Priya. As the Sindhava Satchara's mother, Lakshmi Priya and Chaitanya Das. Chaitanya Das used to go to Lord Jagannath every day and beg Lord Jagannath to give him a song. And that…”

maps.title: Radha Sunya · Session 25 · Gadadhara Pandit Rectifies His Offence

nodeData.topic: Session 25 · Gadadhara Pandit Rectifies His Offence
nodeData.note: SB 3.2.23 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Gadadhara Pandit, a lifelong renunciant, met Pundarika Vidyanidhi — whom Mahaprabhu called 'father' — and took him for a sense gratifier because of his royal opulence, until Mukunda's recitation of the Putana verse threw Pundarika into hours of ecstatic trance. Gadadhara rectified his mental offence not only by apologising but by taking initiation from him so he could be corrected. Maharaj warns that assumptions are very dangerous, calls the episode a lila for them and a lesson for us, and answers questions on genuine versus showy devotion, hope and faith, mental offences, and devotees who mistreat us. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Mahaprabhu would cry out 'Father!' though Jagannatha Misra had long departed, and said no one would recognise this person: outwardly he looked like a gross materialist, inwardly he was fully Krishna conscious. — “That is a paradox.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:54 (auto-transcript): “Chitama would say, Father, Father, Father. The devotee was surprised. Who is Father? Jagannamishra lived a long time ago. Chitama is feeling suppression. So what you ask, who is the father you are calling? Sri Tita Mahaprabhu would say none of you would understand him. If you…”

In this world a fool is a fool and a scholar a scholar, but Krishna is supreme and also the servant of his servants without losing his position. His pure devotees share such qualities — Pundarika Vidyanidhi was externally a materialist and internally a perfectly pure devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:54 (auto-transcript): “Yes, we don't see it like that in this material world. Someone is a fool is a fool. Someone is educated is educated. We see a different situation in Krishna. Krishna is the supreme personality of God. At the same time, he becomes a servant of his servants. yet his position…”

Mukunda Datta told Gadadhara Pandit, who loved pure devotees' company, that a great Vaishnava had arrived and took him for darshan. Gadadhara, simple and renounced since childhood, found a man in a palace among servants, oiled and perfumed, wearing ornaments and eating opulently.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:24 (auto-transcript): “What his dear devotee, Gododara Pondit, the external appearance. The great devotee Mukundadat was telling Gododara Pondit about the wonderful Vaishnava. And Mukundadat suggested that they go and have his darshan. When they arrived, they saw what appeared to be a complete…”

Maharaj describes the golden bed-throne with ivory and a diamond canopy, steps of coral and pearl, a golden spittoon, young girls fanning him and mirrors on three sides in which he admired himself and smiled. For a brahmacari this was disturbing: where is the sadhu?

🎙 Maharaj at 26:05 (auto-transcript): “Buddha Nidhi was sitting on the throne, the bedstead. The bed is made of gold, the throne is made of gold, ivory, the canopy on top of the throne was sitting. It is of diamonds. The steps to climb to the bed, the steps to climb to the throne, the asana, made of corals,…”

Pundarika at once noticed how devotion showed in the young Gadadhara's body. But Gadadhara, too simple to see behind the externals, judged only the outer standard and was disturbed in his mind. — “and he was somewhat disturbed in his mind.”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:16 (auto-transcript): “But because Pundalipi was so simple, he didn't hear that. At least he would have understood. A person who is seeing this, we're a different person, but he just look at the standard appearance. and he was somewhat disturbed in his mind. So he asks, where is the sadhu? Where is…”

A true friend stands by his friend in every circumstance. Mukunda read Gadadhara's mind and sang a Bhagavatam verse about Krishna giving liberation to the witch Putana.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:18 (auto-transcript): “Bukundu Dad was able to see the mind of Gatudara Tundu. A friend who is actually a friend will always have the friend in all circumstances from the heart. So, Mukundadhar perceived Gata Dara Pondi's mentality and began to chant a verse from Simad Bhagavatam about the amazing…”
Uddhava marvels that Krishna gave even Putana, who came to poison him, the position of a mother — so whom else should one take shelter of?

Putana's body was twelve miles long; the Vrajavasis needed ladders to lift Krishna from her. Earlier, as Bali Maharaja's daughter, she wished Vamanadeva were her son, then wished to kill him when he humbled her father. Krishna fulfilled both: she became one of his seven kinds of mothers, a nurse in Goloka — not on Yasoda's level. — “krishna fulfilled both of them”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:25 (auto-transcript): “Here we don't see, but she was 12 miles long. The height, 12 miles. So people were not able to see Krishna. The Brazibarshi have to use ladder to climb Putana's body to pick up Krishna from her chest. That is height of Putana, 12 miles. Before she became Putana, she was a…”

Sung in Mukunda's voice, which could melt stone, the verse pierced Pundarika's heart and he lost external consciousness.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:06 (auto-transcript): “When Pundaripi Nidhi had these bears from Mukundi, And Mukunda's voice is a powerful singer. When he sings, the stone melts. So when he's not like what we did, when Mukunda recited this verse, it entered into the ear of Pundalipi Jainidi and penetrated his heart, his…”

He fell from his throne, his jewelled crown smashing and gems scattering; many servants could not hold him. For six or seven hours he lamented that Krishna liberates even demons yet he had not received that mercy — his consciousness had entered the spiritual world.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:21 (auto-transcript): “He was unconscious After he fell from his throne smashed the crown the valuable gemstone of crown on his head smashed it on the ground all the jewels scattered everywhere he fell to the ground and the speed he fell 300 people were unable to hold him still that is the…”

Watching this, Gadadhara saw he had thought offensively and grew apprehensive. Maharaj asks us to remember how often we assumed something and later found the opposite — he has many such memories himself. — “Assumption is very dangerous.”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:33 (auto-transcript): “Assumption is very dangerous. Assumption, very dangerous. All of you can try to remember how many times we assumed something and later discovered that it was 100% opposite. I have many. So it took some time for Pondaribhidenji to regain consciousness, external consciousness.”

Only those on that level, like Mukunda, could know him. Pundarika is Vrishabhanu Maharaja, Radharani's father, and Gadadhara Pandit is an expansion of Radharani; by Krishna's desire pure devotees appear in different forms and rasas, as Svarupa Damodara, a sakhi, appears as a teacher.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:19 (auto-transcript): “Sri Chita Mahaprabhu has already told devotees that a person who is calling father, no devotee when they see him because he dressed differently and he behaved differently but his Christian consciousness is completely inside reserved only for those who are on that level like…”

Pundarika would not go to the Ganga by day, unable to bear people washing feet, clothes and pots in her; he went at night and sipped her water before his deity worship.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:05 (auto-transcript): “Because he knows himself. He will never go to Ganga in the daytime because he doesn't like to go and see people washing their feet, washing their cloth, washing their utensils inside Ganga. He considers this a disrespect. He will only go to Ganga only in the night when nobody…”

Hearing one verse, Pundarika was absorbed and showed complete disinterest in his surroundings. Devotees reflect on the assumptions they make about devotees who don't fit their image of saintliness, and how real absorption differs from outer show.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:59 (auto-transcript): “Going internal through reflections. Recognizing hidden devotion. Ten minutes. By hearing a special first time about Krishna, Pundurik Vidya Nigi became immediately absorbed, showing his complete disinterest in his physical environment and situation. When he had something…”

We judge by age, dress, tilaka and bead bag, or by a different counsellor's style; good kirtan singers are not necessarily absorbed. Signs of real absorption: humility, service attitude, how one treats others, steady sadhana without show, and how one responds when Krishna is described. Some admit they would not have recognised Mahaprabhu himself.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:41 (auto-transcript): “so i would like to reflect on the points that we discussed in the in the group i request other group representatives to please raise their hands so there were three questions first was like what are the what assumptions do i make when i see when i see devotees who don't fit…”

Gadadhara did not only apologise; he asked Mahaprabhu and others if he could take initiation from Pundarika Vidyanidhi — receiving not just forgiveness but favour.

🎙 Maharaj at 71:57 (auto-transcript): “Perfect rectification through surrender. How do you think Godotra Pondi responded to this revelation? Godotra Pondi not only apologized, but he asked Mbaha, Prabhu and others if he could take shelter of Pundari with the identity by initiation. In this way, he not only…”

children.topic: Lila for them, lesson for us
children.note:
Gadadhara is an eternal, pure associate who cannot truly fail to recognise his own father. The offence was arranged in the lila to warn us about assumptions — and since we don't know who is who, we should treat everyone nicely. — “For us, it is a lesson.”

🎙 Maharaj at 73:40 (auto-transcript): “Godal Jirah Pandit is trying to convey to us. We should be very careful with the assumption. For Godal Jirah Pandit, Pondri Vidyanidi and Chitam Mahaprabhu, this is Lila. It's a Lila for them. For us, it is a lesson. What are they teaching us? We should not have in perfect…”

children.topic: A guru who can correct him
children.note:
Citing Gour Govinda Swami, Maharaj says Gadadhara wanted a guru who could drag him by the ear and purify him; Mahaprabhu told him to take initiation at once. Krishna uses pure devotees to show us that even they accept a spiritual master to guide and correct them, without pride.

🎙 Maharaj at 74:42 (auto-transcript): “his teaching was a lesson so his holiness god vina maharaj said put uh god on that point did after seeing this he considered let me take initiation for him let me become his disciple so he can just touch me and drag me by the ear in this way i will get purified for this…”

Some who offend Vaishnavas can be freed only by becoming devotees themselves, making restitution as well as receiving forgiveness. Commit aparadhas and a devotional life that could have been easy becomes very difficult.

🎙 Maharaj at 77:20 (auto-transcript): “The complexity created by Aparo. People who have offended Vaisnava will have to suffer so much. For some of them, the only way they can be freed from all reactions is to become devotees. In other words, a reaction can be so overwhelming that they must now take to the…”

Write about a devotee you judged by appearance and what you missed; use the Bhagavatam test — who becomes absorbed when Krishna is discussed; plan one concrete act of respect; and check whether you behave in ways that invite others to offend. Protecting each other's creepers is teamwork. Treating everyone kindly is also how lust is transformed. — “Yes, it's a teamwork.”

🎙 Maharaj at 79:17 (auto-transcript): “Realization through compilation. Continue your 30-day notebook with today's focus on recognizing and rectification. External judgment. Awareness. Write about one devotee you have judged based on external appearance. What assumptions do you make? What devotional qualities…”

Questions on recognising genuine devotees, pleasing the guru, and hope versus faith.

🎙 Maharaj at 82:01 (auto-transcript): “thank you so much Shri Lakriti for the nourishing feast we will now have few questions I see hands of Romil Mataji would you like to go first Mataji yes Hare Krishna please accept my humble business Maharaj onto your lotus feet Maharaj just now we had a discussion about to…”

How can we tell — and doesn't suspecting show contradict thinking well of others?

🎙 Question from the floor at 82:34 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj just now we had a discussion about to determine who is general devotee and who is doing the external show so first of all I want answers from your end like how you would like to give a light on this and secondly if we are thinking this way, that they are doing…”

Be sincere and straightforward and Krishna in the heart will show who is who; then there is no need to assume. Some devotees who dress the deities and recite perfectly in the temple behave very differently at home. — “Everything we are doing shows.”

🎙 Maharaj at 84:02 (auto-transcript): “If a devotee is genuinely participatory, We have mentioned before, if a devotee is very sincere and a good practitioner, we don't have to assume who is who. We have mentioned before, a christian shows who is building it. It will show everything we are doing shows. One day,…”

At an annual festival Maharaj's guru honoured a godbrother as best devotee of the year for his management. Maharaj stayed silent and privately called him a rascal; within months that devotee broke principles and left. Praise from a pure devotee is dangerous if it inflates the ego — Maharaj says he simply tried to be sincere, and Krishna showed him.

🎙 Maharaj at 88:12 (auto-transcript): “But once, you know, one time, we had a festival, we used to have an annual festival, and one devotee was glorified as the best devotee of the year. I could have given him my word. I could have given him my word. he's the best devotee of the year so he got that word all the…”

children.topic: Q2 · Is my guru pleased with me?
children.note:
Maharaj answers with a little play — asking for water, then juice, then something else — to ask how she would feel. Try to understand the guru as he tries to understand you, and ask him directly, but not in the class.

🎙 Question from the floor at 94:14 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna. Guru Maharaj, Danvat Pranam, my humble and respectful obeisance is on to you. My question is, how can we know our spiritual master is happy with us or not? So, like I keep on messaging you so much, telling you everything. I think in my mind, my spiritual master…”

Should a devotee dwell on hope, or only on faith?

🎙 Question from the floor at 97:44 (auto-transcript): “I wanted to ask this question yesterday Maharaj as a devotee between hope and faith which one do you have to dwell more on that most of the times we have a lot of hopes and we're beginning to pray to Krishna over it and it is said that when all hope is lost it's where Krishna…”

Srila Prabhupada told a disciple that a case looked hopeless but he was always hopeful — because he had faith that Krishna would act. Hopelessness comes from lacking faith; Krishna is always there, it is we who are absent. — “But you know very well that I'm always hopeful.”

🎙 Maharaj at 99:07 (auto-transcript): “See, the Papa said that he was talking to one of his disciples. The case we have at hand is like a hopeless case. But you know very well that I'm always hopeful. I'm always hopeful. That is Prabhupada. He's always hopeful. Means what? That he has faith in Krishna. Krishna is…”

Rupa Gosvami's asa-bandha means hoping against hope. Faith gives hope: our prayers expect mercy because the acaryas and pastimes assure us, and whoever fully understands SB 10.14.8 becomes completely hopeful and faithful.

🎙 Maharaj at 100:40 (auto-transcript): “Rupa Goswami told us that. Asarbanda. What is the meaning of Asarbanda? who can tell us Asarbanda what does it mean? this is Rupa Goswami's words Pritamai Asarbanda means what? we are mooted yes we are mooted hope against hope Asar means what?”

Questions from the chat on the Putana verse, mental offences, unwanted thoughts and devotees who mistreat us.

🎙 Maharaj at 104:44 (auto-transcript): “we have two more questions from the chat box. One question is from Gaur Dayanath Prabhuji. He wants to know, he has two questions. He mentions that the words from Srimad Bhagavatam that speaks about Krishna's mercy on Puthana quoted to Pundarik Vidyanithi is the same verse…”

The verse said to Pundarika is one of those Vyasadeva's disciples recited to attract Sukadeva Gosvami. The common point is mercy: Krishna overlooked Putana's ill intention and accepted her act as service.

🎙 Question from the floor at 104:48 (auto-transcript): “One question is from Gaur Dayanath Prabhuji. He wants to know, he has two questions. He mentions that the words from Srimad Bhagavatam that speaks about Krishna's mercy on Puthana quoted to Pundarik Vidyanithi is the same verse quoted by Brahmanas sent by Srila Vyas there to…”

Gadadhara's offence was only mental. Maharaj: in Kali-yuga mental offences do not manifest immediately, but they are recorded and they grow until they become verbal and gross. Thinking we are safe is self-deception. — “Everything we do is considered.”

🎙 Question from the floor at 107:20 (auto-transcript): “Another question from Gaurudhaya Nath Prabhuji is, Gadadhar Pandit's offense was mental. It didn't become a verbal or physical offense. Yet, it is considered an aparadha. How should we analyze this leela regarding offenses to sadhus, especially since Srimad Bhagavatam states…”

children.topic: Q6 · Thoughts that just pop up
children.note:
We cannot stop a contaminated mind from producing such thoughts, but we need not let them stay: feel sorry, beg forgiveness and chant.

🎙 Question from the floor at 109:19 (auto-transcript): “so sometimes we don't want to think something but the thought automatically pops up into our mind and we immediately realize that this thought is not good and we want to discard that thought immediately I understand that this is mainly because we are carrying a lot of garbage…”

Stop taking it negatively: they are helping you pay debts from the past. Tolerate patiently without hurting them; when the debt is paid the same people will start liking you. Reacting with anger only adds to the debt — so see them as well-wishers.

🎙 Question from the floor at 110:23 (auto-transcript): “Vishnu Umurthi Sivak Prabhuji he says let's say we have some devotees who are not treating me well they are not doing good with me naturally I develop negative feelings for them how to purify this thought and how not to develop negative feelings for them if the devotees are…”
