nodeData.topic: Class 1 · Why So Many Religions?
nodeData.note: SB 6.4.1–43 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj opens SB 6.4 with the Pracetas, whose austerity left them angry, and Soma's plea for the trees, teaching that true knowledge and pure austerity soften the heart and that every body is a temple of the Lord. Through Daksha's Hamsa-guhya prayers he stresses that Krishna is reached by the attitude of service, not speculation, and explains why there are so many philosophies and religions: Krishna gives each person what he desires and level by level draws all toward himself. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Daksha was given the service of populating the universe, so Maharaj asks how anything auspicious should begin: with prayer and with austerity, which invokes the potency to do it well. King Vena took his post without austerity and met disaster; Daksha first went to the Vindhya hills to perform austerity, and his prayers came when the Lord appeared.

🎙 Maharaj at 09:36 (auto-transcript): “Anything that is very auspicious has a principle, which we see throughout the whole Vedic culture. What is that? What is the best way to start anything auspicious? What is the best way to start anything auspicious? Anything auspicious? anything you want to be want to get the…”

children.topic: A guru's fire passes to the ripe
children.note:
Narada's words so affected King Pracinabarhi that he could not wait to leave for the forest. Maharaj explains that a bona fide master always transforms a ripe disciple, passing on the fire of bhakti he himself received from the sages; if the disciple is not ripe, nothing happens.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:40 (auto-transcript): “someone's effect on him this is how expression masters will act a social massage will influence the life of the disciples that his potency if the disciples are ripe if the disciples are not right even if the spiritual master is bona fide and right nothing will happen but if…”

The Pracetas return from meditating in the water to find the land overgrown with trees. Maharaj asks what this means: with no government, everyone becomes a ruler, which is the sudra condition seen all over the world today; the useless trees stand for our sinful, unnecessary activities.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:40 (auto-transcript): “trees what does that mean what does it mean yes this neglect no government when there is no government no ruler in the community what will happen it is no ruler every person will become a ruler and in the community where everybody is ruling what is that sudra that is sudra…”

The verse tells how the Pracetas, angry at the trees, sent fire and wind from their mouths. Maharaj explains that austerity and knowledge produce one of two results: a softened, purified heart or pride; book knowledge alone makes people proud, while true knowledge makes one humble and gentle. — “A true knowledge makes one gentle.”

Maharaj presses the class: Prabhupada says a devotee is never angry, yet he and other masters chastised disciples strongly. The answer: it only looks like anger in our language. Real anger contaminates the angry person and the atmosphere, but a pure devotee's chastisement is love, and both the disciple and the environment are purified. Haridasa Thakura, beaten in the marketplaces, never became angry. — “when a pure devotee chastised does it look like anger it is love”

🎙 Maharaj at 25:06 (auto-transcript): “okay all right the word proper use is a devotee is never angry the word he used is never angry so my question was he is chastised many times disciples and probably i also have many chastisements so there are no devotees that was my question they are giving me an answer. I…”

children.topic: What is in the heart transfers
children.note:
Angry people cannot preach, for every pure devotee, even the Lord himself, was harassed by those he came to help. Maharaj says whatever we carry in the heart passes to listeners: doubt transfers faithlessness, purity transfers Krishna consciousness. Prabhupada called people rascals and they still became devotees because of his purity.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:00 (auto-transcript): “They cannot preach the Christian consciousness because they don't have the purity to affect the people whom they're preaching to. Because we are not going to meet with what we're expecting. glory is all over. It's not possible in this material world to meet with us. Nobody is…”

The moon-deity Soma, maintainer of all plants, sees the trees burning and pacifies the Pracetas with sympathy. Maharaj asks how the moon maintains vegetation: he places the six tastes in plants, giving us fruits, flowers, vegetables and oxygen.

The moon moves even the ocean, and on a full-moon night the senses are stirred while moonlight cools the mind. Maharaj recalls that the second prostitute came to Haridasa Thakura under a full moon, and that Krishna danced the rasa on the full moon. The trees are not at fault for overgrowth; fruit and flower trees must be kept.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:27 (auto-transcript): “people are very civilized or we can try it right you can try it on the full Monday how do you feel on the full Monday how do you feel in the full moon when the moon is full how do you feel yes it is agitating the sense of we are disturbed even though you see the ocean is…”

children.topic: Moon landings and the moon stone
children.note:
Following Prabhupada, Maharaj reasons that the maintainer of vegetation cannot have a barren planet: had the scientists really gone, they would have seen trees and met the moon-god. All they brought back was a stone, nothing like a perfectly designed Salagrama sila.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:29 (auto-transcript): “that means that they don't go there if they have gone to the moon they will have seen trees, vegetation moon go out also they would have seen him. They would have met with him. So he didn't go there. The only thing they got was Chanda Sila, the stone from the moon. We have so…”

Soma reminds the Pracetas that a king must wish his citizens prosperity and protect them. Maharaj adds Prabhupada's point that a citizen is anyone born in the land, so animals and trees are citizens too and must be protected, not killed. — “That means that animals are also citizens.”

children.topic: A cow's hairs, a cow's milk
children.note:
Who could count the hairs on one cow? Maharaj says killing a cow keeps us bound for that many years, one reason we stay so long in this world. We drink our mother's milk for some months but cow's milk for a lifetime, so the cow is more our mother and must be protected.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:16 (auto-transcript): “are they are hairs on the body of a cow can you imagine that who can count the hairs on the body of the cow just one cow who can count this is one of the reasons why we are staying too long in the material world because of one cow we are going to take bed as many times as the…”

The class began late because everyone ate a heavy feast after fasting and fell asleep. Maharaj uses it to teach sense control: break a fast lightly and gradually, and do not listen to the mind, which says you are tired when you are only full. — “because the mind is not a devotee”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:26 (auto-transcript): “what what was the reason what the reason for coming late eating heavy fists eating heavy fists you know when you fast and then you eat heavy what will happen to the body the body will be weak the body will be really weak so we cannot control the senses like that we cannot…”

Sense control begins not with the tongue but with the mind, the master of all the senses; control the mind and the rest follow. Maharaj explains that although intelligence should guide the mind, the mind is often strong enough to overpower it.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:13 (auto-transcript): “or to practice controlling the senses could begin from if you want to control our senses what does it begin from the mind not the tongue the mind if the mind is not controlled the tongue will not be controlled the mind if you control all the senses without the mind is failure…”

The verse asks us to see every body as a residence of the Lord. Maharaj says unity in diversity can never come until this is realised: if I do not see the Lord living in you, I will not value you and will naturally misuse you. — “If we want to have unity and diversity, then this should be realized.”

Real knowledge from a self-realised soul shows that all living beings belong to Krishna. Maharaj says such knowledge changes how we relate to and treat everything, and it makes one humble; that is why pure devotees respect all.

The verse praises one who subdues sudden anger. Devotees ask daily how to control lust and anger; Maharaj says tolerance depends on inner strength, which comes from purity, not from philosophy, just as only a well-prepared student passes. We should measure our progress by how much we can tolerate, as a traveller must know the distance to set his speed.

Soma offers the Pracetas Marisa as their wife to pacify them. Maharaj compares Hiranyakasipu, whose meditation was broken by anger after Narada chanted; he went home to his wife, Prahlada was conceived, and he returned to his austerities.

🎙 Maharaj at 63:29 (auto-transcript): “how did he control it the money came to him and chanted my enemy became angry with that contamination he cannot control meditation so what did he do he came back to the house and he slept with his wife that is how he anger was removed they control the anger and that is how…”

Marisa's mother Pramloca was no ordinary apsara. Maharaj tells how two demon brothers won a boon that only they could kill each other; Vishnu gathered beauty from everything to form Pramloca, and the brothers quarrelled over her until they killed each other.

🎙 Maharaj at 66:12 (auto-transcript): “From Rocha is as is mentioned in Absara is not the Absara like we get in the heavenly planet. From Rocha came from Krishna himself because after Hirakasipu was killed along with some others. There's some who fled out of fear on the second day. So, those who fled, they went to…”

Daksha means expert, a quality of a Vaishnava, but Maharaj notes this Daksha is expert for sense gratification. Having offended Lord Shiva, he once received a goat's head, and the same Daksha is now born again of the Pracetas.

🎙 Maharaj at 70:13 (auto-transcript): “one of the qualities of vajshanma is daksha so this is daksha here is that quality this is daksha here is that quality when this is quality for vajshanma daksha which one is this which one is this this one is sanctification daksha it's part for sanctification not that it has…”

Daksha's Hamsa-guhya prayers were not his own composition but already existed in Vedic literature. Maharaj asks why: Daksha, materially motivated, lacked the purity to compose such a prayer from his heart, yet the prayer was so potent that the Lord was pleased and appeared.

Understanding the Supreme Personality of Godhead is very difficult, which is why few follow this path. Maharaj says only the extremely fortunate take to Krishna consciousness, where service makes one's existence pure.

All the coverings on our consciousness are removed by the attitude of service. Maharaj recalls Prabhupada's saying that advancement depends on the attitude of the follower.

🎙 Maharaj at 86:15 (auto-transcript): “The Lord can be realized by the attitude of service. The attitude of service. All these coverings in our consciousness can be removed completely by our service attitude. And the famous quote from Prabhupada's instruction, famous quote, famous advancement”

Kamsa and Sisupala thought of Krishna day and night, the very absorption we struggle for, yet their meditation is condemned because their attitude was demonic. Krishna already has everything; what he values is our attitude. — “Even when he's sleeping, he thinks of Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 87:20 (auto-transcript): “Okay, for example, Kamsa was 24 hours Krishna conscious. What was wrong with his meditation? Kamsa, unfavorable, unfavorable attitude. Sissupal, think of Krishna 24 hours. Sissupal. Kamsa, he think of Krishna 24 hours. What is wrong with your meditation? Something which we…”

Maharaj tells the Bible story of a poor woman who gave her only coin while others gave fortunes; Jesus held up her gift as the purest he had received. She gave everything without thinking of tomorrow; a gift given condescendingly is no gift at all.

🎙 Maharaj at 91:01 (auto-transcript): “There is a story like that in a Bible. there is a story like that in the bible jesus was in the church and thousands of followers are there and they were giving him amount of money they were giving so much there was a lady one lady in her entire life she has only one rupee…”

On one sankirtana day one devotee distributed five books and Maharaj forty-five, yet the five-book devotee was glorified. Maharaj, feeling slighted, was told the other devotee had put in more effort and so received more purification. — “the energy he put into this is more than the energy”

🎙 Maharaj at 92:38 (auto-transcript): “one day we we went on Sankita one devotee distributed only five books and one other god brother he distributed more than us he did 45 books one did five when the resolve was announced grudel was glorifying the one who gave who distributed five books and the one who did 45…”

The verse places the Lord beyond everything expressed by material sound, mind or senses. Maharaj says Krishna exists before, during and after creation and is reached only by his causeless mercy when senses, mind and intelligence are engaged in service with the right attitude, beginning with the tongue.

The verse says the Lord, from within, keeps speculators agreeing and disagreeing without conclusion. Maharaj asks why Krishna does this: because they want to forget him, he gives them ample reason to forget, just as he gives devotees reason to remember. It is not his fault but his nature. — “He's doing it by our desire.”

Those who do not want Krishna get thousands of subjects to discuss. Maharaj points to endless cell-phone and car models that only change name and colour and keep us anxious; no phone can reach Krishna, but the tongue he gave us can. — “Only our tongue has to call that Krishna direct number.”

🎙 Maharaj at 109:02 (auto-transcript): “how many varieties of cell phone we have how many varieties cell phone yeah thousands because I use the word so thousands of subjects simple what is it what is it useful yourself what did you use common useful is make a call and receive a call right so then we're having…”

If God is one, why so many religions? Because people are at different levels, Krishna lovingly provides for each, like kindergarten, primary school, college and research. We also came through that speculation over many lifetimes, so being a devotee is great fortune; Prabhupada wrote to one devotee not to take the process cheaply. — “we should not take it cheaply”

🎙 Maharaj at 114:13 (auto-transcript): “this is one side that is just one side what are the other reasons if the absolute is one if god is one why soon the religion why why so the religion if god is one because everybody is not uh is not on that level to understand everybody is on a different level therefore there…”

Sankhya and bhakti both point to the same ultimate cause, but the analyst goes the long way round, counting elements, and few arrive. Maharaj says even the royal road of bhakti has accidents, and the rough road far more, so it is fortune to take to Krishna consciousness.

Krishna consciousness is the most difficult thing in the world: a degree takes five years, but how many lives to graduate as a devotee? Prabhupada and his guru wanted disciples to go back this life; Prabhupada's purports explain that most do not really want to go back. Krishna has opened the gate; it depends on us.

🎙 Maharaj at 121:41 (auto-transcript): “to take to christian consciousness in fact the most difficult thing for anyone to do in this world is is the most difficult thing one can ever do in life christian consciousness it's christian consciousness go to any college after five years we are graduate is it not how many…”
Is the Lord partial to devotees? Maharaj says no: those who worship him as a person see him as a person, and those who deny his form get no form. His names, form and pastimes are not material.

Impersonalists think any form must be defective like ours, so they treat deities as a means to be thrown away later; Maharaj says formlessness comes from frustration. A prison commissioner who visits a prison does not become a prisoner; his visit brings amnesty, just as Krishna's coming lets us see and hear him. — “formlessness is due to frustration”

🎙 Maharaj at 132:25 (auto-transcript): “they think that there is so much problem in name and form here so if lord also has form and name that means so all forms in this this world has some defect they are conditioned so if the lord has form he also become a conditioned person conditioned soul that is their…”

The Lord's name is not material: Ajamila called his son Narayana, and Narayana responded to his own name and delivered him.

🎙 Maharaj at 135:50 (auto-transcript): “And his name is not material like the proper said. Just calling Narayan, he got liberated. Even though he was not calling Narayan. But Narayan says, my name is calling. Let me do something. Let me do something. And he got what he did again. Because in the name of the Lord is…”

The verse compares the Lord's appearance through lower forms of worship to air carrying a fragrance. Maharaj says the Lord reveals himself only by his grace, not by speculation; the devotee's prayer is to see him as he actually is.

The Lord appears on Garuda with eight arms, ornaments and his associates. Maharaj insists these ornaments are no imagination; seeing Jagannatha or Radha-Krishna decorated every day, devotees have the great fortune of serving the Lord in person.

Daksha falls flat like a rod, as Dhruva did in another age; the same response in different ages shows it is real. Maharaj cites the saying that the eye that sees God shall die: one is transformed, as Dhruva no longer wanted the kingdom he came for. Losing taste for old attractions is the sign of advancement. — “you can never be the same person again”

A devotee raises a point after the reading.

🎙 Maharaj at 152:40 (auto-transcript): “Comment. You said Dhruvam Arad and Daksha, both God-Dashna of Lord, Dhruva and Daksha. So here is the Lord saying I am very pleased with your Ashrati and devotion, but we don't see the transformation of heart which Dhirva felt. He got transformed. He didn't ask for any…”

children.topic: Q1 · Why was Daksha not changed?
children.note:
Dhruva and Daksha both saw the Lord, but Dhruva was transformed and gave up his desire while Daksha took his boon and stayed materialistic. Why?

🎙 Question from the floor at 152:51 (auto-transcript): “You said Dhruvam Arad and Daksha, both God-Dashna of Lord, Dhruva and Daksha. So here is the Lord saying I am very pleased with your Ashrati and devotion, but we don't see the transformation of heart which Dhirva felt. He got transformed. He didn't ask for any material…”

Daksha is expert in sense gratification, and one attached to it cannot avoid offences, for material desire means envy. Maharaj adds that parents deserve respect only if they train children in Krishna consciousness: Narada delivered Daksha's eleven thousand sons, while Daksha could not deliver one. — “it's offensive personality it's not daksha for krishna consciousness”

🎙 Maharaj at 153:31 (auto-transcript): “Yes. Daksha is very offensive. it's offensive personality it's not daksha for krishna consciousness it's daksha for sense gratification and anyone who is attached to a sense gratification was cannot be free from offenses cannot be free only if one is free from sense…”

maps.title: Manah Siksa · Session 01 · The Life of Raghunatha dasa Gosvami

nodeData.topic: Session 01 · The Life of Raghunatha dasa Gosvami
nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj opens the Kartik series by explaining why we study instructions to the mind, then tells the life of Raghunatha dasa Gosvami — his boyhood fire of bhakti, Nityananda's 'punishment' at Panihati, his escape to Puri and his years at Radha-kunda. Along the way he draws lessons on association, integrity, and renunciation as opulence rather than poverty. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj opens the Kartik series: after visiting the holy places of Vrindavan, the aim is to stay in Vrindavan by remembering it. This year's feast is Raghunatha dasa Gosvami's instructions to the mind, because success in Krishna consciousness depends on the mind.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:44 (auto-transcript): “We are having these very, very powerful instructions. Instructions of Sularupa as Raghunath Das Goswami. It's popularly known as Das Goswami. Das Goswami. Splendid instructions to the mind. This instruction to the mind. We know very well that in Baragetal Rukesha, they don't…”

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 16:44

children.note:
Krishna does not ask for our face or our leg; He asks for the heart. So Raghunatha dasa Gosvami has given a feast specifically for the heart and mind.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:20 (auto-transcript): “We know very well that in Baragetal Rukesha, they don't say give me your heart give me your face give me your leg listen said give me your heart what manner of a mother doctor christian says you give the parts so rabbi has specifically given this feast for the heart how we…”

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 17:20

children.topic: Conquer the mind, reach the Supersoul
children.note: The mind is the leader of the senses and everyone's biggest enemy; when it is controlled, the other senses follow. Maharaj cites the Gita: one who has conquered the mind has already reached the Supersoul.

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 18:04

children.note: At the end of the Gita Krishna asks Arjuna whether he has heard with full attention, because such hearing destroys illusion. Maharaj asks us to hear this series the same way.

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 20:04

children.topic: From refusing to fight to obeying
children.note: Arjuna replies that his illusion is gone by Krishna's causeless mercy. The man who said he would not fight now says he will do whatever Krishna asks, because his mind has feasted on that nectar.

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 21:30

children.note:
Maharaj reads how young Raghunatha learned Vaishnavism from Balarama Acarya and received Haridasa Thakura's association, then ran away at fifteen to meet Mahaprabhu at Santipura despite his father's fears.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:05 (auto-transcript): “suppression he experiences. In his boyhood, Raghuna Das was instructed in the principles of Vaisnavism by Balaram Acharya, one of the most advanced devotees in Saptagram. Having received the association of Sri Titania's intimate devotee, Aridastakura, Balaram Acharya was…”

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 26:05

children.note:
Once the fire of bhakti burns in the heart, nothing can extinguish it. Haridasa Thakura's association lit that fire in Raghunatha. — “when the fire of bhakti is burning”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:52 (auto-transcript): “when the fire of bhakti is burning nothing can put it up nothing there's nothing that can put it up the fire of bhakti is there in the heart of raguna das goswami haridai sekura sparked that fire by his association and in that association he introduced the ultimate…”

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 28:52

children.note:
Business people talk business, professors talk about their profession, ordinary people talk about the body; when we meet a sadhu, he plants Krishna consciousness. That is what Haridasa Thakura and Balarama Acarya did.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:32 (auto-transcript): “we are talking about the heart manner the mind this is what happens when we meet with the side when we meet with business people they will talk business when we meet with the professor they will talk about their profession in the middle of business people they will talk about…”

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 29:32

children.note:
From his own experience Maharaj says a father's and mother's affection can obstruct spiritual life. In the same way, the affectionate dealings of neophyte disciples around a guru can obstruct, because they tell you one thing while the guru says another.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:38 (auto-transcript): “from the time of the father were thinking about him of course this is a this is a fatherly motherly affection from my experience from my spirit practical experience fatherly motherly affection can become an impediment for the same way the neophyte lovely dealings, neophyte…”

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 30:38

children.note:
At the second meeting Raghunatha weeps with love. Maharaj then points out how Mahaprabhu silently placed his associates in every kind of birth — an opulent home, a Muslim court, a demonic family, an animal form, a barren land — and later gathered them all to Navadvipa.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:05 (auto-transcript): “does go from there. As if seeing an only friend. Yes, they are seeing an only friend. I was seen how Chita Mohap who perfectly supremely taught so many lessons very silently. He sent Raghunadar Goswami to opulent life. He sent Rupa Goswami, Sanatana Goswami from Brahmanic…”

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 34:05

children.note: Mahaprabhu is showing the Gita's teaching that Krishna is the seed-giving father of all beings. Poverty, lack of education or birth in a land without the Ganga cannot stop anyone from Krishna consciousness. — “Poverty cannot stop”

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 36:04

children.topic: Not a mistake but a blessing
children.note:
Sending them to such places was a deliberate plan to plant bhakti there and bless the most unfortunate. No one is bereft of his mercy if we are fortunate enough to appreciate it. — “it was a deliberate attempt”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:09 (auto-transcript): “Why Chetanamakrabhu sent all his associates these places? It was not a mistake. it was a deliberate attempt to give blessing to the most unfortunate. In this way, he demonstrated that no one is bereft of his mercy, provided we have the fortune to appreciate Christian…”

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 38:09

children.note:
Mahaprabhu sends Raghunatha home to live outwardly like a worldly man until Krishna arranges his renunciation. Maharaj stresses that renunciation is not poverty, a hideout or avoiding responsibility.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:55 (auto-transcript): “Again, another lesson. Renunciation is not poverty. Renunciation is not poverty. Renunciation is not a denier. Renunciation is not a hideout. It is not avoidance or responsibility. Renunciation is natural opulence. nature of plants so you're talking about using Raghunada…”

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 39:55

children.note:
Starvation means I have nothing, so I do not eat. Austerity means everything is there, yet one deliberately refuses sense gratification for a higher purpose — as Raghunatha did in the midst of wealth. — “Austerity means that you have everything to eat,”

🎙 Maharaj at 40:38 (auto-transcript): “renunciation or austerity is different from starvation starvation is different austerity is different austerity means Raghunada Goswami is in the middle of wealth but it's not attracted it's not attracted starvation I don't have So I will not eat. That is, okay. I don't have…”

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 40:38

children.note:
During a period of heavy austerity Maharaj visited a temple in Nigeria. A devotee brought him a rice-milk preparation; when Maharaj said he had finished eating for the day, the devotee quietly uncovered it to test his vow. They both laughed, and the devotee covered it again.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:38 (auto-transcript): “some years ago that time I was doing very heavy or silly things so I went to visit one temple here in Nigeria and a devotee brought rice milk and he gave to me said Maharaj this is your prasada bravo this is your prasada I said oh I'm sorry I have finished my eating for today…”

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Brief History of the Author | Session 01 | Oct 17, 2024 · 41:38

maps.title: Manah Siksa · Session 02 · Introduction — A Step-by-Step Guide

nodeData.topic: Session 02 · Introduction — A Step-by-Step Guide
nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj introduces Manah-siksa as a step-by-step guide from the beginning of bhakti to perfection, urging each devotee to ask whether Krishna consciousness is truly his path and how he is living it. He explains practice and detachment, Prabhupada's temple as an environment for rehabilitation, and gives an overview of the twelve verses before answering questions on the wandering mind, gossip and detachment. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj asks whether our tradition has a handbook that takes a devotee from the very beginning to perfection. The answer is yes: Manah-siksa is that guidebook.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:16 (auto-transcript): “Do we have in our tradition a quick book to bhakti in its different stages? A book which will bring a person from the beginning to perfection The answer is yes. What is that? Manasikshara is a guidebook which takes us to full Krishna consciousness. A statement from…”

children.topic: Paddhati: one step at a time
children.note:
Bhaktivinoda Thakura calls it a paddhati, a step-by-step guide to progress. In his commentary, Bhajana-darpana (the mirror of bhajana), he says it answers the question that comes once faith awakens: how do I do it?

🎙 Maharaj at 10:47 (auto-transcript): “A statement from Bhaktivinotakura in Jaiva Dharma says that Manasikshara, When we call something a padati, it means a step-by-step guide to progress. Padati means a step-by-step guide to progress. Pada means foot and hattie progress. So Bhaktivno Takura says in his commentary…”

Maharaj calls it a very important step for every sincere devotee to ask whether, among all religions and activities, Krishna consciousness is the one he will live his life by. — “every sincere devotees will ask this question”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:01 (auto-transcript): “It is a very, very significant step, very, very important. And it is very much a necessity for any devotee who wants to be successful to understand this point. to ask ourselves a question of all the activities that one can do in this world of all the religion that are…”

A senior devotee asked long-time members to rejoin the movement — not by leaving and coming back, but in consciousness, because the mood we came with is often ninety percent different from the mood we keep now. — “Rejoining, it is within the consciousness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:56 (auto-transcript): “Even if we are already 100 years in the movement, His Solanus Bhakti Chema Haras requested that all of us Hare Krishna members, Hare Krishna devotees who have been practicing for 70 years to rejoin the movement. To rejoin the movement doesn't mean you have to go back to…”

Many came with great speed for 'back home, back to Godhead'; ten years later it is no longer the priority. People who called family life, school or gambling maya later went back to them. The mind brings in funny ideas, and situations always appear to support it. — “Don't forget, we are dealing with the mind.”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:20 (auto-transcript): “In the beginning, for some of us, we came here with heavy speed. Tomorrow, you're not from Godhead. Back home, back to Godhead. But after 10 years, that doesn't seem to be the goal or the priority. Don't forget, we are dealing with the mind. The mind will start to bring in so…”

Is this the religion I want to live by? What must I do to reach the goal? Am I doing it? How am I doing it? Maharaj calls this accountability — knowing the goal and doing what is needed — and promises it brings back the mood of our beginning. — “It means that we are existing, not floating.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:17 (auto-transcript): “Because we didn't answer ourselves this question. Is Krishna consciousness the religion I want to live my life into? The answer is yes. The next question should be what am I supposed to do to achieve the goal what am I supposed to do then we should also ask ourselves if we…”

Raghunatha dasa Gosvami reveals the secrets of harinama-bhajana by instructing his own mind. Maharaj stresses there is a formula: while chanting we must also work on ourselves.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:15 (auto-transcript): “Harinam Bhajan, Harinam Bhajan, Harinam Bhajan. As there is a formula for everything, the Harinam Bhajan, to do Harinam Bhajan is a formula given to us by all of Acharyas, and particularly Slambhakti Nautak, which we have repeated many times. As we are chanting the holy name…”

Chanting without working on ourselves is like lighting a fire and pouring water on it — in the end we get frustrated. Better to pour gasoline: the association of those who are successful in chanting. — “Better to pour gasoline.”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:17 (auto-transcript): “It's just like lighting fire and pouring water on it. One will get frustrated at the end. If you light fire, we should not pour water on it. Better to pour gasoline. the flame will go away the flame will go away what is that gasoline good association with those who are…”

Pure devotees are very careful not to hurt anyone. Srila Prabhupada said sorry to his disciples, Maharaj's own guru did so, and Krishna himself apologised to his servants. We must learn these things.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:25 (auto-transcript): “we will observe that One of the most important things we see in the pure devotees is that they are very careful what happens to anybody, even the objiri. Sir Papa said sorry to the disciples. My Guru Devastus said sorry. Sorry. We have simulated him. Sorry, sorry, sorry.…”

children.topic: Humility is a sign of purity
children.note:
Bhaktivinoda Thakura begins his commentary calling himself poor. Maharaj says the purest are the most humble, and quotes a Gosvami who calls humility the greatest weapon for conquering those of bad character. — “those who are pure, they are extremely humble”

I, poor…”

Bhaktivinoda was the wealthiest of devotees, materially and spiritually, yet presents himself as poor. Pure devotees put themselves in our position to show us how we ought to pray. — “So it is we who should pray like this.”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:22 (auto-transcript): “Look at the beginning. Bhakti Nautakura said, I, poor Bhakti Nautakura, I will say that is his humility. He is not a poor Bhakti Nautakura. Prabhupada called Krishna consciousness a culture of the mind. Krishna tells Arjuna the restless mind is hard to curb but can be controlled by practice and detachment; Manah-siksa gives both, the practical way to live the Gita.

children.topic: A day designed for the mind
children.note:
We have the holy name to chant, deities to worship, scripture to hear and read, devotees to associate with and service to do. Our lives are arranged so the mind always has something for Krishna. — “Our lives have been designed in such a way that we have everything to do”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:22 (auto-transcript): “It is also a suitable practice we can do every day. Our lives have been designed in such a way…”

To help a smoker quit, you take him out of the environment where smoking is normal. Prabhupada did not leave us with philosophy in the air; he made temples where illicit sex, gambling and intoxication are not allowed. — “He practically created a rehabilitation temple.”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:06 (auto-transcript): “What is detachment? In the material world, they say rehabilitation comes. Rehabilitation. What is that? a person who is addicted to a particular habit, for example, smoking. If we want the person to give smoking, we cannot keep the person in the same environment.…”

The training of the mind teaches us to look upward toward spiritual objects and persons. Looking up we feel bhakti and are drawn into bhava and finally prema; looking down we move the opposite way. — “we have to look up”

The first three verses give the qualification for spontaneous attraction to Krishna in Vrindavan: humility and freedom from pride, affection for all connected with Krishna, detachment from karma, desire for service, and worship of the Krishna of Vraja.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:29 (auto-transcript): “Verses 1 to 3 Qualification for the inner part of spontaneous attraction to Krishna in Vandava Basic humility and lack of pride These are technologies These technologies to be applied Basic humility and lack of pride A mentality conducive to affairs and eliminate one's inner…”

Krishna's cows, his friends, the Yamuna, everything in Vrindavan — these are our spiritual valuables and necessary ingredients for our festival in Krishna consciousness.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:32 (auto-transcript): “means Krishna's house, Krishna's boyfriend girlfriend's, Krishna's house Krishna, everything in Vrindava Jamula God, God than everything connotable Krishna. It's our spiritual value. They are all necessary ingredients for our festival in Krishna concessions. Detachment from…”

Detachment from karma does not mean doing nothing; activities connected with Krishna become spiritual. But Maharaj jokes about misusing the idea — 'I'll kill you while chanting', 'go to sleep, I'll eat for you' — a dangerous misunderstanding.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:10 (auto-transcript): “Of course, all this needs explanation. It does not mean we should not do any activity but our activities will be connected with Krishna our activities will be connected with Krishna anything we do in connection with Krishna becomes spiritual but one cannot say Prabhu, I want…”

The instruction is to worship Vraja Krishna, the son of Yasoda — not the Yadu prince or Vasudeva Krishna. Maharaj notes Mahaprabhu urged devotees toward Radha and Krishna of Vraja as the ultimate, and that Krishna himself says this.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:44 (auto-transcript): “worshipping Vraja Krishna He didn't say we should worship Yadukuma He didn't say that He didn't say Vasudev Krishna it is said here Braj Krishna Yasudhananda yes that Krishna was worshipped St. Mahavadu told his exalted devotees give up worshipping Sitaran give up worshipping…”

The middle verses remove obstacles at ever subtler levels by the mercy of Krishna and his devotees, and the later verses engage us in our eternal position under Radharani.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:16 (auto-transcript): “Verses 4-7. The process of eliminating obstacles, going subtler and closer to the root, but he stepped by the mercy of and love for Krishna and his devotees. Verse 4. Problems absorption in mundane topics, desires for liberation and desires for the uplands of Naraya. He gave…”

Each verse names a problem and its remedy: mundane talk and desires for liberation or Vaikuntha, wicked deeds born of lust and anger, deceit and pretence, and the hunger for fame — answered by service to Krishna, crying to his devotees, love for Radha and Krishna, and serving a great devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:35 (auto-transcript): “Verse 4. Problems absorption in mundane topics, desires for liberation and desires for the uplands of Naraya. These verses describe taking shelter of Krishna's pleasure potency and tasting many flavours of love through hearing, meditating and serving Krishna, Radha, Lalita, Visakha, Radha-kunda and Govardhana.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:02 (auto-transcript): “Engaging in our eternal spiritual position through taking shelter, meditating and serving Krishna's eternal pleasure potency. The last verse glorifies the others: following these teachings brings the jewel of service to Radha and Krishna in Vrindavan as a follower of Rupa Gosvami, joining Krishna's pastimes with his pure devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:05 (auto-transcript): “Now verse 12. Glories of these verses. As a summary. children.topic: Q1 · My mind wanders while chanting
children.note:
During this Damodara month the mind keeps drifting while chanting — how to bring it back?

🎙 Question from the floor at 45:34 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna Maharaj. Accept my humble obeisance Maharaj. Thank you very much. Regarding this, actually about controlling the mind because in this Dhamudur month we keep on chanting Hare Krishna mantra suddenly we stop the mind is getting diverted thinking of something like…”

Prabhupada answered a disciple with the same complaint: forget your mind, chant with the tongue and hear with the ear. A fixed mind is the perfect stage; we cannot jump there first, so we keep practising patiently. — “Forget your mind.”

🎙 Maharaj at 46:35 (auto-transcript): “The Wotero always ask this question. My mind is still going here. My mind is still going there. My mind is still this. My mind is still that. nodeData.topic: Session 03 · Verse 1 — Give Up All Pride
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 1 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Through Bhaktivinoda Thakura's song and commentary on the first verse, Maharaj explains why the mind must be given, without pride, to the guru, Vrindavan and its residents, the devotees, the mantra and the holy name — we cannot reach Krishna without them. He stresses straightforwardness with the guru, the unity of diksa and siksa gurus, the five kinds of pride, and taste in chanting as the test of progress. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:

nodeData.topic: Session 04 · Verse 1 — Develop Attachment
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 1 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Returning to verse 1, Maharaj shows how pride creates illusion and explains Bhaktivinoda Thakura's five kinds of pride with examples from Brahma, Indra and Duryodhana. He then explains the seven objects of attachment, how the soul's natural love becomes lust, the call to intense endeavour without defeatism, and why love grows by hearing rather than physical nearness. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:

nodeData.topic: Session 05 · Verse 2 — Implied Doubts in Verse 1
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 2 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj opens verse 2 by explaining why no reward was promised this year: he wants devotees who come for Krishna, not for certificates. Through Bhaktivinoda Thakura's song and commentary he explains going beyond Vedic dharma and adharma, living in Vraja as absorption in Radha and Krishna, and the doubts verse 1 raises about livelihood — answered by Srivasa Pandita's faith in Krishna's promise to maintain his devotees. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:

nodeData.topic: Session 06 · Verse 2 — Approach a Pure Devotee
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 2 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj completes the second verse: Caitanya Mahaprabhu is to be remembered as non-different from Krishna, and the spiritual master as the dearest servant of Mukunda, sent by Krishna to take us home. He lists six ingredients of worship, closes with a meditation on how Krishna received Radharani's love and golden complexion, and answers questions on recognising pure devotees, working while staying Krishna conscious, and serving without familiarity. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 07 · Verse 3 — Offer Obeisance to Three Personalities
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 3 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The third verse asks the mind, if it longs to serve Radha and Krishna in Vraja, to remember and bow to Svarupa Damodara, Rupa Gosvami with his associates, and Sanatana Gosvami. Maharaj explains holy greed and Krishna's own restlessness for Radharani's love, Svarupa Damodara's intimacy with Mahaprabhu, the Ratha-yatra mood of bringing Krishna back to Vrindavan, and how Rupa Gosvami read Mahaprabhu's heart. Questions follow on friends in the next life, minimising the guru, keeping distance without hatred, and praying in difficulty. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

maps.title: Manah Siksa · Session 08 · Verse 3 — From Vaidhi to Raganuga Bhakti

nodeData.topic: Session 08 · Verse 3 — From Vaidhi to Raganuga Bhakti
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 3 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Continuing verse 3, Maharaj takes up the question behind it — can the unique love of Vraja be had outside Mahaprabhu's line? — by explaining vaidhi bhakti done out of loyalty, raganuga bhakti driven by taste and spiritual greed, and how rati matures into prema. He concludes that this love comes through the Gosvamis, who must be accepted as instructing gurus, and closes with the pastime behind the name Damodara. Questions cover madhurya and audarya, meditating on guru, when raganuga practice begins, deity worship, and Bhishma. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 09 · Verse 4 — Mundane Talk, the Plundering Prostitute
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 4 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj begins verse 4, taking only its first line: mundane talk is a prostitute that plunders the heart's treasure, and its worst form is criticism of others. He illustrates it with gossip in temple kitchens, Ramacandra Puri's offence to his guru Madhavendra Puri against Isvara Puri's humble service, and a stern lesson on forgiveness, then touches on the tigress of impersonal liberation. Questions follow on Pundarika Vidyanidhi, true forgiveness, business talk, and how even advanced souls can fall by offence. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 10 · Verse 4 — Beyond Liberation and Vaikuntha
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 4 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Continuing verse 4, Maharaj explains why impersonal liberation is a tigress — selfish, born of frustration and empty of service — and why even attachment to Narayana is set aside: in Vaikuntha love is veiled by awe, while Vraja is pure sweetness. He glorifies Haridasa Thakura's heart stolen by Krishna and closes with the story of Krishnadasa Babaji, who left Vraja and burned in separation. Questions cover moods in the spiritual world, temple quarrels, Arjuna's duty, choosing a guru, and a child who wants to see Krishna. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 11 · Verse 4 — Love Beyond Vaikuntha
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 4 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Continuing verse 4, Maharaj shows why pure devotees see heaven, mystic power and liberation as trash next to Krishna of Vrindavan, telling of a yogi destroyed by the crowds his powers drew. Through Gopa-kumara's visit to Vaikuntha he explains that awe and reverence cannot satisfy a soul whose love is intimate, and in a long Q&A he speaks on humility, the guru as Krishna's postman, and using the human body for devotional service. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 12 · Verse 5 — The Six Highway Robbers
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 5 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj opens verse 5: lust, anger, greed, illusion, madness and pride wait like robbers on the devotee's path, and the remedy is strong determination and crying out to Krishna's devotees. Using the sparrow and Garuda, Ambarisa's Sudarsana and Bhagavad-gita 2.62–63, he shows how we fall and how we are protected, then answers many questions on focus in service, provocation, surrender and anxiety. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 13 · Verse 5 — The Power of Association
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 5 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Continuing verse 5, Maharaj explains how our six enemies tie the ropes of wicked deeds around our neck, and why the remedy is to cry out to the devotees of Krishna, the killer of Baka, who stands for duplicity and hypocrisy. Through Prahlada in the womb, Narada as a servant boy and Jivana Thakura's touchstone he shows that real association means attentive, faithful hearing, not just sitting near a sadhu. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:

maps.title: Manah Siksa · Session 14 · Verse 6 — The Donkey of Deceit

nodeData.topic: Session 14 · Verse 6 — The Donkey of Deceit
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 6 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj begins verse 6: beyond lust and anger lies a subtler enemy, deceit, pictured as a donkey whose urine we bathe in thinking it pure, when we should bathe in the ocean of Radha and Krishna's love. He warns leaders that followers copy them blindly, lists how each kind of practitioner hides duplicity, and tells how Rama said Hanuman could not recognise him while disguised. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 16 · Verse 6 — Bathe in Radha's Ocean
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 6 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj defends Srila Prabhupada as the complete foundation, then finishes verse 6: the urine of the donkey of deceit has no value, a special hell awaits religious cheaters, and the cure is to bathe in the ocean of love at Radha and Giridhari's feet. Through Bhaktivinoda Thakura's prayer to Radharani, Rupa Gosvami's eight names of Radha-Madhava and Krishna refusing Duryodhana's feast, he shows that without sincerity and respect for Vaishnavas our service is not accepted. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 17 · Verse 7 — Prestige, the Dog-Eating Woman
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 7 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Closing Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura's song on deceit, Maharaj shows that the cure is to hold the feet of the Lord's devotees and serve them a lot, illustrated by Ravana's spies spared by Lord Ramacandra. He then opens verse 7: the desire for prestige is the root of deceit, and we can test our progress by what attracts us — holy places and Krishna-katha, or buildings, politics and idle talk. On Govardhana Puja day he closes with a meditation on Krishna's dancing and answers questions on deceit, hidden sadhana and Radharani's glance. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj recalls the past days on the demon of deceit, which Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura compares to donkey urine that we should stop drinking in favour of the nectar from Srimati Radharani's lotus feet. Without giving up deceit, he says, liberation is not possible.

nodeData.topic: Session 18 · Verse 7 — Krishna's Incomparable Commanders
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 7 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Continuing verse 7, Maharaj explains who the Lord's 'beloved, incomparable commanders' are and how their potency enters our heart — through their embrace, the dust of their feet, their remnants and their instructions. Ramanujacarya's fish, the Rama-bhakta who met Mahaprabhu and Gaura Kisora dasa Babaji's refusal of pretenders show that only a heart free of duplicity receives this mercy. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 19 · Verse 8 — Cry for Mercy in Vraja
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 8 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Opening verse 8 through Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura's song, Maharaj describes Vrindavan as a spiritual land Krishna brought here for us, and gives the medicine for a deceitful heart: wander in Vraja, sing the glories of Radha and Krishna and cry sincerely for mercy, using Rupa Gosvami's prayers to Gandharvika as meditation. He then urges us to be love-finders rather than fault-finders, with seven 'tablets' against fault-finding, and answers questions on Jagannatha, Tulasi Devi and early chanting. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 20 · Verse 8 — Radiant Love and the Gopis' Shelter
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 8 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. On Srila Prabhupada's disappearance day Maharaj continues verse 8 with ujjvala-prema, the radiant love of Vraja, and recalls how Prabhupada showed the ecstatic symptoms Rupa Gosvami describes as he departed. That love comes only by Srimati Radharani's mercy, through following the gopis, serving her sakhis, giving up a 'masculine' mentality and serving the deity — Giridhari — when advanced association is not at hand. Questions cover steady prayer, deity worship, mindfulness and fitting japa into family life. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 21 · Verse 9 — Meditating on Vraja's Moon
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 9 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Beginning verse 9, Maharaj presents its meditation: Krishna as the moon of Vraja's forest and Lord of our mistress Sri Radha, Lalita and Visakha as her friend and teacher, and Radha-kunda and Govardhana as givers of love — reached by constant service under the manjaris' guidance. Through Rupa Gosvami's prayers he teaches the cataka bird's single-minded shelter and the hope of Krishna's mercy, and in questions explains attraction, hidden practice, pleasing Krishna as the measure of service, and the glory of Govardhana. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 22 · Verse 9 — Lalita, Visakha and the Yamuna
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 9 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Continuing verse 9, Maharaj reads Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakura's commentary on remembering Lalita as Radharani's dearest friend and Visakha, whose other form is the Yamuna, with Rupa Gosvami's prayers to both; he stresses that the Yamuna purifies even by sight. A long question session follows: why this world can never become heaven, the special sweetness of Krishna in Gokula, how sadhana stays fresh, Krishna as the eternal witness, and why Krishna permits us to act against our own good. nodeData.topic: Session 23 · Verse 9 — Radha Kund and Govardhan
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 9 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Completing verse 9, Maharaj gathers its six meditations and dwells on the last two: Radha Kund, the liquid form of Radharani where the divine couple's pastimes go on unseen, and Govardhan, the best of devotees who secretly watches those pastimes. He tells of the water fight and the blue lotus, his own experience at a wish-fulfilling tree at Radha Kund, and the process of begging for mercy from those who have it. Questions follow on separation (viraha) as the keeper of prema, Tulasi's curse, fault-finding and chanting with attention. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 24 · Verse 10 — Worship Radhika, Hari's Beloved
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 10 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Opening verse 10 on Gopastami, Maharaj explains why Radharani cannot be compared with anyone — she is the source of all beauty and the only one who fully controls Krishna — and why there is no reaching Krishna without her mercy. He goes through her twenty-five principal qualities with pastimes, closing with Jayadeva Gosvami and the line Krishna wrote himself. Many questions follow, on obstacles, Tulasi Devi, Radharani's covered feet, mindfulness, the Dvaraka queens, exclusive worship and how to check our progress. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
The verse says Radharani's beauty outshines the goddesses and her fortune surpasses Krishna's queens. Maharaj explains why no comparison is possible: every other beauty takes its beauty from her, for she is the origin. — “She is a source of all beauties.”

nodeData.topic: Session 25 · Verse 10 — Radha's Mercy and the Serpent's Hood
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 10 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Continuing verse 10, Maharaj reads Rupa Gosvami's flower-offering of praise to Radharani and Raghunatha dasa Gosvami's cry for her mercy, then the commentary's path to Vraja love through a guru in the mood of a manjari — possible only with humility, eagerness and fixed resolve. The parting story of Rupa's 'serpent's hood' and Sanatana's vision shows how disagreement between pure devotees only deepens their love. Questions cover the siddha-deha, preaching to the uninterested, gurus at different stages, following temple authorities and taking the guru's medicine. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 26 · Verse 11 — Bhajan Under Sri Rupa's Guidance
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 11 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Beginning verse 11, Maharaj explains Bhaktivinoda Thakura's quiet method of bhajan: drink the nectar of Radha and Krishna's pastimes without display or politics, follow Sri Rupa's specific instructions as a patient follows a physician, and keep outer sadhana with inner meditation. From the commentary he shows how service begins at a distance and comes closer only with training, illustrated by Lord Siva waiting as a gopi and Isvara Puri's service to his guru. Questions follow on Radharani's role, spiritual and material anger, signs of advancement, etiquette for newcomers, and attachment. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 27 · Verse 11 — The Five Daily Nectars
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 11 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. On Ekadasi at the start of Bhishma Pancaka, Maharaj continues verse 11: the mind should drink every day the nectars of worship, glorification, meditation, hearing and obeisances, and worship Govardhana. He dwells on the sweetness of Krishna's form and his 'faulty' qualities that attract renounced sages, the stages of remembrance, and the cell phone that has replaced evening hearing — then answers many questions on austerity, holy name, the dhama and dealing with colleagues. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: Bhishma Pancaka: purified to serve better
children.note:

🎙 Maharaj at 14:05 (auto-transcript): “Krishna gave Bishma the five days to prepare his consciousness because he has been army general for years, for thousands of years, thousands he fought, thousands of battles he fought, thousands of discourses he conducted. so Krishna gave him five days to adjust the…”

orbit.ref: Manah-Siksa: Splendid Instructions to the Mind | Session 27 | Kartik | Lagos, Nigeria | Nov 12, 2024 · 14:05

nodeData.topic: Session 28 · Verse 12 — The Final Blessing
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj begins the closing verse, in which Raghunatha dasa Gosvami blesses whoever recites and studies the eleven instructions with the jewel of serving Radha and Krishna in the forest of Gokula. A 'sweet voice' means a sweet heart; the teaching must be studied daily; every group and every guru serves under Rupa Gosvami and Radharani; and living in Gokula means absorption in Vrindavan wherever we are. Through Lord Shiva's story and Rupa Gosvami's praise of Mathura he shows the dhama's protection, followed by wide-ranging questions. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:

maps.title: Manah Siksa · Day 29 · Sri Tulasi–Saligrama Vivah — Vrinda Devi Descends

nodeData.topic: Day 29 · Sri Tulasi–Saligrama Vivah — Vrinda Devi Descends
nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. For the Kartik wedding of Tulasi and Saligrama, Maharaj tells from the Brahma-vaivarta Purana how Vrinda Devi and Sudama were cursed in Goloka, took birth in this world as Tulasi and Sankhacuda, performed immense austerities and were married by Lord Brahma. Along the way he draws lessons on austerity compared with our five-day Bhishma Pancaka, on compatibility in marriage, on the power of chastity and on the eight names of Tulasi, then answers many questions. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Today's subject is Vrinda Devi, Tulasi Maharani. Maharaj read her full story years ago in an English translation of the Brahma-vaivarta Purana, because he has deep attachment to her and wanted to know everything about her.

nodeData.topic: Day 30 · Verse 12 — Vrindavan, Radharani's Forest
nodeData.note: Manah-siksa 12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. On the last day of Kartik Maharaj completes verse 12 through Rupa Gosvami's eight prayers to Vrindavan: Brahma's longing to be grass there, a land where everything is reversed, and the pastime in which Krishna himself must admit that Radharani owns the forest. After the commentary closes, devotees begin their gratitude offerings, and Maharaj answers them with teachings on hope, prayer, desire to serve, and sadhana as the spiritual warrior's weapon. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:

nodeData.topic: Closing · Gratitude Offering — Kartik Continues Within
nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The series closes with devotees' gratitude offerings for the month of Manah-siksa: vows kept, early rising, steadier chanting, new realisations about austerity, poems and prayers. Maharaj answers each briefly — sixteen rounds are non-negotiable, the acaryas were never lazy, bhakti's fire burns every impurity, scripture is a mirror for the heart — and asks that Kartik continue within by meditating daily on what was heard. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

maps.title: Bharata Maharaja · Session 01 · SB 5.7.1–5 · Leadership by Following the Father

nodeData.topic: Session 01 · SB 5.7.1–5 · Leadership by Following the Father
nodeData.note: SB 5.7.1–5 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj opens the series by showing that Bharata Maharaja's greatness came from rigidly following his father: he was chosen for sincerity and obedience, not by fame or voting, and that following empowered him to change the world. Perfect leadership means loving the citizens like one's own children and keeping everyone engaged; we lack such a king today because we lack the qualities to merit one. The animal sacrifices of old are forbidden in Kali-yuga, and sankirtana is the yajna for this age. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: Following the father, step by step
children.note:
Bharata Maharaja was strict in religious principles because he walked fully in his father's footsteps. Maharaj draws out the point: Bharata is a follower who valued parampara.

🎙 Maharaj at 00:34 (auto-transcript): “That means that he is a follower and he valued parampara. Our success in Krishna consciousness depends on how we rigidly follow the instructions of our spiritual master in total.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 00:34

children.note:
Our success in Krishna consciousness depends on how strictly we follow the instructions of our spiritual master, in total. — “Our success in Krishna consciousness depends on how we rigidly follow”

🎙 Maharaj at 00:52 (auto-transcript): “Our success in Krishna consciousness depends on how we rigidly follow the instructions of our spiritual master in total. So, Bharat Maharaj ruled a citizen very successfully.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 00:52

children.note: Maharaj asks why Bharata ruled the citizens so successfully, and answers: because he followed his father.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 01:36

children.note: Sukadeva Gosvami tells Pariksit how Bharata, by his father's order, began to rule the earth and married Pancajani.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 06:01

children.note:
Not by fame and not by scholarship. When the guru or the father sees sincerity and obedience, that person receives special attention. — “This is how to select a successor.”

🎙 Maharaj at 07:38 (auto-transcript): “This is how to select a successor. It's not by fame. It's not by scholarship. When the guru or the father sees the symptom of sincerity and obedience to the father or the guru, he will be given extra special attention.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 07:38

children.topic: No voting among a hundred sons
children.note:
Rishabhadeva had a hundred sons, yet there was no voting and no personal interest. It came naturally: Bharata manifested the qualities, so his father noticed him and placed him on the throne.

🎙 Maharaj at 09:46 (auto-transcript): “There was no voting here. Lord of Sabadev had warned on their songs. There were no voting. Among the hundreds, there were no voting. It came naturally. He manifested the qualities. Therefore, the father noticed him.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 09:46

children.note:
Maharaj sums it up as the natural sequence of empowerment, in one word: follow. — “Anyone who follows will be empowered.”

🎙 Maharaj at 11:26 (auto-transcript): “Anyone who follows will be empowered. This is a natural sequence of empowerment. Follow. Yes. Text number two. Just as a false ego creates the subtle sense objects, Maharaj Bharat created five sons in the womb of Panchajani, his wife. These sons were named Sumati, Rashtra…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 11:26

children.note: These verses name Bharata's five sons by Pancajani and tell how the land once called Ajanabha-varsa came to be known as Bharata-varsa.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 11:51

children.note:
No appointment, no campaign, no election — the world was changed simply by Bharata's purity. Maharaj asks what that potency is, and answers: following his father's footsteps. — “Everything is happening by the potency, the purity of Maharaj Bharat.”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:13 (auto-transcript): “Yes. Still no appointment. There is no appointment here. There is no campaign here. There is no election here. Everything is happening by the potency, the purity of Maharaj Bharat. It changed the world.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 14:13

children.note: This verse describes Bharata as an experienced ruler who cared for his citizens as his father and grandfather had, keeping them in their duties.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 15:34

children.note:
He was expert and learned because he received perfect training from his father; therefore he could rule perfectly.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:43 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj Bharat was experienced and well learned because he underwent perfect training from his father. Therefore, he perfectly ruled the citizens.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 16:43

children.note:
Maharaj puts the question to the room. Perfect rule means Bharata loved the citizens — he saw them exactly as he saw his own children.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:34 (auto-transcript): “What do we mean by perfect leadership, perfect rule? What is perfect rule? leadership. Perfect rule means Maharaj Bharat was as affectionate to the citizens as his father and grandfather had been. It means what? He loved the citizens.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 17:34

children.note:
Following Srila Prabhupada's purport, a chief executive must keep every citizen engaged in his occupational duty. That is perfect leadership.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:45 (auto-transcript): “And he kept all the citizens busy, engaged in their occupational duties. As Papa said, it is most important that a chief executive rules the citizens by keeping them fully engaged in their respective occupational duties. This is perfect leadership. Everyone was being engaged.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 18:45

children.note:
Out of love he maintained varnashrama: brahmanas, ksatriyas, vaisyas and sudras each engaged, and the spiritual orders of brahmacari, grihastha, vanaprastha and sannyasi visibly present.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:43 (auto-transcript): “Because Bharat Maharaj loved the citizens, he divided the citizens, he maintained the Varnashram system, he maintained Varnashram system. Brahmanas, Chatriyas, Vaishyas, Chudras were perfectly engaged.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 19:43

children.note:
If we want peace under our leadership, everyone must be engaged; no one should be left unemployed or unoccupied. — “No one should remain unemployed or unoccupied in any way.”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:30 (auto-transcript): “No one should remain unemployed or unoccupied in any way. This is leadership. That is, if we want the peace in our leadership, everyone must be engaged. Although formerly the government was a monarchy, all the kings were very affectionate towards the citizens and they…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 21:30

children.note:
Maharaj asks the audience his own question before taking theirs: why is there no Maharaja Bharata today?

🎙 Maharaj at 23:17 (auto-transcript): “We can see that we don't have Barat Mahdash now. Yes, it is true. We don't have Maharaj Bharat now. We don't have him now. Why? We don't have Maharaj Bharat. I know many questions are coming. Let me ask you my own question first before you start. Can you tell me, why there is…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 23:17

children.note:
Devotees answer: no disciplic succession followed, Kali-yuga, no varnashrama, no father like Rishabhadeva, no spiritual education from childhood, Krishna not at the centre, leaders seeking sense gratification, great people not wanting to lead.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:29 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, Gurudev. Please accept my most humble of instances. Gurudev, I think because no disciplic succession was following that that is why Okay, very good, thank you because Kaliyuga Very good And Varnashram system was also missing that is also the reason Gurudev Very…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 24:29

children.topic: Citizens must merit such a king
children.note:
Maharaj's answer: to have a Bharata Maharaja there must also be good citizens who merit his qualities. We do not have him because we lack those qualities ourselves.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:16 (auto-transcript): “To have Barat Maharaj, to have Barat Maharaj, there should be also good citizens that will merit Barat Maharaj qualities. To have Barat Maharaj, today, we don't have him today because we also lack the qualities or merit, the quality of Bharat Maharaj. We shouldn't blame our…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 28:16

children.note:
We should not blame our leaders, because they are the combined consciousness of the people. — “our leaders, they are aggregate consciousness of the citizens.”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:47 (auto-transcript): “We shouldn't blame our leaders because our leaders, they are aggregate consciousness of the citizens. If we are good children, we have good parents.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 28:47

children.note:
If we are good children we have good parents; the parents' consciousness produces the child, and the child's consciousness reflects the parents. Everything is connected.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:18 (auto-transcript): “If we are good children, we have good parents. The consciousness of the parent produces a child. The child's consciousness is also the result of the parent's consciousness. So we are all connected. Everything is connected.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 29:18

children.note:
We all contribute to what is happening today, so we are all responsible for it.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:06 (auto-transcript): “So we are all responsible for what is happening today. All of us are responsible. We contribute to what is happening. Toh is sab ke liye, ham sab log sayam jimmedar hain. Ham sayam is ke bhaagidar bhi hain. Take summa five. Paanchwa number shlok, agla. With great faith, King…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 30:06

children.note: This verse lists the many Vedic sacrifices Bharata performed with great faith, sometimes fully and sometimes in part, to worship the Supreme Lord.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 30:20

children.topic: Why such yajnas are forbidden now
children.note:
These sacrifices are not required today — they are forbidden. They were never meant for the participants to eat flesh; their purpose was to test the priests' ability and to give the offered animal a new, young body.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:42 (auto-transcript): “Now these Jagyas are not, they are not required, they are forbidden, yes, they are forbidden. Because these yagya were not performed for the performers or the participants to eat the flesh of the animals.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 31:42

children.note:
Because we have become fallen, there are no priests able to give the old animal a young body and achieve the result, so these yajnas have stopped.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:56 (auto-transcript): “Because we became fallen, therefore there is no qualified priest to perform this jagia that the old animal will be reunited to a young body and the perfect result is achieved because this preparation is no more there, therefore these jaggy eyes are being stopped. So prophets…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 33:56

children.note:
From the purport, Maharaj recites the verse quoted in Caitanya-caritamrta naming five things forbidden in this age, and explains that sankirtana-yajna, the congregational chanting of Hare Krishna, replaces the old sacrifices.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:40 (auto-transcript): “So prophets quoted in this Chitama Pundis Loka Aswamedam Gavalambham Sanyasam Fala Paitrikam Dibarena Support Patim Kalu Panchar Ibarajayet In this age of Kali Five acts are forbidden The offering of a horse and sacrifice is forbidden The offering of a cow in sacrifice is…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 34:40

children.note:
Of the old sacrifices, all are forbidden; the chanting of the holy name is the one that still works today.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:41 (auto-transcript): “So the five things which are forbidden, they are forbidden, only one is still functioning. The instructions refer not to Krishna devotees who are preaching Krishna Consciousness.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 38:41

children.note:
The ban on sannyasa does not apply to devotees who preach Krishna consciousness. It is meant for ordinary people who take sannyasa only to fill their belly without preaching. — “It is meant for ordinary people who take sanyas”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:13 (auto-transcript): “The instructions refer not to Krishna devotees who are preaching Krishna Consciousness. It is meant for ordinary people who take sanyas only to fold their belly without preaching.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 39:13
