I said, what do you mean by leaving? Stay there now, you suffer. I will not stay until anything happens on my head. Let me go before you…”

In the elevated state devotees are fully convinced there is no greater gain for mind and senses than devotion to Krishna, and so are freed of all miseries.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:44 (auto-transcript): “But you know, in such an elevated state, devotees are fully convinced that there is no greater gain to be had for their mind and senses than devotion to Krishna. Thus liberated, they are freed of all miseries. To summarize, in Krishna's word, he whose mind is controlled and…”

Krishna assures success to one who controls the mind and strives by the right means. Without control one lives with the all-devouring enemy of BG 3.37, and at best faces a long, rocky road on which the mind must still be confronted.

Two questions: on past karma and progress, and on the mind's bad memories.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:23 (auto-transcript): “Thank you very much for the last class. Judith, one time you mentioned in your class that a person's level of devotional service can be judged by his karma, like the nature he has acquired. children.topic: Q1 · Does past karma cap progress?
children.note:
A devotee asks whether past karma limits how far one can go in devotional service. Maharaj says no — we can pass beyond it and rectify; that is why we are here.

🎙 Question from the floor at 42:23 (auto-transcript): “Thank you very much for the last class. 🎙 Maharaj at 46:20 (auto-transcript): “also asking me a question. We have so many people who are already married and often that after we become sannyasi. So one can say, oh, no, I didn't, I will not be brahmatari from that, so one needs to. That's a failure. If one has made a mistake, it doesn't mean you don't…”

Maharaj cites a Gosvami that Krishna appreciates souls who return from this world more than those who never left, because they came through a hard process of purification.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:45 (auto-transcript): “satan goswami said that when you get back to godhead christians that appreciate you more than those who are there. Why? He said we are new devotees. New devotees mean? He just came from there. From there. So he said, Krishna appreciates new devotees than the old devotees. All…”

In Vrindavan, Maharaj says, a register marks each Govardhana parikrama. Like class attendance, every programme, harinama and round of japa is recorded, so put in effort; Krishna may not yet reveal our position, but it is there.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:46 (auto-transcript): “oh it's recorded the whole place you have visited is counted and in brindavan there is a there is a a registrar if you if you do a goba dam parikama it will mark you one if you do two times in life you will mark it when i live in a body it will show this person have done goba…”

While chanting, the mind brings up past bad experiences rather than good ones. Why?

🎙 Question from the floor at 52:36 (auto-transcript): “your body is mine you have to say a chanting or do something in your mind you tell the same things unwillingly your chanting is so serious, it's not possible you don't know, you just bring them one thought yes and these things are the things that have passed in our journey,…”

Everything we have done, thought, seen and heard leaves residues in the subconscious mind, a storehouse of garbage. That is why controlling the mind is so important: a controlled mind is liberation.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:26 (auto-transcript): “Very good. Thank you. That is the nature of the mind. You know, everything that we do, there has residues of that. is stored in the mind, subconscious mind. Everything, all activities we have performed, what we have been thinking, what we have been doing, everything, what we…”

children.topic: Keep sweeping; don't mind the mind
children.note:
Practice is like sweeping a dirty room: dust rises, and if we drop the broom and run, it follows and settles. Agitation shows Krishna consciousness is working; let thoughts come and go without maintaining them, and one day they will finish. — “don't mind the mind”

maps.title: 30 Qualities · Class 06 · Non-violence (Part 1)

nodeData.topic: Class 06 · Non-violence (Part 1)
nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up ahimsa, explaining that for a Vaisnava non-violence means never obstructing anyone's spiritual life, so failing to share Krishna consciousness, harming oneself, or creating an unsafe devotional environment are all forms of violence. Through the story of Sanatana Gosvami he shows why suicide is never sanctioned, then surveys the violence of a low-grade Kali-yuga society. Questions bring out how a householder can earn honestly and why the soul is beyond happiness and distress. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: After reciting the verse, Maharaj turns to today's quality, ahimsa, which Srila Prabhupada translates as non-violence: not putting any living being into the threefold miseries.

Ahimsa is not only about other beings; Maharaj stresses that it also applies to the self, so we must not do violence to our own body and soul.

🎙 Maharaj at 07:00 (auto-transcript): “it is not other other entities that we we should not have we should not also do violence to the self ahimsa can be applied to oneself non-violence has long been associated with and identified as one of the qualities of spirituality.”

Pacifists define non-violence as not harming another person's body. Vaisnavas define it as conduct that does not interfere with another living being's spiritual development, which goes far beyond the physical.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:03 (auto-transcript): “And while non-violence is a duty of even the non-religious sections of society, the way that pacifists and non-devotes define non-violence is different than the Vaisnava's definition. Pacifists define non-violence as not harming another human's body. While Vaisnava's define…”
Maharaj notes that ahimsa also appears in the Gita's list of the qualities that make up real knowledge.

Following Srila Prabhupada, Maharaj says that not giving Krishna consciousness to others is violence, while vigorously sharing it makes one truly non-violent. — “If you are not preaching Krishna Consciousness, it is violence.”

🎙 Maharaj at 09:49 (auto-transcript): “Ahimsa means that one is not giving Krishna consciousness to others, that is violence. If you are not preaching Krishna Consciousness, it is violence. So it is beyond the body. So one is considered non-violence if we are very vigorously distributing Krishna Consciousness,…”

children.topic: A good devotee preaches by example

nodeData.topic: Class 07 · Non-violence (Part 2)
nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Continuing on ahimsa, Maharaj traces violence to envy and shows how it appears in society, in careless words and habits, and even in devotional service done in passion or ignorance. Non-violence begins by accepting Krishna as the proprietor, serving to please, and weighing every act by its effect on others. In questions he urges visiting hospitals to soften the heart and reads King Nrga's story as a warning against taking what belongs to brahmanas and Vaisnavas. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Class 08 · Celibacy
nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains brahmacarya as regulated sense life for every asrama, householders included, rooted in the fact that the duality of man and woman epitomises our bondage. The answer is not to wait for purity but to engage the senses in Krishna's service with changed consciousness, supported by culture, cleanliness, early marriage and a working varnasrama. Questions turn to weak standards among devotees and how parents' consciousness shapes their children. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: After ahimsa comes brahmacaryam. Maharaj reads Srila Prabhupada's word meaning, which covers continence for the unmarried and regulated life within marriage.

children.topic: For grhasthas as much as brahmacaris
children.note:
The definition is meant for householders too. Vedic culture designed everything perfectly; even the Bible says the marriage bed should be kept holy, by mutual agreement and at the proper time.

In other words, it is not only mentioned here for Brahmacharya. this is also for grihastas particularly here people don't mention and brahmachari here it is grihastas the prominent here the prominent meaning here prophet gave is brahmachari and grihastas…”

Many say they will marry because they cannot control their desires. Maharaj says that disqualifies them: without sense control, what kind of children will be born?

Disqualified. Qualification for anyone to get married is sense control. If your senses are not controlled and are…”

People complain about children nowadays, but the children come according to the combined consciousness of husband and wife. — “It is not the children, it is you, the parent.”

Stuffed and weighed down by the prasadam, Madhumangala could no longer cry for more, and lamented that Krishna did not have 365 sisters so there could be such a feast every day. Krishna only smiled.

Remembering the pastime, Maharaj compares the shining faces and big smiles he saw at a temple feast that Saturday with the near-empty temple on Sunday morning, and jokes that every day should be a feast day.

Among the thirty qualities, celibacy needs special attention; others like truthfulness one can simply do. Varnasrama prescribes different celibacy for each asrama, but Narada gives one underlying reason for all.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:28 (auto-transcript): “Of the 21 qualities, celibacy restricting the association between men and women is one that requires additional attention. It requires additional attention, like austerity, you can not do it. Silence, you can do it. Satyam, you can just do it. But celibacy requires additional…”

Until fully self-realised, a soul identifying with the body stays in duality, epitomised by man and woman, and can fall. The same root makes us see things as separate from Krishna and meant for our enjoyment.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:44 (auto-transcript): “As long as a living entity is not completely self-realized, as long as he is not independent the misconception of identifying for the body, which is nothing but a reflection of the original body and senses. He cannot be relieved of the conception of duality, which is…”

Unregulated bodily enjoyment between two conditioned souls is not liberating; it only keeps them conditioned. — “I am conditioned, you are conditioned.”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:35 (auto-transcript): “You are conditioned souls. I am conditioned, you are conditioned. What is our activities? Conditioning. Not a libertarian activity, it is a libertarian activity. It is more conditioning activity. We are already conditioned. And we are also continuing with the process of…”
Krishna identifies himself with sex life that does not go against religious principles; activity on the bodily platform binds, on the spiritual platform it liberates.

Being conditioned does not mean no one should marry; no scripture says so. As Rupa Gosvami teaches, devotional service is done with our present senses, engaged under regulation so they become purified.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:49 (auto-transcript): “Then, if one is conditioned, so yes, we are a conditioned soul, so that means that nobody should get married. Because we are conditioned, right? We should get married. No. No scripture says that. But we need to understand. What is that? Even though we are on the conditioned…”

The material senses are still engaged, but when the consciousness changes, the activity and the result change too, and one gets a spiritual result. — “The consciousness makes the difference.”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:41 (auto-transcript): “When the consciousness is changed, not when the consciousness is still on the condition level, we cannot get changed. That's the difference. That's the difference. The consciousness makes the difference. We are regulated. We allow the senses to be regulatedly engaged.…”

The tongue is purified by chanting and tasting prasadam, the eyes by seeing Krishna's form and his devotees. Yet one can look at the same deity and think only of stealing the gold.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:29 (auto-transcript): “the tongue is one of the senses conditioned when it is engaged in chanting the holy name and the glorious of krishna and then testing krishna's prasadhan becomes purified similarly other senses will also be equally engaged in krishna consciousness we are engaging our eyes and…”
We cannot wait for purity before serving; this verse describes bhakti as freedom from all designations by engaging the senses for the master of the senses.

For a serious devotee every activity is an offering to Krishna, so married life too must have a good purpose; otherwise it remains conditioned activity between two conditioned souls.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:56 (auto-transcript): “Now that holds on to all the activities that we do in Krishna consciousness. And we are repeatedly saying, a sincere, serious devotee is all our activities are offering to Krishna. So, this life is also an offering to Krishna. Therefore, it should be done with a good cause.…”

The rules on conduct between men and women apply to all asramas, with differences set by each order's duties. Srila Prabhupada calls restricting such association the basic principle of spiritual life: brahmacaris and sannyasis do not even think of women, while householders unite only for progeny.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:33 (auto-transcript): “The rule is that to regulate the general conduct between men and women are said to apply equally for Grehastas as they do for Bhannacharis, Bonaprastas and Sanyasis. They are, of course. Differences between them are implied by the duties inherent to the ashramas themselves.…”

Prabhupada gave ample instructions; the challenge is whether devotees formed by a permissive society will practise them. How are the children born in this movement doing?

🎙 Maharaj at 39:15 (auto-transcript): “The challenge is whether devotees who are born to race in and molded by a sexually or by permissive society are willing to put those instructions to practice. How are our children doing? Our children born in this movement, how are they doing? Ready? They will keep these…”

Maharaj recalls a letter in a magazine from a girl who was pregnant but did not know which of several boys was responsible, and imagines devotees resorting to DNA tests. — “Is it not a shame?”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:53 (auto-transcript): “I remember a few years ago in BTG magazine. I saw in the BTG magazine a girl. Today I am confirmed pregnant. But I don't know which of the boy is here, he's responsible. What does that mean? What does it mean? All the men have the same. All the men have the same.”
Narada's comparison of man and woman to butter and fire is cited to show why even close relatives avoid being alone together, and why regular study of scripture is essential.

These are heavy cultural standards, the opposite of today, where a chaste girl of eighteen is mocked when she should be honoured.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:53 (auto-transcript): “Quite a cultural seat. See that? It's a heavy cultural seat. Why? Because in the ways... The opposite of what is there. Yes. Yes. You are considered Bush girl. children.note:
People say the young are too young to marry, never too young for sex, which Maharaj calls demonic. In the past marriages were arranged early and husbands protected their wives.

children.topic: Marriages built on a bad foundation
children.note:
Many marriages fail because couples married only after being caught in illicit relations. Character and taste should be checked for compatibility, or unwanted children result, and devotee children do not stay devotees.

nodeData.topic: Class 09 · Charity
nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj presents charity as a universal and compulsory duty that purifies even saints, and widens it beyond money to giving knowledge, the holy name, a phone call or a smile. He discusses Srila Prabhupada's fifty-percent standard, the importance of giving to those who use everything in Krishna's service, and the three modes of charity, with Bali Maharaja as the ideal. In questions he explains that the giver never lacks and that 'charity' that burdens the receiver is no charity. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: In text 8 the quality is giving in charity, which Srila Prabhupada's word meaning puts at at least fifty percent of one's income.

Charity is the varnasrama quality with worldwide recognition. In the past kings and merchants built wells, gardens and rest houses; today there are many foundations, and though not always free of motive, giving purifies the donor.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:40 (auto-transcript): “Charity is one characteristic of Narasana Dharma that has worldwide recognition and it's a very nice topic also because it has different This is the other Sama Srim, the Bhagavad Gita. Draw out in one world fine wells, gardens, dharma showers, and orchards.”
Krishna says sacrifice, charity and austerity are never to be abandoned. Maharaj has the room repeat the Sanskrit and stresses that charity is compulsory.

Charity is so powerful that it purifies even great souls. — “Charity purifies even saints.”

🎙 Maharaj at 15:48 (auto-transcript): “It is the problem. Charity purifies even saints. Even saints. It is so powerful. The people who say, I have to give up. You should not be giving up. should not be given up. Never. No, they are German. Act of sacrifice, charity and penance are not to be given up. They must be…”
In Gita chapter 17 Krishna grades charity in goodness, passion and ignorance, and there is also transcendental charity.

The tradition survives, but misunderstood and misapplied; few know what charity is or how it should be given, so it is often done in a dangerous way.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:50 (auto-transcript): “Misunderstood, misapplied. This day we see charity wrongly done. Wrongly, wrongly. Doing charity in a very wrong way, a very dangerous way. Dangerous way, charity. Although it is very powerful, it should have been given up, but not many people know what is charity and how…”

Krishna says the twice-born must perform sacrifice, study and charity for purification. Since devotees are initiated as twice-born, the principle extends to everyone: charity is a universal duty.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:29 (auto-transcript): “Charity reinforces itself. It reinforced, charity is composed for the three higher orders of society and for great aspects. Krishna says, Jiyadhyayana Dhanani Saravesam Chadi Janmanam Prati Grahuda Pa Namcha Brahmana Shaiva Yajanam Twice born men, parents, satriyas and voices…”

Maharaj asks the room what can be given: grains, land, houses, fruits, a daughter in marriage.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:38 (auto-transcript): “That means, especially human beings. Human beings, who? you? She gives charity. It depends on your level. House, school grains, land, houses, fruits. Yes, giving in daughter. Yes, give daughter and charity.”

All material gifts stay here, but knowledge takes us out of this world, so giving books is the highest charity. — “To give knowledge, that is the highest.”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:31 (auto-transcript): “What else? Don't end. What else? Book distribution. What is that? Book distribution is what? Giving someone knowledge, what is it? Charity thing? Yes. To give knowledge, that is the highest. Of all the things you mentioned, knowledge is the best. Everything you mention now,…”

children.topic: A call, a smile, a visit
children.note:
Calling a devotee you have not seen, making someone smile, and actually visiting and serving the sick, not merely saying 'I pray for you', are charity that costs nothing. — “Make someone smile, to make a devotee smile especially.”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:31 (auto-transcript): “if you don't see a devotee and you call a devotee what is that you call a devotee I'm not saying what is it which we don't do which will is charity called a devotee to see how he's doing what she's doing it is what we're making someone to smile put smile someone's face what…”

Chanting in the street, when someone hears the mantra or receives the holy name, is charity too. So everyone can give.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:19 (auto-transcript): “Chanting her, a Christian mantra in the street. Someone sees you, just seeing you here in the street, Terminate the person going to her. She says, see you do her right now. A giving holy name? Yes. Charity. So a variety of charity. So everyone has to give charity. Everyone.…”

In India people leave pots of clean water by the road for travellers, and trees are planted along roads. Trees give oxygen and support life, yet are cut down; only trees that cause distress should be avoided.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:57 (auto-transcript): “In India, you see, people, they will put a pot of water by the roadside. So people are walking somewhere like this very hard. Free water is there, very common, natural. You volunteer, just volunteer to drink, just keep water for you to drink. You will test it, put water…”

A devotee mentions the mango trees planted in colonial times; Maharaj remarks that people used their independence to cut down the good things left for them.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:08 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj, in the past, the colonial people, they planted a lot of mango trees. Because they are better, civilized. No, there are people who cut them down, plant them, and they don't do it. That is your independence. That is your independence. Don't rule ourselves. Don't rule…”

children.topic: A nightly notebook of good deeds
children.note:
Before sleeping, check: what good did I do for someone today? Did I call someone, make someone smile, give a small gift? Maharaj admits it is good advice that few follow.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:11 (auto-transcript): “Every day look and see what good have you done to somebody today, before you sleep. How many of us do that? It's good, but who will do? Who will hear? Every day we look at my notebook. What good have I done to someone today? Did I check on someone? Did I call the person? Did…”

Money has its role, but wishing someone well from a sweet heart is worth more. A person of character easily puts a smile on others' faces; one chasing only money forgets. — “many things money cannot do, but character can do them.”

🎙 Maharaj at 30:10 (auto-transcript): “You don't need to give money to make someone happy. It's not the money that makes someone happy. Materially, it is there. It has a significant role to play. But to wish someone good from their sweet heart is more than the money. So there are some things money cannot do, many…”

Devotees are by nature givers of knowledge, the name and preaching. Even the tilaka on our forehead purifies those who see it, reminding them of Vishnu, Brahma, Shiva and Tulasi Devi.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:16 (auto-transcript): “So as God is a voice nervous, we are literally charity givers. So we have to give charity. Distributing knowledge, the holy name, preaching. Even when you move in, you don't see your tillap on your face, you get purified. Because when you see the forehead, Lord Vishnu, Lord…”

Some argue that sannyasis and liberated souls need not give, but Krishna says even they are purified by charity; having received gifts, they should give something back.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:11 (auto-transcript): “The Bhagavad Gita says that some sages will argue that one of Pratts, Sanyasis, and Liberated souls need not give charity. However, Krishna's opinion is that even they are purified by an act of charity. Therefore, since they are all recipients of gifts, this gray soul should…”

Prabhupada engaged brahmacaris and brahmacarinis in giving transcendental literature in exchange for donations and in distributing prasadam.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:45 (auto-transcript): “and see brahmacharis live solely for the benefit of their guru we see from the purpose example how the spiritual master engages his disciples in charity and it's come brahmacharis brahmacharinis learn to give the gift of transcendental in exchange for charitable donation and…”

Giving is compulsory unless one does not want spiritual progress. — “If you want to make advancement, give charity.”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:10 (auto-transcript): “to distribute prosada. Everyone should give charity. Giving charity is for everyone and it is compulsory, except you don't want advancement. If you don't want advancement, then it is not compulsory for you. If you want to make advancement, give charity. in the military so…”

The question could fill a book. Maharaj acts out the objections: from a salary of 100,000, half is gone on school fees, bills and transport in two weeks; why belong to such an organisation, what benefit am I getting?

🎙 Maharaj at 34:42 (auto-transcript): “while that controversial question is short the answer could form a book the moment you say 50% how do you feel you know discussing this is a book 50% I'm I'm getting 100,000, I'll get 50%. They remain only 50,000. School fees, light bills, transportation to the office.…”

Prabhupada's most common answer is fifty percent, with variations on either side. For wage earners already committed it may be hard; affluent professionals can meet it more easily.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:18 (auto-transcript): “And then there are variations on either side of that medium. On one side is at least 50%, and the other up to 50%. Because the proper expectation that one given, some percentage of income is not. Objective fashion will say that while Shilapapad was accommodating, he…”

children.topic: Young earners: plan from day one
children.note:
Young devotees starting a career, before mortgages, can set aside half their income for Krishna from their first salary and live on the rest.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:28 (auto-transcript): “However, those who are affluent, especially those young devotees who are looking for a career, and have not yet made financial commitment to mortgages and so forth, who do well to plan how they can meet that formula. It's difficult for a salaried earner, it's only good for…”

The plan rests on faith that doing right brings the right result; such faithful souls are assured spiritual and material prosperity.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:04 (auto-transcript): “The plan has to be based on the implicit fact that doing what is right, he will give a right result. It means that from day one of their employment, a young devotee sets aside half of their income for Christian service and only lives on the other half. Those faithful souls…”

children.topic: To whom, and in what mode
children.note:
The best recipient is Krishna, and Prabhupada established ISKCON as his representative. Full-time members may receive charity on the understanding that all of it goes to Krishna's service, which Maharaj says is not always so.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:42 (auto-transcript): “But if you do it, to whom should one give? When and how? The best person to give is to Krishna, so that Prabhupada has established ISKCON as Krishna's representative. Because ISKCON's mission is to further Krishna's service. Devotees who are full-time representatives of the…”

Scripture recommends giving to pure devotees who use every penny for Krishna; the recipient's purity determines the reward.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:33 (auto-transcript): “Scriptures therefore recommend that charity be given to first-class transcendentalists because they will fully utilize every penny they receive in Krishna's service. Charities will be given to first-class transcendentalists. First-class, pure devotee. According to the purity…”

Giving to senior devotees who use it for themselves or private projects was not Prabhupada's vision; very few can rightly accept charity. Give to those serving the mission of Krishna consciousness.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:35 (auto-transcript): “Nowadays, it has become fashionable to give donations to senior devotees who are the provisional, that they do not use the form for school, but for themselves or their project. That was certainly not Shlapapa's vision of charity. He wants that only very few brahmanas can…”

Charity in goodness is authorised, while that in passion and ignorance wastes money and energy. Householders are protected by their donations, raised by building temples, and blessed with love of God by supporting Caitanya Mahaprabhu's mission.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:16 (auto-transcript): “When charity is not of such a transcendental nature, but is subject to the mode of nature, Then time, place, and passion become governing factors. And while charity in goodness is authorized, that impassion and ignorance is a voice of money, time, and energy, the aggregate of…”

Among the varnas only pure brahmanas may accept charity, and ksatriyas are forbidden even in emergency; for those in the retired order living on alms it is compulsory.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:45 (auto-transcript): “As there are guidelines for giving charity, there are guidelines for accepting it. Among the four others, only pure Brahmanas may accept charity. On the other hand, for Banapastas living by charity, which quickly phase one from illusion, is compulsory. Charity may be taken…”

Bali Maharaja is the ultimate example of charity. His words, that many die fearlessly in battle but rarely does one get the chance to give everything faithfully to a saintly person, are worth remembering.

Five questions on what to give, the right mood of service, the giver's welfare, and charity done badly.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:23 (auto-transcript): “Comment? Krishna. The Brahmanas or the wise ones, they give charity by giving out knowledge. Yes. But I also read sometimes that when they have been giving charities by chastriyas also, maybe like donations like goods and stuff like this, they also tend to also give it”

children.topic: Q1 · Is knowledge the only gift?
children.note:
Brahmanas give knowledge, but may they also give goods? Yes: whatever we have can be given, and Prabhupada would pass a gift on to another devotee after a few days so both giver and receiver were happy.

🎙 Question from the floor at 50:43 (auto-transcript): “The Brahmanas or the wise ones, they give charity by giving out knowledge. Yes. But I also read sometimes that when they have been giving charities by chastriyas also, maybe like donations like goods and stuff like this, they also tend to also give it out to other people too.…”

children.topic: Q2 · Helping in the proper mood
children.note:
How can we serve others, even juniors, without pride or offence?

🎙 Question from the floor at 51:49 (auto-transcript): “Yes, my second question. You mentioned that we should have a group and a pen, that we are able to dictate what good we are doing for some people. I wanted to ask, how do we do this also in the proper mood? because you know like there's something like seniority should not do…”

Not 'he is useless, let me help him', but 'this is my fortunate chance', as shown by Isvara Puri's service to his guru.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:21 (auto-transcript): “The same who can apply it, when I read the puri, he's very puri, demonstrating to show the way. He's very puri, he was not thinking, my god is incapable, let me help him, he's useless, whatever he can exist. You were not thinking, ah, this is my chance, I'm fully fortunate…”

children.topic: Q3 · Why do some givers struggle?
children.note:
Some give, then seem to suffer and reduce their giving. How does Krishna bless the giver so one can keep giving?

🎙 Question from the floor at 56:20 (auto-transcript): “Today's topic is very interesting, how they have found out the charity for the teacher and the sacrifice they do not. Then there is a contribution of wisdom. I observe that when one gives charity irrespective of the percentage, and you now get the Krishna blessing, you will…”

Krishna is in the heart and sees everything. Give heartily and keep faith; even materially the giver never lacks, so how could Krishna not reciprocate? — “So if you do the right thing, you will never be left alone.”

🎙 Maharaj at 57:41 (auto-transcript): “If Krishna is right there in the heart with us and he's seeing everyone, everyone perfectly, completely, knows everyone completely. We don't even know, I said, Krishna knows all completely. So if you do the right thing, you will never be left alone. You cannot give and then…”

Wealthy visitors give no donation but drop off used clothes and leftovers that the temple must clear away. Is that charity?

🎙 Question from the floor at 59:07 (auto-transcript): “So we are talking about 50% and then we talk about the affordability, okay whatever you can afford you should give. But what I see practically here is like multi-millionaires. People come here, they have a temple. They don't come for Darshan, generally Indians. They don't put…”

Charity should relieve the receiver's distress, not add a burden. Maharaj recalls asking for help with a kitchen problem and being given something he never asked for, and people made to queue for hours in the sun for a small handout. — “Charity is to relieve you from the distress you have.”

🎙 Maharaj at 60:07 (auto-transcript): “That is not charity. Charity is to relieve you from the distress you have. That is not charity. Not to put you in anxiety. In the beginning I will say something. When people give charity that you will be angry also. Like what he is saying. He gives you a game because you…”

Charity in goodness purifies; charity in passion and ignorance, mixed with offence and foolishness, brings distress and keeps one in darkness. That is why scripture explains how to give.

🎙 Question from the floor at 66:02 (auto-transcript): “Master, the three kinds of charity, is there any blessing like this in the last week, or is there any blessing in the last week, or is there any blessing in the last week, like with you, or is there any blessing you need, good, any blessing among, inside you? Yes, if you do…”

maps.title: 30 Qualities · Class 10 · Reading the Scriptures

nodeData.topic: Class 10 · Reading the Scriptures
nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj presents svadhyaya, regular study of scripture, as a sacrifice no one is exempt from: without it life runs on whim, and Krishna consciousness loses its meaning. He contrasts real hearing, as in Rukmini, Pariksit and Kulasekhara, with pretending to read, and shows that scripture stays ever fresh, captures Krishna in the heart and makes one humble, not proud. He urges families to read together and closes with a practical method of prayerful reading. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Still in text 8, today's quality is svadhyaya. Srila Prabhupada explains it as reading the Gita, Bhagavatam, Ramayana and Mahabharata, as an austerity for purification.

Prabhupada encouraged people outside Vedic culture to read the Bible or Koran regularly. Many in the room came through the Bible, which shows how important such reading is.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:54 (auto-transcript): “Srila Prabhupada says to read Vedic literature, to understand Vedic literature, to act according to the direction of the Vedic literature. This is called Swadhyaya Jagia and in elaborating on Swadhyaya as one of the 21 qualities, Lakhapat prescribed the scriptures to be read…”
Krishna lists study of the Vedas among the sacrifices. Anyone who considers himself human must follow such regulated activities; reading scripture is a yajna for purification.

Reading scripture appears twice in Narada's list of qualities. It is both a religious and a devotional practice, without which no one can be religious or reach pure devotion.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:02 (auto-transcript): “so Nadamuni also mentioned that here sacrifice reading scripture is mentioned twice in the list of 32 qualities to be cultivated and acquired by all human beings Nadamuni mentioned it twice it is both a religious and devotional practice without reading scripture no one can be…”

Scripture shows what is right and wrong and what one's duties are. Without it life is speculation and whim, and Krishna says such a person fails in all he attempts.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:47 (auto-transcript): “no one is exempt from reading scripture by reading scripture one will know what is right what is wrong and what one's occupational and spiritual duties are and can those integrate those values into one's life without reading scripture one's life is based on speculation and…”

Getting behind the wheel without knowing how to drive ends in hospital. Maharaj recalls his college motor-engineering teacher's first rule: press the clutch before starting. Not reading scripture is the same: life full of disaster. — “Your Krishna consciousness will not be meaningful.”

🎙 Maharaj at 13:51 (auto-transcript): “Everybody know the result? Go to go to go to hospital. Yes. You don't know how to drive. You enter the car and spark it. Hospital. Not only you go to the hospital. Whoever is the government, right? In the college, our motor engineering teacher, the first thing he taught us is,”

A devotee who does not read can still succeed with one fortunate quality, real hearing, which Maharaj says many lack. Hearing means the mind never leaves what it has heard about Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:50 (auto-transcript): “Except you have a very fortunate quality. What is that? Hearing. Which I have seen his contemporaries, many his contemporaries doesn't have. We don't hear. We don't hear. Hearing is different. We have spoken about it. Hearing is different. What do we say here? Different. When…”

Hearing about Krishna, Rukmini developed an ever-increasing longing for him as her husband and vowed to continue her austerity into the next life if needed.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:30 (auto-transcript): “When Devi heard about Krishna, what happened? She developed an unquenchable taste to have Krishna, as her husband. Unquenchable taste. The taste to have Krishna increases every moment. And she vowed, If my austerity is not sufficient to have Krishna this lifetime, no problem.…”

children.topic: Pariksit: Krishna planted in my heart
children.note:
Maharaja Pariksit tells Sukadeva Gosvami that he has worked a miracle, planting Krishna in his heart, and it was done by hearing.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:08 (auto-transcript): “Parikshin Maharaj, he taught his spiritual master, you have done miracles, you planted Krishna in my heart. How did he do that? Hearing. Hearing? Hearing. That's what he means by hearing. When they say someone has heard, that's what he means. The mind can never go away from…”

King Kulasekhara, author of the Mukunda-mala-stotra, heard his priest describe Lord Ramacandra's battle with Ravana, leapt from his throne and led his army into the sea to help. The priest saved them by announcing that the battle was over and Ravana killed.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:57 (auto-transcript): “Kula Shakra Maharaj. Kula Shakra Maharaj. He sang that song, we called him Mukunda Malashtutra. He was hearing from his priest. He was sitting on his throne. And the priest was narrating the pastor of Ramachand. He jumped down from the Asama. He came down from the Asama,…”
Krishna warns that one who sets aside scriptural direction and acts on whim attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme goal.

Prabhupada himself lamented that devotees do not read regularly. Vaisnava tradition presents scripture through drama, poetry, song and dance so it penetrates; Maharaj mentions a drama devotees made about his own life.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:29 (auto-transcript): “However, Vaishitama tradition offers the study of this aforementioned transcendental literature, not just in book form, but in dogmatic performance. poetry, recitation, dance and song. The idea is that our entire cultural life should embody and not diverge from the histories…”

Regulated devotion means scheduling priorities, so reading always finds a place in a competent devotee's day. Prabhupada said to read again and again even without understanding; repetition brings understanding. — “We should read, it is compulsory to read.”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:59 (auto-transcript): “Varnasham is about Vaidhi Bhakti, regulated devotional service. One of the implications of regulation is that devotees prioritise their duties and schedule their time to facilitate those priorities. Since reading literature is a high priority, it always finds its way into the…”

Reading takes repetition, so it is an austerity, and it means giving up the mentality of cheating ourselves.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:01 (auto-transcript): “it's difficult so to understand it requires a reputation therefore it's an austerity instead of us to go and play games with a cell phone do what you say do play games play games with it and sometimes they even go to a very pervasive one going to What do you call it? Blue?…”

Instead of reading we play games on our phones, or worse, watch pornography. Sacrificing these is the austerity of svadhyaya.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:10 (auto-transcript): “instead of us to go and play games with a cell phone do what you say do play games play games with it and sometimes they even go to a very pervasive one going to What do you call it? Blue? Yeah, in a movie. Very, very dangerous. You can't become a devotee. You cannot be a…”

Pretending to read deceives neither Krishna nor the guru, only oneself. Others may sympathise when someone cheats you, but no one sympathises with one who cheats himself. — “Your head will be empty.”

🎙 Maharaj at 26:54 (auto-transcript): “up this mentality of cheating ourselves. Yes, we're cheating ourselves. If you're hiding yourself under the book until you're reading. When you see you say you're reading but you're not reading what I'm doing again. Who is who is deceived? Who is deceived? Krishna? The guru?…”

Bhaktivinoda Thakura describes four misfortunes; one is asat-trsna, a taste for temporary things: bodily pleasure, heaven, mundane films and idle talk. Maya hides their danger, so scripture is needed to show what to do and how.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:09 (auto-transcript): “So she said, the Bhagavad Gita Nhat Kaur had described the Bhagavad Gita Maha Prabhu's word. Do daivam, a misfortune. He said there are four, and they all have subdivisions. Principally, there are four misfortunes. One is Asat-Trishna. Trishna, not Krishna. Trish means taste.…”

Even eating must be done rightly: eaten with anxiety, food becomes poison and does not nourish. Maharaj jokes that this is why he stays tiny, and explains that bon appetit means eat without tension. — “That is not food, this is poison.”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:50 (auto-transcript): “Even as simple as eating, if you don't know how to eat, the food becomes poison, do you not? You are eating with anxiety. That is not food, this is poison. People are eating always like this. They would remain skinny and tiny like me. You will not be fresh. Yes. You will not…”

The fruit of reading and hearing is devotion to Krishna, constant remembrance of him and seeing everything in relation to him. Without reading we cannot remember Krishna or understand how to serve him.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:27 (auto-transcript): “The result of such reading, hearing, and seeing of scripture is to awaken devotion to Krishna, to always think of Him, and to learn to see everything in relation to Him. Krishna advises Arjuna that while performing one's prescribed duty, one should think of Him, and such…”

Reading the same books seems boring only to those who do not know how to read and have no taste. Cultivating prayerful reading develops the taste.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:18 (auto-transcript): “Yes, it is boring for those who don't know how to read and for one who doesn't have taste. therefore it is very important for us to also learn how to read we must cultivate or develop the attitude of prayerful reading prayerful reading will help us to develop tests for…”

children.topic: The devotee lured by a job
children.note:
On sankirtana a man flattered a devotee's intelligence and offered him a manager's post. The devotee left the temple boasting, but the man had travelled and there was no job, and shame kept him from returning. Without reading, small temptations defeat us.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:38 (auto-transcript): “On Sankitan, some, Krishna in Power Song, Maya, agents, tell devotees, hey my friend, just look at your intelligence. I will give you a managing position in my company. why are you wasting your time like this for this intelligence just how brilliant you are you're wasting it…”

Asked to teach a Bhagavatam course in India, Maharaj requested the sections in advance to read them again. Organisers laughed since he teaches them every year, but each year brings new realisation; Krishna's topics grow fresher with every reading. — “It's the same thing, but different realization.”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:35 (auto-transcript): “This year I was going to, I was requested to teach in Bhagavatam, one time course in India. So the teacher Rappavu told them that I want the section you want me to teach, because I have to read them because you have been teaching this thing for years. What are you reading…”

An illiterate brahmana, ordered by his guru to read the Gita daily, sat holding it, even upside down, while scholars laughed. Caitanya Mahaprabhu asked why he was in ecstasy; he said he was only following his guru's order.

The brahmana wept because he saw the Supreme Controller of all controlled by his devotee's love, driving Arjuna's chariot and tending his horses. Maharaj adds how the Pandavas were praised for holding Krishna under their control.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:41 (auto-transcript): “you are very static i can see because you are getting something from the gita i say yes when i'm when look you say just just see to see the supreme personality of godhead supreme personality of godhead is a supreme controller of the whole world including great powerful person…”

Reading under the guidance of brahmanas, Vaisnavas and the spiritual master keeps one on course socially and spiritually, raises one to pure devotion and finally to liberation.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:12 (auto-transcript): “wonderful, this is wonderful, this is amazing, those by reading scripture under the guidance of Gramanas, Vaisnavas or the spiritual master, one can very easily chat a true cause in both the social and spiritual orders and avoid the pitfalls of conditional life thus one is…”
Vyasadeva says that for those who hear submissively, the Lord is at once established in the heart. Maharaj has the room repeat 'avarudhyate': devotees lock Krishna in their hearts.

Mother Sarasvati told Kesava Kasmiri that her mantra was not for conquering scholars but for meeting the Lord. Study is for becoming a devotee; even busy householders should know scripture well enough to detect speculation.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:50 (auto-transcript): “yes it should be noted that reading scripture is not just about becoming learned it is not becoming a pondid that is not saraswati told the keshava kashmiri the purpose of the mantra I gave you is not to become a divijaya, a conqueror of the directions of the scriptures and…”
The verse describes the wise as both learned and gentle, seeing all beings equally. One made proud by study has learned only the alphabet. — “a knowledgeable person is not proud”

If Krishna is the centre of family life, the family should sit together morning and evening to read, not each member alone with a phone or computer. Commodities have divided the community.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:16 (auto-transcript): “meant to be the center of family life hearing about him collectively as a family function is essential we should sit together as a family and hear the scriptures a wife husband children sit together and read the scripture not their son is in that room with the computer the…”

Children absorb whatever they hear and see; give them devotee books and hide the phones. Lectures stream endlessly online, yet our appetite turns to garbage. The acaryas' blessings wait in their writings; do nothing we will regret tomorrow. Krishna consciousness is as much about reading books as distributing them.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:38 (auto-transcript): “with material desires rather than attachment to krishna you know and hide away the cell phone and soft food and garbage garbage is known to the unlimited lectures now that they use the word stream is constantly flowing go to youtube they say stream the stream of lectures and the”

One question on the technique of prayerful reading.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:28 (auto-transcript): “Slavodaya, did you mention about prayerful reading? Yes, prayerful reading. Slavodaya, what is the technique to develop a taste about reading? Yeah, very good. Thank you. Prayer for reading. Prayer for reading. What is the techniques for prayer for reading? Select a quieted…”

What technique develops a taste for reading?

🎙 Question from the floor at 56:34 (auto-transcript): “Slavodaya, what is the technique to develop a taste about reading? Yeah, very good. Thank you. Prayer for reading. Prayer for reading. What is the techniques for prayer for reading? Select a quieted place. Select a quieted place. Not in the middle of Kiritan. That is a…”

Choose a quiet place, not in the middle of kirtan; sit alone or with an interested companion, upright and comfortable but not so comfortable that you fall asleep.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:52 (auto-transcript): “Select a quieted place. Select a quieted place. Not in the middle of Kiritan. That is a quieted place. Sit alone. Or when someone else is not going to talk to you. and that is if you have a companion who is also interested in this empty so a quiet place you sit alone and if…”

Pick a subject you are eager to understand, such as anger, and find where the Gita and Bhagavatam discuss it, like the gates to hell in chapter 16. Interest keeps you awake.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:15 (auto-transcript): “Select a topic that you like to hear. Select a topic. So, I want to hear something about anger. Select that. And then start reading something about anger. Because you want to know the danger of anger. So, we know the reason why I should not be angry. So we selected that…”

Treat reading as your communication time with Krishna, like a private phone call where you want no one else present, so that you focus.

🎙 Maharaj at 59:35 (auto-transcript): “So, the next thing you understand is, I want to communicate with God, with Krishna. It's my communication period. Communication time, I want to communicate. You want to have a special phone call, no? You don't want somebody else every day with you. See that? You want to have…”

Read the verse, then look in the purport for philosophy, example, history and similar verses elsewhere in the Bhagavatam.

🎙 Maharaj at 60:35 (auto-transcript): “When you read the verse, in the pop-up, there are four things inside. There are four things in the pop-up. Improper to put something in there. What is the philosophy in the proper part about anger? What is the philosophy? You see philosophy? Anger is this, this, this, this.…”

Notice the personalities Prabhupada quotes in the purport and picture yourself sitting with them to hear Krishna. Reading this way makes one very strong. — “If you read like this, you become very strong.”

🎙 Maharaj at 61:31 (auto-transcript): “and you also see that in that purport the prophet has quoted himself as number one because no not number one christian who is supposed to be number one and proper is there and he has put our chariars inside the purport so check family personalities on that purport that then…”

maps.title: 30 Qualities · Class 11 · Control of the Senses (2): Taming the Mind

nodeData.topic: Class 11 · Control of the Senses (2): Taming the Mind
nodeData.note: SB 7.11.8–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up sama and dama together, saying sense control must begin with the mind, because a mind left to run whimsically keeps us slaves of the senses. Drawing on Bhagavad-gita chapter 6, he teaches sincerity, a carefully planned life with no spare time, practice and detachment, and above all hearing Krishna's pastimes, which brings devotion, experience of Krishna and detachment together, like eating brings satisfaction, nourishment and relief from hunger. Questions turn to why worldly leaders are called dangerous and whether the struggle with the mind lasts forever. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Today's qualities are sama and dama. Maharaj explains sama as not allowing the mind to act whimsically, and presents mind and sense control together because they cannot be separated.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:16 (auto-transcript): “So today we are looking at Samur, Samur. Samur, proper translated. Samur as control of the mind, not allowing the mind to act whimsically. Should allow the mind to act whimsically. This is the proper translation. So, we are looking at controlling the mind and controlling the…”

Asked where sense control should begin, the answer is the mind: it is the workshop where all the other senses show their abilities, so controlling them while the mind runs free still leaves us in trouble. — “If we want to control the senses, we should start controlling the mind.”

🎙 Maharaj at 11:04 (auto-transcript): “if we want to control the senses, where should we start? Which of the senses should we start? The mind. If we want to control the senses, we should start controlling the mind. if the mind is not controlled but other senses are controlled they are still in trouble all the…”
Intelligence should rule the mind, but practical experience, and Arjuna's words in Gita chapter 6, show the mind dominating the intelligence.

Among the thirty qualities some weigh more than others; mind and sense control is indispensable, because one must first become a good person to become a good devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:20 (auto-transcript): “qualities some are more important than others control the mind and senses is a it's a practice that is indispensable and become a good person and a good devotee we have to become a good person then we can become a good devotee while the money list control of the mind and…”

Yogis go to the forest to master mind and senses; such mastery is liberation. Without it, Maharaj says, Prabhupada calls us slaves, and a slave has no independence.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:30 (auto-transcript): “The senses will be put under control. That is the whole purpose for spiritual life. See, the yogis are going to the forest to do what? To control the mind, to control the senses. If the senses and mind are controlled, then you can be a perfect yogi. can be a master of the…”

We talk of independence while every sense pushes us at every moment. Maharaj asks which sense is not pushing us; only ignorance makes us think we are free.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:25 (auto-transcript): “So while we are fooling ourselves in this material where we talk of independence and the senses are our control what are we talking what is independence when at every moment we are already addicted to our senses what is independent independent to what independence of our…”

Maharaj points to one whose senses are in his grip: he does what he chooses, and that alone is independence, not being controlled every moment by the senses.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:54 (auto-transcript): “Right? Hanuman does not chant that mantra. Hanuman does not chant the mantra. So therefore, it is only him who is independent, because his senses are under his grip. What he likes, he do. That's independence. Not someone who is controlled at any moment, any moment, every…”

Eyes, nose, tongue, ears and mind all demand at once, and we follow helplessly. Like someone pricked with a pin, only a dead body would not react. — “All of them are demanding.”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:27 (auto-transcript): “But in all directions, why are we restless? What makes someone restless? What is restlessness? The senses are not controlled. Restlessness. The eye is demanding. The nose is demanding. The tongue is demanding. The ear is demanding. The mind is demanding. All of them are…”
Maharaj calls this verse an assignment Krishna gives everyone: before leaving this body, learn to tolerate the push of the senses, desire and anger, and so be happy in this world.

children.topic: The world says: if it feels good
children.note:
No institution teaches sense control; the message everywhere is to do whatever feels good, whatever the harm. Maharaj calls this demonic.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:16 (auto-transcript): “Where is organization teaching you how to control the senses? Whatever makes you feel good, license. Anything that makes you feel good, do it. Even if it's going to put water or hair, it doesn't matter. Provided you feel good, do it. Demonic, His Holiness Baptista Mara said,…”

children.topic: Check first: does it benefit others?
children.note:
Quoting a senior Vaisnava, Maharaj gives a test before any act: will it benefit others, or put them in anxiety? What helps only me is not good; what benefits everyone is good, and that is Krishna consciousness. — “Anything which is beneficial for everyone is good.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:55 (auto-transcript): “Opposite. Before you do anything, before you do anything, check. Will this benefit other people apart from myself? Will the teacher go to do now, will it benefit others? You're going to put others on anxiety. If the answer is no, don't, even if you feel, don't, we are…”

Reading teachings drawn from Gita chapter 6, Maharaj stresses that controlling the mind matters most: once it is controlled, the senses follow automatically.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:28 (auto-transcript): “So Krishna is saying, before we quit this body, let us practice to control all these senses. become a happy person. Many books have been written on these topics but the most concise and authoritative is the Bhagavad Gita. We have therefore extracted the teachings of the sixth…”

Senses may be regulated by devotional routine while the subtle mind wanders. Such mechanical service, if not upgraded, can lead to falling down.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:23 (auto-transcript): “Even if the gross senses are regulated by art of devotion, the subtle mind may remain distracted and unengaged. This is called mechanical service. And if not upgraded, such devotion will lead to fall down and the abandonment of religious principles. On the other hand, if the…”

Control begins with sincerity, determination and faith. Maharaj explains sincerity as honestly admitting that we do not control our mind and senses, so the work can start without pretence.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:08 (auto-transcript): “What is sincerity? What sincerity has to do with control of your mind and senses? Sincerity, what does it do? Why is it? The mind is like a slippery fish, hard to hold. Its handler is intelligence, strengthened by deep study and the conviction that the mind can be tamed. — “The mind is like that, slippery fish.”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:36 (auto-transcript): “Pretend. This is what I want to do. Let me just face it. Yes. Particle mind control. Particle mind control. Like a slippery fish. Some person has a robot. No more fish. Fish. Sleepy. You see what? You have a slippery fish. When you hold it. Black one, not black one. Sleepy.…”

children.topic: Prahlada: untamed senses lead to darkness
children.note: Why bother controlling the mind? Maharaj answers with Prahlada Maharaja's words that those whose senses are untamed enter darkness; given freedom, the senses take us to hell.

children.topic: An enemy: never drop your guard
children.note:
The untamed mind is an enemy, and in a fight the enemy can come from any direction, so we stay careful at all times.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:18 (auto-transcript): “Since the untimed mind is a foe, enemy. Right? It's an enemy. One can never let down one's guard to be careful. To be careful. This is sincerity. If you are fighting, you have to be careful. The enemy can come in any direction. This was said like that. Behold! Comet, yes,…”

A devotee's life should be so carefully regulated that the mind cannot wander even for a moment. This is discipline: study the scriptures and leave no spare time.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:15 (auto-transcript): “From the practical point of view, that means a devotee's life should be so carefully regulated that the mind cannot digress for a moment. We should be so careful, regulating the mind, so that the mind cannot digress for a moment. Instead, it remains constantly under control…”

Engage the mind in planning service: how to cook, what, when, how to get the things, and why. Prabhupada repeatedly asks us to mould our life so as to remain Krishna conscious twenty-four hours.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:20 (auto-transcript): “Engage our mind in planning our Christian consciousness. How to cook, what to cook, when to cook, what are the things, how to get the things, what is the purpose we are cooking, how we want it to be planning. The mind should engage in planning our Christian consciousness. So,…”

If the mind is busy thinking where to find fresh tomatoes for Krishna, Maya cannot disturb it. An idle mind is Maya's candidate. — “this is my candidate, come on, let me do something.”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:54 (auto-transcript): “If you are thinking, where will I get the nice fresh tomatoes for Krisha? Do you know Krisha Confessions next? Will Maya disturb you? If you are not thinking that, then Maya will say, this is my candidate, come on, let me do something. If you are thinking, I want to start my…”

Rushing late into the kitchen on a high flame is passion, and passion offered comes back as passionate prasadam. Start on time, cook on a gentle flame, and the pot will not burn. — “So what Krishna is going to give back?”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:44 (auto-transcript): “I want to cook. I'm late, and you jump in the kitchen. What is that? Passion. You are kind of passionate, so I want to demonstrate passion. What I want to cook is passion. Do you expect it to be goodness, even after offering? Do you offer goodness to Krishna? What do we…”
Krishna admits the restless mind is very hard to curb, but says it is possible by practice and detachment.

Like Arjuna, every sincere person says it is impossible, and it is. The only loophole is Krishna: because he comes in, it becomes possible. — “But because Krishna comes in, therefore it is possible.”

🎙 Maharaj at 37:03 (auto-transcript): “We, like Ajuna, may be inclined to say, It is impossible. I didn't say that. Every sincere person would say, Ah, Krishna, this is not possible. It is true, it is impossible. Therefore, Krishna said, That is the loophole. That is the loophole. That is the only loophole.…”

Practice means regulation, like a fan's regulator. Maharaj jokes that devotees' fans everywhere run only on five, and asks for goodness, even turning phones down during japa.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:04 (auto-transcript): “Like we have a fan, a fan has a regulator. So we have to fine-tune the senses, you have to fine-tune. This will regulate it. But do you know Hare Krishna devotees? Do you know Hare Krishna devotees? They don't have a regulator. If you look at the fan, the manufacturer put the…”

To give up smoking, do not go where it is done, do not sit with those who do it, and do not talk about it. That is regulation and detachment.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:35 (auto-transcript): “Regulating the senses means detachment, detachment, detachment. How do you understand that? For example, if you want to give up smoking, how do you do that? Don't go to where these activities are done. Don't have to say with people who do it and also don't talk about it.…”

Of the nine limbs of devotion, chanting with humility is emphasised, and Prabhupada adds hearing Krishna's pastimes as especially powerful for the mind: whatever we hear about for some time, we become attracted to.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:19 (auto-transcript): “Suitable practice for Gaudiya Vaisava needs an intense regiment of engagement within the framework of the nine themes of devotion which we are discussing. Of these nine devotional practices, the yoga dharma of chanting Christian holy names with humility is one that is to be…”

Advertisers win us the same way, making people buy what they do not need. Phone and car models change number and body while doing the same work, and we rush after them.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:25 (auto-transcript): “and winning us today many people today are buying something because they don't need why what's happening about this man this is good for you brahboo you don't you're not really happy Because you don't have it, the moment you have it, you will be on top of the world. Just try…”

Scientists, politicians and philosophers are dangerous because their endless theories leave no room to think of Krishna. Citing Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, Maharaj calls them dry, while those who hear and chant about Krishna are juicy.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:44 (auto-transcript): “It's still proper server scientists are dangerous. Politicians, dangerous. Philosophers, dangerous. Why? They don't give us a chance to think of Krishna. They bombarded with so many hush-hush things. Krishna is not God. Vishnu is the plain person of Godhead. Where do you get…”

Maharaj cites the Bhagavatam verse that devotion, direct experience of the Lord and detachment come together for one who takes shelter, as satisfaction, nourishment and relief from hunger come with each bite of a meal.

These three are the proof that one is Krishna conscious, so we should check ourselves. That needs a clear purpose; without it we just float. — “Floating is not Bhakti.”

🎙 Maharaj at 48:36 (auto-transcript): “This is practical. So we should measure where we are in our Christian consciousness. Don't just float. Floating is not Bhakti. We should exist. Check where we are in our Christian consciousness. Where are we in our Christian consciousness? We should check. We should look at…”

A full stomach loses interest in food, but the more we hear about Krishna the more we want to hear, like Rupa Gosvami wishing for more tongues and ears.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:06 (auto-transcript): “You understand? If we become Krishna Conscious, our taste to become Krishna Conscious, to increase. While if you have eaten food to your full satisfaction, do you have interest in it again? No. That is the difference. No, it doesn't make sense again. People are like, ah, no,…”

Renunciation gives something up while still hankering for it; detachment gives it up for something more enjoyable, Krishna. Each time the mind wanders, the devotee drags it back, and the wandering slowly stops.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:25 (auto-transcript): “Renunciation and detachment are different. Understand? Renunciation and detachment are different. They later indicate giving up something enjoyable while still remaining and hankering for it. But detachment indicates that one gives up something materially enjoyable for…”

Mind control is like curing a disease: hearing Krishna's pastimes is the treatment for the mad mind, and prasadam is the diet.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:42 (auto-transcript): “So the Prophet gives a fourth example with which he compares the control of the mind to curing a disease by treatment and diet. Healing of Krishna's passion is treatment for the mad mind, and eating food offered to Krishna is the diet. This treatment is the process of Krishna…”

Two questions after the class, following a devotee's comment that Krishna consciousness brings tolerance.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:41 (auto-transcript): “My person said, the scientists, the philosophers, they are very dangerous. Politicians? Yes, politicians. They are very dangerous because they don't allow us to think of Christians. They are bringing so many things to death. who are now helplessly following what they are…”

If we receive only what we merit, why call scientists, politicians and philosophers dangerous?

🎙 Question from the floor at 57:09 (auto-transcript): “who are now helplessly following what they are saying and what they are doing. So, Marad, my question is, is it their fault or our own fault? Please, Marad, I want you to respond to this in view of what you said in a couple of days ago. that things are usually given, negative…”

Everything comes as we merit, but leaders have a duty to bring people out of their plight towards Krishna consciousness; deliberately keeping people where they are makes them dangerous to themselves and others.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:19 (auto-transcript): “Because they are leaders. Their duty as a leader is to get us out of our predicament, our deplorable situation. That is their duty. One is a leader to help a leader become successful in life. Success in life means to become peace and conscious. But their duty is a deliberate…”

children.topic: A king must be a sage
children.note:
The Gita's ideal is the saintly king. A leader who is not a sadhu carries a share of his people's sins; Maharaj contrasts leaders flying private jets to a football tournament while roads, light and water are lacking. — “The leader must be a Sadhu to lead.”

🎙 Maharaj at 59:26 (auto-transcript): “A Christian told us about Gita, The Imam Raja is the only one who lives in the world. The Imam Raja is the only one who lives in the world. Raja Rishi. children.topic: Q2 · Does the struggle ever end?
children.note:
Must we keep checking the wandering mind forever?

🎙 Question from the floor at 62:54 (auto-transcript): “You were mentioning about controlling the mind, and then you were saying that it is something that you do consciously, that every day we should always be, not just every day, every time we should always be checking, okay, when, you know, it will always want to deviate, and…”

Nothing material is eternal. We practise to undo our conditioning, and it decreases as we go; in the association of sadhus, hearing and chanting naturally happen and anarthas go away. Only those who neglect the process, offend or disturb others stagnate.
